# Treatise

But why by the influence of the **sevenfold number**? Do not the true **Alchemists** <note>original: "Chymici"</note>—those far removed from the status of pretenders—say that a thing must be prepared and opened by a **sevenfold soaking** <note>original: "septena imbibitione"</note> and a **sevenfold distillation**, so that light may shine out of the darkness? And the **Scriptures** say that no one is worthy to open the **seven seals** of the book except the **Lamb**, who is Wisdom itself. The **Kabbalists** <note>original: "Cabalistæ"</note> also recognize that the **seven beasts of the palace of virtue** must be opened before it is possible to reach His glorious vision. She [Wisdom] dwells in a dark and inaccessible cave, and in the center, as if in that **Daedalian Labyrinth** <note>A reference to the complex maze built by Daedalus in Greek mythology; here it signifies the complexity of nature and spirit.</note>. Thus, without the instruction of a most skilled master—the industry of an artist taught by a spirit sent from heaven—she cannot be led out of that prison into the sight of men. Yet we are exhorted to lead **light out of darkness**, for which a reward is promised to the one who labors and overcomes: namely, the **hidden manna**, or the **white stone** in which a name is written that no one understands except the one who wins it, or the **tree of life** situated in paradise, or that **morning star**, and so on.

I would also wish that the **monk** <note>Referring to Marin Mersenne, who was a member of the Order of Minims.</note> would collect his senses and consider what the **seven Churches**, the **seven angels**, and the **seven lampstands** with **seven candles** signify. What? Are they of no value or significance? But men far wiser than **Mersenne** <note>original: "Marino"</note> accept that primary angel as that **Wisdom** which is the **Alpha and Omega**. Insofar as the **sevenfold lampstand** in his right hand proves it, they seem to indicate by the seven candles within it the **seven planets**, and by those seven angels, those **seven Intelligences** <note>In celestial hierarchy, "Intelligences" are the angelic beings or spirits that govern the movements of the heavenly spheres.</note> which govern the said globes shining in heaven and dispose them to carry out the divine will. But what need is there for these things if they do not flow their virtues into the lower things, and that by the **sevenfold number**? Has infinite **nature** made anything in vain? But he will answer that the stars were ordained by God solely to give light to the earth. Truly, why did the Creator ordain such a great and immense multitude of stars which give little or almost no light during the night—as if the **sun** for the day and the **moon** for the night were not sufficient to govern those lower things?

But to come even closer: why was the power of raining down influences assigned to the stars of the **eighth heaven** (or the **firmament**) and not only to the **planets** (or wandering stars), since the planets are closer to the earth and the elements themselves? *Can you bind the sweet delights or the influences of the Pleiades?* Finally, perhaps he himself will reply that the words of the Holy Page are expressed concerning a true and real well of the earth and the waters common to an ordinary well, and from this he concludes that such parabolic words of the **Venetian** are to be held as trifles and Kabbalistic fictions. To this man, I say—and I have even learned from **Mersenne** himself—that the Scriptures have not only a **historical** but also a **mystical** meaning. For the historical text is sometimes nothing other than a type and figure of a divine mystery, just as a **sheath** is the image of a **sword**, or the **body** is the icon of the **soul**, or the **letter** is the semblance of the **spirit** (to use the words of St. Paul).

This is none other than the house of God and the gate of heaven.* Whereupon, rising, he took the **stone** and, setting it up as a monument, called it the **House of God**. For a clearly similar reason, the Venetian said, *The Father and the Son dwelt there together.* And where? At **Beersheba** <note>original: "Bersabah." # Concerning the Highest Good, etc.

...with overflowing divinity and wisdom—that is, with the Father and the Son dwelling at **Beersheba** <note>original: "Bersabah"</note> or the **well of the oath**—so that from this, readers may judge whether the Venetian is a "peddler of trifles" <note>original: "nugiuendulus"</note> of a Kabbalist, according to Mersenne’s opinion.

But indeed, with this single stone—like a javelin taken from the armory of the Kabbalists and placed in a well-aimed sling—I shall now attack this **Goliath**, the defender of the enemies of truth. I speak of this single Hebrew word <term>אבן</term> (**Aben**), which means **"stone."** It is the safest weapon of war against him, as it is most full of the power of wisdom. For in this single word <term>אבן</term>—in this Kabbalistic stone, I say—we have the **Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit**. This is not difficult to show even from its "bark" or letters <note>In Kabbalistic thought, the "bark" or "shell" refers to the literal surface of a word, while the "kernel" is its mystical meaning.</note>, since in the Hebrew language <term>אב</term> (**Ab**) denotes the **Father**, and <term>בן</term> (**Ben**) denotes the **Son**. And truly, where the Father and Son are present, the Holy Spirit cannot be absent.

<margin>Reuchlin, *On the Wonder-Working Word*.</margin>
By these things, according to the consensus of all Kabbalists, we observe that three persons are found in this single **Aben**—not only from an external view, but also in an internal and mystical respect, which consists and resides not in the letter or the bark, but in the true spirit and kernel.

But perhaps that **Monk** <note>Marin Mersenne.</note> will reply with words of this sort, saying:

> "What, I pray, is this stone of such great wonder? What is your **Aben**? Or from where does its power come, that it alone and nothing else is required for the consistency and sustenance of both the small and great worlds <note>The "small world" (microcosm) refers to man; the "great world" (macrocosm) refers to the universe.</note>? Have I not written a great volume—indeed, have I not commented on the very mystery of Genesis and set forth the most celebrated questions on that subject? Is it possible that a man of such great learning and reading as I am could err so remarkably? By the faith of God and men! How vain and of how little importance (as it seems to me) is that **Aben**, and how puny it is, since it is not at all subject to my mind, which is capable of grasping everything! Therefore, it is either nothing at all, or at least a thing so vile and ignoble that it cannot possibly appear to such an exalted intellect as mine."

I, however, confidently respond to such a vain and frivolous opinion of a boastful man: Although it is true that "the eagle does not catch flies" and "Jupiter has no time for small things" <note>Two Latin idioms suggesting that great men or gods do not bother with trivialities.</note>, nevertheless, by Mersenne’s leave, a **tiny sucking-fish** <note>original: "eheneis." The remora or "stay-ship," a small fish believed in antiquity to be able to stop large ships by attaching to their hulls.</note> is known to stop huge ships.

By the same reasoning, it is not to be doubted that our **Aben** here, since it can do all things, is able to perform greater feats than the giant imagination of Mersenne (relying on the wings of inept self-love) can imagine. Regarding this, the words of the **Apostle** intend the following:

<margin>1 Corinthians 3.</margin>
> *The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain.*

And elsewhere:

<margin>1 Corinthians 1.</margin>
> *God has chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God has chosen the weak things of the world to confound the mighty; and the base things of the world, and things which are despised, has God chosen, and things which are not, to bring to nothing things that are, etc.*

By this speech, the Apostle seems to suggest that those things which seem foolish, weak, ignoble, contemptible, tiny, and indeed non-existent to worldly people, are to God Himself more essential and powerful. He seems to confirm this elsewhere with the thread of a similar discourse:

<margin>1 Corinthians 3.</margin>
> *The wisdom of this world is foolishness with God.*

And Saint **James** understands this kind of wisdom, saying in a passage often repeated:

<margin>James 3.</margin>
> *The wisdom that contradicts the truth does not descend from above from the Father of Lights, but is earthly, sensual, and devilish.*

<margin>1 Corinthians 1.</margin>
But truly, the **Wisdom of God** is that which the saints speak of in a mystery, which is hidden and revealed only to the elect, as St. **Paul** testifies. Therefore, it is no wonder if Mersenne is deceived in his own wisdom, and consequently believes those things to be foolish, weak, contemptible, and non-existent which in truth **are**, and besides them there is nothing, while all other things are false shadows that are seen but do not exist.

### Treatise

We shall therefore hasten at a steady pace toward our *Aben* <note>original: "Aben"; Hebrew for "stone," which Fludd interprets as a combination of *Ab* (Father) and *Ben* (Son)</note>, the unique house of wisdom. By this means, we may more clearly prove that this Stone is the foundation not only of the Macrocosm <term>Macrocosm: The "Great World" or the entire universe</term> and every one of its members, but also of the Microcosm <term>Microcosm: The "Little World," referring to the human being as a reflection of the universe</term> itself. From this, we will show that any person in general can be truly and rightfully called both *Cephas* <note>original: "Cephas"; Aramaic for "rock," the name given to St. Peter</note> and *Aben*, just as St. Peter himself was specifically named. First, we shall approach the *Aben*, or the fundamental Stone of the Macrocosm.

The Patriarch Jacob says: *How terrible is this place! This is none other than the house of God and the gate of heaven.* And rising, he took the stone he had placed under his head and set it up as a pillar, pouring oil on top of it, and said: *This stone which I have set up shall be called the House of God.* <note>Genesis 28:17-22</note> If it is the house of God, then God is in that place or in that earthly substance.

It was for this reason that the Patriarch, while sleeping upon this stone, conceived divine and wonderful things through the power of that spiritual rock. This spiritual rock related to the physical stone as the soul relates to the body. Indeed, that spiritual rock was Christ, and Christ is Eternal Wisdom, in which—as the sacred page testifies—there are many mansions. All of these are undoubtedly distinguished according to various degrees of blessedness and happiness. Furthermore, happiness follows from knowledge or understanding, for the greater and more numerous the things we know, the closer we approach to God.

From these things it is right to conclude that since happiness itself follows knowledge, all true knowledge must come from God, or from the House of Wisdom, whose role alone (as has been said) is to teach all things. This, then, was the origin of Jacob's happiness and knowledge; this was the source of his blessed fellowship with Jehovah.

But someone might object: "Wisdom, or Christ, is said to fill all things and to be present everywhere; therefore, if a stone is his house, then everything that exists is a stone." To this we reply that the spiritual Stone is "Catholic" <note>original: "Catholicum"; here used in its literal sense of "universal" or "all-encompassing"</note> and, according to its own pleasure, it puts on an earthly garment. Therefore, both the heavens and this earth overflow with the gifts of that divine light; for the heavens are his seat, while the earth is his footstool, and as the Wise Man testifies, *Wisdom fills the whole world.* <note>Wisdom of Solomon 1:7</note>

Nor is it at all inappropriate for it to be called the spiritual rock, the universal stone, and the cornerstone, insofar as this light alone is the essence and basis—the foundation—of every thing, whether celestial or terrestrial, upon which it is established in the entire world. For in celestial things, such as the Sun (that most beautiful of creatures), this is the cornerstone. By its mediation, the Sun is established in its sphere, and is observed to hasten from the east to the west, and to look out from its center toward every part of the world's circumference.

<margin>
Psalm 19.
Ecclesiasticus 24.
2 Esdras 16. <note>Original: "4 Esd. 16"</note>
</margin>
For it is said of this spiritual stone—this Christ who fills all things with this wisdom, or the splendor of eternal divine brightness—that he *placed his tabernacle in the sun* <note>Psalm 19:4</note>, and elsewhere he is called the *Sun of the Lord’s full glory.* Similarly, regarding the stars in general, it is written *that they were founded in the word of the Lord.* It is as if he had said that their fundamental stone, through which they exist and are sustained, is the Word, which was the super-essential light of the world, or Holy Wisdom, without whose support nothing can exist or be sustained.

<margin>
Job 26.
</margin>
Furthermore, the earth also has its own spiritual stone: namely, the Divine Word, by whose assistance it is suspended over the void and nothingness, and is adorned with its many-sided properties. # On the Highest Good, etc.

...subsist and are established; wherefore it was not said without consideration by <margin>Wisdom 12</margin> the Wise Man, that the "incorruptible spirit of God is in every thing," <note>Wisdom of Solomon 12:1: "For thy incorruptible Spirit is in all things."</note> inasmuch as in it is the life <margin>Job 28. Furthermore, by this cornerstone God adjusts the "weight of the air, and weighs the waters in measure, and makes a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder"; finally, the works of God are wonderful, because he has made all things in Wisdom.

From these things it is evidently clear what this Macrocosmic <term>Macrocosmic: Relating to the "Great World" or the entire universe</term> *Aben* <note>original: "Aben"; Fludd interprets this Hebrew word for "stone" as a mystical union of *Ab* (Father) and *Ben* (Son).</note> is, both external and internal, and that its fiery or central spirit is the Catholic <term>Catholic: In this context, it means "universal" or "all-pervading" rather than referring to the Roman Catholic Church.</term> and universal stone or rock. By its presence, as if by a cornerstone, every created thing is sustained and established. Indeed, it dwells in one thing more than in another, according to the doctrine of all the theophants <term>theophants: Those who reveal or manifest the divine; here referring to divinely inspired teachers.</term>; for this God-like spirit, strengthening all things and consequently being the basis and cornerstone of all things, dwelling in the body as if in its own house, also gives to its tabernacle the name of the "corporeal stone," as it were a spiritual stone made animate. For just as the heaven is something spiritual, so the vessel suited to receive and contain it is the earth itself, from which every rock is hardened; indeed, it even behaves according to a stony nature.

At this point, Mersenne <note>Marin Mersenne (1588–1648), a French monk and scholar who was Fludd’s primary intellectual opponent, criticizing Fludd’s "occult" blending of religion and science.</note> either laughs, or is struck dumb, or clearly, if he considers the matter rightly, is rather astonished—and this for the sole reason that he is ignorant of that *Aben* of the Patriarch, that strongest arrow of mine drawn from the quiver of the Cabalists <term>Cabalists: Practitioners of Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism that Fludd integrated into his Christian philosophy.</term>.

I will, however, say no less boldly than confidently, that the matter of that mystical rock described by Moses is the purest earth, made spiritual, and reduced from all dross and heterogeneity, by divine help, into a divine substance. Was not the body of Christ reduced from an earthly and mortal state into a heavenly and immortal body by the power and assistance of the strongest and holiest spirit of wisdom? From a state (I say) of the corporeal, common to humans, to a spiritual and divine state proper to God?

Hence, most correctly, the Apostle says: *All ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the Rock was Christ.* <note>1 Corinthians 10:3–4</note> Therefore, no absurdity can arise from this when I say that the body of Christ, or the temple of the incarnate Word, was made from the uncreated earth itself, according to that saying of Job: *Man dwells in a house of clay or mud, etc.* <note>Job 4:19</note> But concerning this microcosmic stone, more will be said in the conclusion of this second part.

It will therefore be no more absurd to affirm this than that the stone of Jacob, called *Aben*, was first of earth and coarse substance, which was not impossible to be reduced later from its earthly and coarse nature into a spiritual essence, by the assisting and working Word, or the cornerstone, or the wisdom dwelling in it—inasmuch as it is its house, no differently than human members are a temple. Wherefore the prophet returns to this sentiment: *If the earth be opened, it will bring forth a Savior.* <note>Isaiah 45:8</note> I conclude, therefore, that this *Aben* or stone of the Patriarch was the house of that spiritual rock, which became the head of the corner—that supreme, <margin>Acts 4.</margin> cornerstone (I say), tested, chosen, and precious, which is placed in Zion, the true foundation upon which the Prophets and Apostles built, but which to all those who are ignorant and build poorly is a stone of offense and a stumbling block; and this stone is Christ, who became the head of the corner. # Treatise

...which is the fullness in all things, the head of the church, and the prince of all dominions, and consequently, the stone of the Patriarch <note>Jacob, who anointed the stone at Bethel (Genesis 28).</note>, since it is the house of a spirit so Universal <term>Universal: Fludd uses the word "Catholici," meaning all-encompassing or worldwide, referring to the spirit's presence throughout creation.</term>, truly, and only to be held as the universal church.

<margin>Ephesians 2; Isaiah 25; 1 Corinthians 11; 2 Corinthians 13.</margin>
But indeed, so that we may arrive at the second part—namely, the Microcosmic <term>Microcosmic: Relating to the "Small World," or the human being as a reflection of the universe.</term> stone or rock—we say that just as the human body is called by Job "dust, earth, and a fabric made of clay" <note>Job 10:9-10</note>, which was composed and curdled into hardness like cheese, so too may the external man himself be called a stony temple of God, inasmuch as the Holy Spirit has claimed his seat within him from the beginning.

For the name Cephas <note>original: "κηφᾶς" (Kephas); an Aramaic word meaning "rock" or "stone."</note> does not belong to Simon [Peter] alone, as if "Peter" comes from "petra" (for Cephas also signifies a rock), but this name Cephas belongs to us and to every believer equally with Peter. This we shall attempt to prove with very few words and demonstrate clearly: and consequently, that the Macrocosmic *Aben* <note>original: "Aben"; Fludd's term for the mystical stone of the universe.</note> of the Patriarch and the Microcosmic Cephas (though they may differ in outward form or figure) agree with each other in essence and matter. Consequently, I have not erred in the least in this assertion of mine: namely, that the house of God is always one and the same. This, therefore, is the reason why both Rocks, namely the macrocosmic and the microcosmic, are joined together by a wonderful sympathy of union.

Hence it was that when the Patriarch, considering the nature of his stone, said, *Truly God is in this place, and I knew it not* <note>Genesis 28:16.</note>, so also the Holy Scriptures testify that the Word and Christ are within the animate rock <note>Man.</note>. Again, Jacob conceived divine and wonderful things upon his stone; in man, or Cephas (who is not only a true Microcosm, but also the image of the living God), much greater things are conceived and miraculously produced into effect, just as you have confirmed by the holy page. Wherefore we say that those who occupy themselves with the *Aben* or *Cephas* without knowing its internal nature act in vain.

Nor indeed do we think that Mersenne <note>Marin Mersenne (1588–1648), a French philosopher and mathematician who famously criticized Fludd's Hermetic and alchemical views.</note> would be so ready to go into judgment of others if he had rightly known himself; if this (I say) had been well perceived by him, he would not have plunged so hastily into the correction of the works of others, since his own works are observed to teem with errors on every side. For if he had rightly known himself, he would perceive that he himself, along with Peter and the rest of the believers, is most exactly called Cephas, or a stone.

And although this will appear harsh to him and to some others at first glance—namely, that he should be called Cephas along with Peter—yet if they look into the matter with a slightly more accurate gaze, they will perceive that the matter is indeed most clear. First, therefore, whoever would deny this would declare himself a rebel against Holy Scripture.

For we are admonished by Saint Peter to approach like living stones that spiritual or living Rock of Moses, of which the Apostle says, *The Rock was Christ* <note>1 Corinthians 10:4.</note>. And the prophet says, *Look unto the rock, look unto the rock from which you were hewn* <note>Isaiah 51:1.</note>. That precept would be given in vain if 그 rock were not still with us, and we from it. And the Apostle says that *Christ is one body having many members*, and elsewhere he teaches that *as the head of Christ is God*, so in another place he says *Christ is the head of every man*. Wherefore (he says) elsewhere, *Christ, who speaks in me, is not weak in you, but is powerful in you.*

But the spiritual rock is Christ, filling all things; therefore we are members of the spiritual rock and, consequently, living stones hewn from that Universal Rock. Wherefore the name Cephas belongs not to Peter alone, but to every Christian man.

# Concerning the Highest Good, etc.

And if this monk of ours <note>Fludd refers to his intellectual rival, Marin Mersenne (1588–1648), a French Minim friar and mathematician.</note> should deny this, he would be committing an apostasy against the Holy Scriptures. On the other hand, if he himself were to establish this according to the laws of the Holy Bible, then we shall hold it as granted that Christ was not addressing Peter as a single individual in that specific thread of discourse, "upon this rock I will build my church" <note>original: "super hanc petram ædificabo ecclesiam"; Matthew 16:18.</note>, but rather He was addressing all Christians alike, according to that saying: "What I say to you, I say to all." But if Christ addressed everyone, then He also founded His church upon the rock of all Christians—whence it is called "Catholic" <term>Catholic: In this context, Fludd emphasizes the original meaning of "katholikos," meaning "universal" or "all-encompassing."</term>—and consequently not upon the individual Cephas <note>original: "Cephas"; an Aramaic term for Rock or Stone.</note> or the stone of Peter the Apostle. Thus it is clear that whichever way Mersenne turns, he falls into Scylla while wishing to avoid Charybdis <note>A classical idiom meaning to fall into one danger while trying to avoid another.</note>. And the only reason for this is that he centrally ignores this unique Stone of the Patriarch <note>original: "Ab-en"; Fludd combines the Hebrew words "Ab" (Father) and "Ben" (Son) to explain the word "Aben" (Stone).</note>, or Cephas. For if that is ignored, the aforementioned words of the Savior must necessarily remain hidden from the ignorant person: namely, "Upon this rock I will build my church."

But some will perhaps reply and say: "Those days existed once, but they are no longer; the things you have reported happened in the times of the Patriarchs, Prophets, and Apostles, whereas afterward we believe through faith and are governed according to the statutes and dictates of the Roman Church." They conclude that in this day and age, this kind of earth or this kind of *Aben*, or Stone, is by no means to be found.

To this I shall reply: such distrust in this matter seems to happen to such people because they have not understood this true *Aben* in the slightest.

For that ancient axiom of the church teaches us that such an earth and such a rock exist to this day: "Whatever God has taken up, He has never cast away."

But perhaps Mersenne might concede this, while meanwhile denying that it exists in such a way—as it did with Moses—that it can be touched and possessed by men. But he is deceived in this imagination of his and seems to "miss the mark by the whole sky" <note>original: "toto cælo aberrare"; a Latin idiom meaning to be completely wrong.</note>, since we find many places in the Holy Pages that contradict this opinion.

<margin>1 Corinthians 3:16.</margin>
For in the first place, the Apostle teaches us that all Christians are true Israelites; therefore, Moses and the Prophets address us of this age just as they did the children of Israel in ancient times, as is clear from the parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus, published for our use, where we read: *they have Moses and the Prophets, etc.* <note>Luke 16:29.</note>

Since, therefore, Moses and the prophets address us even to this day, let us hear what the prophet Isaiah says: *Attend, he says, and look back to the Rock from which you were hewn.* <note>Isaiah 51:1.</note> This command would be given in vain if that Rock were not still with us, and we were not made from it.

But we also have this confirmed by this permanent promise of the living God, made in many places of the Holy Bible in this sequence of words.

For first, Jehovah said: *I will place my tabernacle in the midst of you, and my soul shall not cast you away.* <note>Leviticus 26:11.</note> And elsewhere: *I will give my sanctification in the midst of them forever, and my tabernacle shall be in them, and I will be their God.* <note>Ezekiel 37:26-27.</note> And the same is described clearly, though briefly, by the Apostle: *You are the temple of God, just as God says: for I will dwell in them and be their God, and they shall be my people.* <note>2 Corinthians 6:16.</note> And elsewhere: *You are the temple of God, and the spirit of God dwells in you, etc.* <note>1 Corinthians 3:16.</note>

# Treatise

...so that we might call upon the Father in this way: *Thy kingdom come, on earth as it is in heaven, etc.* This means that just as your kingdom is in heaven—that is, in our spiritual part—so may it also come in our earthly and corporeal part. In this way, the soul may be united with the body by your holy bond <note>original: "glutine sancto"; literally "holy glue," a favorite term of Fludd’s for the mystical connection between spirit and matter.</note>, so that both together, joined in piety, may be able to perform and carry out the will of the Father who is in heaven—that is, in the internal or spiritual man. Therefore, those who do not know that Christ and the kingdom of God are within themselves actually repel their own petitions from the ears of God (being, as it were, treacherous and unbelieving) rather than being able to procure any access for them. 

First and foremost, we must believe that Christ, the spiritual and living rock, dwells within us. From that reasoning, we must conclude that we are all many members of the one Christ, according to the opinion of the Apostle; for we are "cut out from that rock" <note>A reference to Isaiah 51:1 or Daniel 2:45, implying believers share the same "substance" as the divine Stone.</note> according to the doctrine of the prophet. It is our duty to approach that living Rock as living stones, according to the teachings of St. Peter. We Christians of every sect ought to look back and pay attention to this, lest like the impious Jews we release Barabbas—that is, the "son of confusion" <note>The name Barabbas literally means "son of the father," but Fludd interprets it here as a symbol of chaos or worldly disorder.</note>—and send Christ back into the chains of a dark prison. This would be to submerge the light and the rays of our understanding into the darkness of ignorance, subjecting Him to a new kind of crucifixion.

<margin>1 John 1:1</margin>
Finally, St. John confesses that this rock is to be handled, seen, and indeed heard, in these words: *That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, and our hands have touched, concerning the Word of life, etc.* 

By these words, he does not mean Christ as a mortal man (insofar as He was not "from the beginning" in that form), but rather the Word, which was from the beginning. I speak of Christ who (as the Apostle witnesses) is said to *fill all things and be present everywhere*. He has been that spiritual rock from the origin of the world, from which the Israelites tasted in the desert, and which true Catholics <note>Fludd uses "real Catholics" to mean universal, spiritual believers, rather than members of the Roman Church.</note> taste in the sacrament.

Ultimately, it would be most difficult to deny that Christ is here the universal ("catholic") rock, clothed and enduring until the consummation of the world. 

But because this pertains more to the "sacrament" <term>sacrament: Used here in the sense of a hidden mystery or "arcana" not meant for the uninitiated.</term> than to public discourse, we shall blunt the edge of our pen and fold its wings, lest by flying too high it should vomit out something undigested to the profane common people.

->*From these premises (most Christian readers), conclusions of this sort arise:*<-

1. **T**hat all Christians can be called "living stones," whereby every single person is equally named "Cephas" <note>original: "Cephas"; the Aramaic name for Peter, meaning "Rock."</note> along with St. Peter.
2. Since all Christians are therefore stones—being members cut out from the Universal Rock—it follows that whoever establishes the foundation of the Church upon a single man, or an individual "Cephas" (whether it be Peter or a stone), is not to be called "Catholic," but "particular," and consequently a sectarian and by no means a student of the Catholic religion.
3. Just as the hidden Christ was concealed by Moses in his "rock" in the manner of a spiritual thing within a corporeal one, so Moses hid the rock in his writings; for this reason, he is said to have written "under a veil." Hence, the Apostle says: *The letter kills, but the spirit gives life.*
4. Just as the Apostle is observed to teach in two ways in the Holy Scriptures—namely, either by speculating or by acting and practicing—so these words, *The Rock was Christ*, must be considered by us both theoretically and practically.
5. That the Holy Scripture [points] us toward this very rock wrapped in flesh...

The Royal Prophet <note>King David, traditionally the author of the Psalms.</note> seems to speak of such ignorant men: *Who are you who dares to take my word in your mouth? etc.*

But to you (O Mersenne), I do not think it is necessary to pour out further words on this matter, since I have observed that you are occupied only with the Cabala of the "second order"—that is, the spurious kind—and not at all with the true matter.

For this reason, I would like you to pay attention to what Reuchlin <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a pioneering German humanist and scholar of Hebrew and Cabala.</note> says about that Cabala of yours, and even about such a sophisticated Cabalist as you are: *Sophists (he says) worthy of mockery, out of their own rashness or, if you prefer, negligence, falsely assert in their defense that a Cabalist is a diabolical man and a heretic, and from this they claim all Cabalists are heretics. Refrain from laughing (if you can), even though the absurdity is great; but I wish to stop laughing at these human monsters and portents, for the true Cabala is not to be sought through the crude touch of the senses, nor by the arguments of the unskillful logician's art.* Thus he spoke: as if he had said in a single word: no one is an enemy of knowledge except the ignorant. For he who is ignorant of this *Aben* of ours (however wealthy he may seem in the vain knowledge of the world), he truly knows nothing at all, especially because *Aben* is the One and the All, and all in all, from which we are taught everything, as the Holy Scriptures testify.

# BOOK THREE.
## In which
# THE ESSENCE AND PRAISES
### OF TRUE ALCHEMY ARE ASSERTED AGAINST THE
->SLANDERS OF MOMUS.<-
<note>original: "Momi Calumniis"; Momus was the Greek god of satire and mockery, personifying the unfair critic or fault-finder.</note>

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial S featuring elaborate scrolling vines, leaves, and a floral motif in the center.</image-desc>

I cannot be seized by enough wonder that such great madness has crept into men, that they long to involve themselves with an unheard-of vehemence in those arts in which they have never even sown the smallest seed, or whose genuine fundamentals they have hardly learned; but rather:

> What does the accursed hunger for gold
> not drive mortal hearts to do?
<note>A famous quote from Virgil’s *Aeneid* (3.56-57), frequently cited by Renaissance authors to condemn greed.</note>

The greater part of men, I say, is incited and driven more by the stings of avarice than by any devotion toward such a profound mystery of divinity. They do not consider that the Philosophers themselves, who were most excellently versed in this essential art, were so secret and cautious in their writings—to better hide the matter from fools and the profane rabble—that they were accustomed to write one thing while sincerely meaning another. They did this so that they might signal the art to those who know it (whom they called the "sons of art"), while the unworthy and boastful <term>Thrasos: A reference to Thraso, the "braggart soldier" character from Roman comedy, used here to describe arrogant and empty-headed pretenders.</term> of the world would by no means taste, along with the worthy, from their Heliconian fountain <note>A spring on Mount Helicon, sacred to the Muses; here, a metaphor for the source of divine wisdom.</note> flowing with living waters, nor be intoxicated by the divine nectar. And hence it was that they were "false" in their books, so that where they spoke more openly, there they more greatly concealed their art.

Why then, in all their works, have they exposed to an unworthy and indeed ungrateful world nothing but a few roses, both white and red, but interspersed and overshadowed by infinite thorns and thistles? They have filled their practical science with so many vain recipes, I say, that they seem to have served nothing but pure lies in place of the truth.

Yet, despite this, the truth is to be found under that fictitious bark or series of words, and is to be perceived by the wise with open eyes. From this, therefore, has arisen that bastard Chemistry with its spurious sons, who, gaping for gold and riches, lose themselves in the <term>Labyrinth: A common alchemical metaphor for the confusing and dangerous path of experimental work without proper theory or spiritual guidance.</term> of this divine science. In such works, they not only vainly consume their own labors, but also squander the fortunes and possessions of others; for they are accustomed to catch and tempt others with that same golden hook, so that they might revive their own lost fortunes or aid their current languishing state. This they strive for with all their might, inducing others through various oaths, vows, and certain promises. And just as they have fallen from avarice into poverty, so indeed this poverty of theirs—instead of transmuting base metal into perfect metal—transforms the practitioners themselves from good men into scoundrels and deceitful tricksters, rather than pious teachers. 

Others, having lost faith in Alchemy, are forced to acquire a life by begging, converting their experiments with <term>Antimonials: Medicines or alchemical preparations made from antimony.</term>, <term>mercurials: Preparations made from mercury.</term>, vitriols, sulfurs, <term>martials: Iron-based preparations (named for Mars, the planet/god associated with iron).</term>, and other things of this sort into medical use (their fortunes being lost). Others, miserably languishing and consuming their entire age and life in that sort of trivial and adulterated Alchemy, are at last abandoned by all their friends and are seen to waste away the remainder of their lives in hospitals.

Hence, therefore, have arisen so many outcries against this holy art, and so many defamations staining its chaste virginity, calling it most false—

<meta>This page continues Robert Fludd’s defense of alchemy. Following the previous page’s introduction to the "sons of art" and the greed of pretenders, Fludd here classifies the different types of alchemy and begins a direct rebuttal of the French priest Marin Mersenne, who had attacked alchemical philosophy.</meta>

...chanting a most false science, worse and more poisonous than a plague or a snake, when in reality it is not the art, but the artist who is primarily to blame. For the Art is most true, and there is none more excellent. But those **pseudo-artists**, by their own folly, deserve to be punished as if by well-merited lashes; for understanding neither nature nor nature’s intention, they nevertheless long to cast themselves headlong (like fools), setting aside all reason, into the deepest sea of the Philosophers.

Alchemy is therefore to be distinguished into its parts or members for the sake of a better method, no differently than we consider Magic and **Cabala**. <note>Cabala, or Kabbalah, refers here to the Christian Hermetic tradition of interpreting the cosmos through divine names and mystical mathematics, which Fludd integrated into his philosophy.</note>

<margin>Therefore we make two species of Alchemy, namely:</margin>

**ALCHEMY**

1. **True and Essential**, defined by:
    *   **One Substance**
    *   **A single and linear Method**
    *   **A twin Operation** occurring in:
        *   **Art**, through the *separation of the superfluous from the pure.*
        *   **Nature**, which disposes the matter through:
            *   *Adaptation* of the prepared thing.
            *   *Corruption* <note>In alchemical terms, "corruption" is the necessary breakdown or "death" of a substance before it can be reborn in a higher form.</note> of the matter.
            *   *Infusion* of a new form.

2. **False, Spurious, and Adulterated**, which acts in the "work" and is divided into:
    *   **Universal**, dealing with *Animals, Vegetables, and Minerals.*
    *   **Particular**, aiming at:
        *   **The Red** <note>The "Red" refers to the final stage of the Great Work (Rubedo), resulting in the Philosopher's Stone capable of transmuting metals into gold.</note> through mediums, cements, powders, or waters.
        *   **The White** <note>The "White" refers to the Albedo stage, resulting in a stone that transmutates metals into silver.</note> through the *whitening of copper*, the *fixation* of *Mercury, Tin, or Lead*, and through *minerals.*

As for **True Alchemy**, I affirm by the authority of all Chemical Philosophers that it is *a science ordered toward investigating and inquiring into latent forms, according to the truth of the matter and not mere outward appearance.* From this definition, those spurious Chemists are excluded who occupy themselves with vain <term>tinctures: In alchemy, a "tincture" is a potent substance or essence capable of transmuting or "coloring" a base metal into gold or silver, or curing diseases.</term>, whether for the red or the white, which can least of all endure the trial of fire. For there is but one single life-giving or specific tincture in the whole world, created from the origin of the world and imparted to creatures by divine goodness. By means of this, every thing in the entire world has both its name and its being. This is that virtue and truth centered in the heart of the creature, without which nothing in the world can live—nay, indeed, cannot exist for even a moment of time. Aside from this, nothing in the nature of things should be called "truth," but rather regarded as a false idol.

Therefore, I cannot wonder enough at the premature vehemence and violence of **Mersenne** <note>original: "Mersenni"; Marin Mersenne (1588–1648) was a French priest and mathematician who was a fierce critic of Fludd’s "occult" philosophy.</note> against the art of Chemistry and Chemists in general. He strives to refute, belittle, and utterly abolish the entire art on account of its worst branch—that which is futilely produced by the spurious invention of men. He fails to understand that a ray of the divine mind, and a finger or spark of **True Wisdom** itself—which is divine and not human—resides within the subject of this art. Even if it is obscured by the shadowy fictions, enigmas, and <term>griffins: Used here to describe complex, hybrid metaphors or riddles that are intentionally difficult to untangle.</term> of Wise men, this is done so that it might not be understood by the foolish and the unrefined as easily as by the truly learned and Wise. Indeed, had they not done so, there would be no distinction between a fool and a Wise man. But let us see what this Monk, led by his stubborn opinion, can object against this sacred art.

### From Column 653 of Mersenne.

> Take note, however, that Paracelsus used the aforementioned terms of resurrection and miraculous—so to speak—words, in order to hide the works and secrets of Alchemy: for it is a very frequent habit among men of this kind to use the same words in recounting their secrets to one another which we are accustomed to use for sacred things and divine mysteries, etc. Indeed, those Chemists deserve the most severe punishment who use, or rather abuse, the words of divine mysteries so that they might hide those alchemical tricks, or certain other secrets (though they are often not secrets at all, but accessible to everyone); they hide them, I say, at least in their own judgment. For to what good are those portentous words if they did not wish to reveal the secrets? Why write anything about it at all? Is it not so that they might gradually instill and persuade others that divine mysteries are ridiculous, fabulous, or at least to be understood only in an allegorical sense? Woe to those scoundrels! <note>original: "Væ nebulonibus istis"</note> I wish a millstone were hung around their necks and they were drowned in the deep Ocean, lest these sowers of such great impieties call back so many men from the ancient faith and holiness of the Church. For what, I ask, can be more impious than that all the words of the mystery of the Incarnation should serve to explain alchemical works, and that such great sacraments should be transferred to profane things?

---

### 2. From Column 1706 of Mersenne.

> That bold Pico della Mirandola <note>Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (1463–1494) was a famous Italian Renaissance philosopher known for his "900 Theses," which attempted to harmonize Christianity with Kabbalah and Hermeticism.</note> rashly blathers many things; whatever he chatters about obscurely, he either did not understand, or it was impious. This is still a familiar practice for many Alchemists of this century, who, lest we detect their ignorance, obscure their alchemical mysteries with fables and barbarian terms, or in some other way. By these means, they claim they can explain all the mysteries of the Catholic Religion far more easily, subtly, sublimely, and truly than the entire school of the Sorbonne <note>The prestigious theological faculty of the University of Paris.</note> or any theologians are able to explain them. Nor are they content to seek that "great and royal and heavenly work" of theirs, and the Elixir—which they propose as the alchemical yolk and fictitious nectar, the heavenly balsam, the solidity of the air, and its oil—unless they also lay their hands upon Theology itself, not to say upon God Himself. This is clear enough from Conrad, <note>Likely referring to Heinrich Khunrath (Conrad Khunrath), a physician and alchemist who blended laboratory work with Christian mysticism.</note> who adapts the Book of Wisdom to his own trifles; but they have their own *Cosmopolitan*, <note>A pseudonym for Michael Sendivogius, a famous 17th-century alchemist.</note> their "fountain of love," and other books. We shall laugh at all of them until they speak more clearly—which I believe they will never do, lest they reveal the fable to the whole world and show themselves to be the greatest of fools, etc.

### Robert’s Examination.

<margin>Column in v.</margin>
From these passages of Mersenne, it is possible to discern clearly what his affection is toward Alchemists and Alchemy. Indeed, it is very likely that in times past, this man devoted his effort to this *Alchemical* discipline with no better result than he did in the *Cabala*, <note>Fludd is referring to Mersenne's "Questions on Genesis," where Mersenne attacked Kabbalistic interpretations.</note> in which he confessed that he had "lost both his work and his oil" <note>original: "operam & oleum perdidisse" — a Latin idiom meaning to waste time and resources in a futile effort, like burning oil in a lamp to study all night for nothing.</note> and had consumed his time and late-night labors in vain. And the reason is apparent: namely, because he was occupied neither with the true subject nor the genuine method; rather, he gave his effort to a spurious *Cabala* and an adulterated *Alchemy*. Thus it happened that, instead of gold, he was <margin>Column 91.</margin> defiled by dark and filthy dregs. <meta>This page continues Robert Fludd’s vigorous defense of alchemy against the criticisms of Marin Mersenne. On the previous page, Mersenne’s harsh words—calling alchemists "scoundrels" and suggesting they be drowned with millstones—were quoted. # On the Highest Good, etc.

one may observe those processes of alchemy which he <note>Marin Mersenne</note> recounts: where he speaks thus: *God looks upon and mocks the errors of the chemists, while they busily burn, calcine <note>original: "calcinant" – the process of heating a substance to high temperatures to drive off volatile substances</note>, cement, dissolve, putrefy, ripen, digest, fix, sublimate <note>original: "sublimant" – the process of turning a solid into vapor and back to solid to purify it</note>, fulminate, circulate, filter, graduate, rectify, reverberate, project, coagulate, etc.* By these words, one can see that he knows no Alchemy except that which is bastard and adulterated, in which the pseudo-craftsmen occupy themselves. Indeed, he is not even well-versed in their own craft when he repeats the same things in his verbal catalog; for what else is true calcination but fixation? What is ripening but digestion? Again, what is digestion but graduation? What is sublimation but fixation? What is rectification but circulation, and so on? I know for a fact from true Chemists that these things are so. Why should I care for the notions of those fraudulent ones? However, that true Alchemists understand nothing by all these operations except a single operation and path—which they call the "linear path"—can be gathered from these words of the true Chemists. For Synesius <note>A 4th-century Neo-Platonist philosopher and Bishop of Ptolemais often cited in alchemical texts</note>, that Abbot and Greek Bishop, says: *Note that to dissolve, calcine, tint, whiten, rectify, bathe, wash, coagulate, soak, cook, fix, grind, dry, and distill are one and the same: and they signify nothing else than to cook nature until it is perfected.* And Morienus <note>A legendary 7th-century hermit and alchemist</note>, that good Hermit, says: *Our whole Mastery is nothing else than the extraction of water from the earth, and the returning of that same water upon the earth until it putrefies.*

From this it is evident that Mersenne, who never sowed any seed in the true field of Chemistry, delights in judging and condemning in his own rash way even true <margin>Text 2.</margin> Chemistry and true Chemists in place of the fraudulent ones. Pico della Mirandola <margin>Text 1.</margin>—a man a thousand times more learned than himself, and more profound in the true Catholic religion—he calls a "chatterbox" and "bold." He calls Paracelsus, along with the other Chemists, a "scoundrel" worthy of the most severe punishment. Indeed, the very name of a Chemist is so heavy and horrible to this <term>homunculus</term> <note>literally "little man," used here as a dismissive insult toward Mersenne</note> that he wishes for a millstone to be hung around the necks of such scoundrels and for them to be drowned in the deep Ocean. Oh, deep Ocean of charity of such a religious man! Oh, judgment of a Christian man, dressed in a monk's habit, the depth of whose solidity we shall soon test more profoundly.

In order, therefore, to more exactly bring the marrow of this monk's three aforementioned texts against Chemistry and Chemists in general to the test of the <term>Lydian stone</term> <note>the touchstone used to test the purity of gold and silver</note>, we have condensed their whole force and substance into these three problematic questions. It is my purpose to examine each of these in its order, so that you may judge whether he himself is a just judge in this matter, and whether or not he should be esteemed as a man of true learning such as he appears to be.

### Question I.

*By what reasoning the Wiser among the Chemists have hidden their mysteries or secrets, and whether—as Mersenne wishes—it is because they did not want to reveal their fable to the world, lest they show themselves to be the greatest of fools.*

### Question II.

*Whether it is so impious, profane, and worthy of such grave punishment among Chemists to refer their work to Theology; and whether it was done so absurdly and thoughtlessly by Paracelsus and certain other Chemists (according to Mersenne’s sense) to use the same words in their secrets which the priests of the Church are accustomed to use in sacred things and divine mysteries. Similarly, whether it is such an enormous crime in Conrad <note>likely referring to Conrad Khunrath</note> to refer the bare subject of his Chemistry to Divine Wisdom itself.*

### Question III.

*Whether it was given only to Adam to know the juice of the tree of life, which can perpetuate life, and whether it is given to men after the fall of Adam to know the perfect natures of plants, stones, and metals.*

### Question IV.

*Whether true Alchemy hands down no certain rules by which <term>potable gold</term> <note>original: "aurum potabile" – a medicinal elixir made from gold believed to have life-prolonging properties</note> might be made, by which youth may be restored.*

<meta>This page continues Robert Fludd’s defense of alchemy against the criticisms of the French scholar Marin Mersenne. ### Regarding the First Question.

Mersenne was of the opinion that Alchemists hide their secret <note>original: "arcanum"</note> for this reason: so that they might not eventually reveal themselves to be the greatest of fools by opening such a legendary and mythical thing to the world. But truly, why would so many Sages <note>the "Sapientes," or wise men of history</note> engage in such a trifling business (if it were indeed a fable or a fiction), since it is their primary duty to distinguish truth from fiction and to separate the pure from the impure? For this alone is the business of the true Chemist. How much "chemical purging" does this false chemist Mersenne require? For he, being ignorant of the central duty of the true Alchemist, judges him to hide a fable or fiction simply to avoid being held as a fool—when in truth the Alchemist is attempting to distinguish fiction from truth.

Indeed, Mersenne should rather understand himself to be conscious of his own folly in this matter, and should be esteemed a fool by everyone. For while he claims to know that the subject of Chemistry is a mere fiction, he nevertheless persists in it stubbornly and does not cease to trumpet its praises to the world every year. For what benefit, I ask, could it bring to Wise men—both Heathens and Christians—to celebrate Alchemy with such great honor if the art were fake and of no importance? Indeed, they would more justly claim the name of "fools" rather than "Sages," as this Mersenne <note>referred to here as "Marinus," a Latinization of Marin</note> seems to assert.

What, then, does Mersenne think of those Heathens held as Sages, not only by the followers of Christ but by the Pagans themselves? Namely: Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note>, Mary the Prophetess <note>an early alchemical authority often identified with Miriam, the sister of Moses</note>, Geber, Calid, Democritus, Avicenna, Pythagoras, Socrates, Plato, Parmenides, Zeno, Arisleus, Anaxagoras, and many other Philosophers most well-versed in the chemical art? Did they follow a fiction or a fable with such great sincerity, or did they hunt for folly rather than Wisdom?

Mersenne calls them fools and regards them as tellers of fables because they were practiced in Alchemy. And truly, if Alchemy were as vain as he drones on about, they would be manifest fools to engage in it with such devotion. But in truth, the chief goal of upright Philosophers is that **Highest Good** <note>original: "summum illud bonum," referring to the ultimate metaphysical or spiritual truth</note> toward which they direct all their desires with such seriousness and diligence.

But if that man should reply that all of these were Pagans, I answer that it would be a greater disgrace to us who (perhaps unjustly) assume the title of Christianity to be ignorant of that true mystery. By this mystery, we might more worthily deserve the name of Christian than those who, though not clothed in the Christian name, understood and possessed the secret of Wisdom.

And now I shall proceed to recount the names of Christian Chemists of no small name or esteem, so that I might enumerate them among the "fabulous fools" of Mersenne. Albert the Great (called "Great" because of the depth of his knowledge), Thomas Aquinas, Synesius, Pico della Mirandola, Roger Bacon (the monk), Ramon Llull (the monk), Arnold of Villanova, Abbot Cremer, Basil Valentine (the monk), George Ripley (the monk), Bernard Trevisan (the Count), Morienus the hermit, Richard the Englishman, Norton, and very many others were most highly practiced in the art of Alchemy, and they announced its praises to the world as if with the sound of a trumpet.

What? Are these men also fools? Were they occupied with fables and fiction? Tell me, by the immortal God, what is more unjust than for men to hate what they are ignorant of? And if the matter deserves hatred, what then is more futile, what is more abject, or what is a greater delirium and madness than to condemn it and hold as nothing a science of which they have caught no scent at all? These are men who have recognized neither nature, nor the majesty of nature, nor its properties. However much that man may croak and blather about his "profound knowledge" in nature, truth—just like true Chemistry—is to be known by its effects: for Truth herself shall enjoy the trophy that she has fixed within true Chemistry.

But someone will perhaps reply by saying: "If the Alchemists did not hide their art for the reason of such improbability offered by Mersenne, then give us a more certain reason for this matter." To him I respond to this question...

### Concerning the Supreme Good, etc.
**DD 3**
<meta>catchword: covers</meta>

The Wise Chemists themselves will promise this. For in the first place, Synesius says so most clearly:
<margin>Treatise on the Stone, chapter 1.</margin>
> The ancient Chemists wrote about the chemical science in various ways, hiding the principles of their art under infinite names; however, they by no means did this without the weightiest considerations. Although they spoke differently in their writings, they were in no way in disagreement with one another, but tending toward one and the same end and speaking of the same thing. They assigned strange and foreign names to the proper agent—names sometimes contrary to its nature and quality—and they spoke through similarities and figures. This was done so that their science would not be understood by the ignorant and unworthy; if that were to happen, it would necessarily perish entirely. For divine souls, after they have penetrated into the "well of Democritus" <note>A philosophical metaphor for searching for truth in the hidden depths of nature</note>—that is, once they know the truth of nature—they would undoubtedly perceive how much confusion there would be in the world, in every order, condition, and mastery, if it were given to anyone to forge gold in whatever quantity they wished. For this reason, they spoke in figures, types, and analogies, so that they might be understood only by the prudent, the holy, and those well-versed in Wisdom.

Thus says Synesius. And Morienus the Roman says:
<margin>On the Transformation of Metals.</margin>
> This mastery <term>magisterium</term> <note>The "Mastery" or Great Work of alchemy—the process of perfecting base matter</note> is covered and hidden, and wherever it may be, it is called by a thousand names. It is also sealed, and open to none but the Wise, for the Wise seek this mastery greatly, and having sought it, they find it, and having found it, they love and pray for it. But fools mock it, and among them, it is regarded as of the least value, or more truly, as nothing.

So says he. Look, Mersenne <note>referred to here as "Marinus," a Latinization of Marin</note>, you "good hermit," <note>A sarcastic jab at Mersenne’s status as a monk in the Order of Minims</note> how justly he hurls your own folly back at you! And Aristotle says that he who would communicate the Secrets of art and nature would be regarded as a breaker of the heavenly seal. And the whole crowd of Philosophers falls into this opinion:
<margin>In the Book of Secrets of the Rosary.</margin>
> that it is not lawful to reveal the secret of the art to anyone. For if it were done, he would be cursed, incur the indignation of the Lord, and die of apoplexy.

And Roger Bacon calls him insane who wished to publish this secret to the world except through riddles and enigmas. And Arbatel says:
> He who wishes to know secrets, let him know how to keep secrets secretly; let him reveal what is to be revealed, seal what is to be sealed, and give not what is holy to dogs, nor cast pearls before swine. Keep this law, and the eyes of your mind shall be opened to understand secrets.

So says he. By which he seems to argue two things: First, that Secrets are not to be broadcast to everyone, but only to the worthy; second, that for men who are ready to reveal and publish mystical secrets, the eyes of the mind will not easily be opened to perceive Secrets. This is also confirmed by that axiom of the natural Magicians <note>Practitioners of "Natural Magic," which in the Renaissance meant the study of the hidden forces and virtues within the physical world</note>, by which we are taught:
> That just as they pursue public and profane names with hatred, so on the contrary they love Secrets. Therefore it follows that every naturally magical experiment in truth flees the public and seeks to be hidden, inasmuch as it is usually strengthened by silence, but truly destroyed by disclosure, so that a complete effect hardly follows from it.

It is necessary, therefore, for the true operator in essential Chemistry, if he wishes to obtain any fruit from it, to be secretive, and to disclose to no one his work, his place, his time, his desire, nor his will—unless to a teacher or a co-worker. But why are more words needed? If these do not suffice for Mersenne, I shall proceed further in our proofs drawn from the Sacred Page: Our Savior warned his disciples to speak to the Jews in parables and enigmas, so that they, having ears, might not hear, and possessing eyes, might not see. <margin>1 Corinthians 2.</margin>
> Do not cast the bread of the sons of men to the dogs, nor pearls before swine.

And the Apostle says, we speak the Wisdom of God in a mystery, which is hidden, which God predestined before the ages for our glory.
<margin>2 Corinthians 2. 4.</margin>
> And elsewhere: No prince of this world knew the mystical Wisdom which God revealed to us through the Spirit.

And Paul acknowledged that he was caught up into Paradise, where he heard secret words which it is not lawful for a man to speak, etc. From this he argues that the secrets of God are not to be broadcast.
<margin>4 Esdras 14.</margin>

<margin>Proverbs 12:22.</margin>
By these things, therefore, he himself seems to assert that true mysteries are to be disclosed only for the use of the Wise; but the rest, which are not to be hidden, are to be broadcast equally to both the worthy and the unworthy. And Solomon says: that knowledge

### Treatise

...a prudent man conceals his knowledge, but the soul of fools proclaims its folly. Furthermore, we read that the Temple of Solomon was tripartite; for in its outer part—open to the air and the sky—access was granted to common men. Its middle region was assigned to the priests of the lower order. But the Holy of Holies, in which the <term>Urim and Thummim</term> <note>Sacred objects used by the ancient Israelite high priests to determine God's will</note> and the divine mysteries were reserved for Aaron alone, the High Priest, was dedicated and consequently denied to the common multitude, and indeed even to the lower priests. 

But perhaps Mersenne will reply: "All these things, taken from the sacred text, pertain to the secrets of mystical Wisdom, which I admit should by no means be revealed to men. But what does this have to do with those fictional and ridiculous secrets of Alchemy?" To this, we shall respond more than sufficiently in the resolution of the following question; but before we proceed to that resolution, I will show from these things already related how inconsistent and absurd this text of Marin Mersenne truly is.

> *For there is something (he says) that moves me vehemently—and I know not by what temperament, whether I should call it melancholic, or proud, or foolish and insane—that makes me most hostile toward those who, when they have known certain secrets pertaining to some art, are willing to reveal them by no means, but bury them with themselves, so that they do not benefit the Republic even in the slightest. Surely the Republic ought to cut them off like monsters and rotting limbs. For to what end did God provide you with the powers of intellect, so that you might investigate many great things daily with such skill, unless you were to communicate your findings to others and help the Republic in which you live, to the greater glory of God? By this means, the sciences and arts—which daily are obliterated and perish rather than being illuminated—might soon progress and be brought to their summit. Truly, I marvel at the Divine Power, that He does not strip such dwellers in darkness <note>original: "tenebriones"</note> of all knowledge, since He sees them using these arts so poorly, which He communicated to them; indeed, He reserves them for eternal fires unless they repent, etc.*

->To whom I reply:<-

Hold back your laughter, friends: for indeed, would not a child still nursing or babbling laugh at the thinness of such an assertion? It is as if he had said that all the mystical Philosophers—indeed, even Solomon himself, and Esdras, Paul, and even Christ the Savior—had greatly moved Mersenne, so much so that he knows not whether to call it melancholic, proud, foolish, or insane, but they make him most hostile because, knowing their highest secrets and mysteries, they were willing to reveal them by no means for the benefit of the Republic. For this reason, he says he marvels at the Divine Power, *that He does not strip such dwellers in darkness of all knowledge, since He sees them using these arts so poorly, which He communicated to them.* Wherefore, having made this inquiry of his, hear his judgment upon such "dwellers in darkness," which is as follows: *indeed, He has reserved them for eternal fires, etc.*

Furthermore, there is a matter in this Monk <note>Mersenne was a member of the Order of Minims</note> worthy of observation: how puffed up and boastful he is in his own opinion, and with what impudence he pursues men—not only mortals with contempt, derision, and his horrendous judgments—but he even insists on calling into question the counsels and works of the Most High God Himself, teaching Him, directing Him toward his own will, and moving Him from piety and mercy toward his own bloody and severe condition, in these words: *Truly, I marvel at the Divine Power, that He does not strip such dwellers in darkness of all knowledge, etc.* Then, since he cannot induce God to follow his will, he presumes to judge in the place of God Himself, saying: *Indeed, He has reserved them for eternal fires.* Is he not here a second Lucifer? 

Finally, it will not suffice for him to say that he has understood these things regarding the mysteries of the arts and sciences; for there is no true discipline except that which has arisen from the Spirit of holy discipline, since it is its role to teach all things. *I will send to you,* says the Savior, *my Paraclete <note>The Holy Spirit, from the Greek "parakletos" (Advocate/Comforter)</note>, who will teach you all things;* therefore, if he teaches all things, then there is no science without Him, who is the Teacher of teachers. But because I know he will reply that there is the greatest discrepancy between the subject of the Chemical mystery and that of Theosophy—since the latter is most true and the former a vain fiction—I shall therefore hasten to the resolution of the second doubt.

# Concerning the Highest Good, etc.

### Regarding the Second Question.

Whether it is so impious, profane, and worthy of such heavy punishment in Alchemists—according to the opinion of Marin Mersenne—to relate their Chemical work to Theology; and whether it was done so absurdly and unadvisedly by Paracelsus and several other Chemists (as that Mersenne says) to use the same words in their secrets which the priests of the Church are accustomed to use in sacred things and divine mysteries: similarly, whether it is such a great crime in Conrad <note>Likely referring to Heinrich Khunrath (1560–1605), a famous alchemist and author of the *Amphitheatrum Sapientiae Aeternae*</note> to refer the naked subject of his Chemistry to divine Wisdom itself.

In defending the Alchemists on this question, let us hold the negative view: namely, that it is neither impious nor profane for them to transfer their <term>formal agent</term> <note>In the philosophy of the time, the "formal agent" is the active force or principle that gives shape and life to matter</note> to Theological mysteries and to the words used in sacred scripture. This will perhaps seem harsh to Marin at first glance. But if he himself were to look upon and explore the matter with more accurate inspection and deeper knowledge, he would find no sin or crime against God or man in such an action as great as he imagines. For what will Marin say if the "formal agent" among Alchemists is the same as that divine Wisdom or that holy emanation found in the sacred Scriptures? If this is so—namely, if both Chemists and Theologians have a common subject, an active power in which both groups are engaged, though in different ways—it will be neither profane nor impious to use those words in both sciences. Nor indeed do we think that the true part of practical Theology (I do not mean moral theology, but the occult and mystical kind) is anything other than mystical and occult Chemistry; for it is by means of this that the divine light, hidden in darkness, can be brought forth into the light for our salvation. I speak of that mystical and hidden Wisdom <margin>1 Cor. 2</margin> which the Apostle <note>Saint Paul</note> understands in the place cited above, and which Solomon speaks of throughout his Proverbs and in the Book of Wisdom. I speak of the Word <margin>John 1</margin> which was from the beginning, which was in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it, according to the Evangelist. Nor indeed do I now mean some "subject" according to the sense of counterfeit Alchemists, but according to that of the Patriarchs, Prophets, and Apostles. I say "of the Prophets," for it was this kind of stone that Jacob first understood, which he called the "House of God." And the "Rock of Moses" is that stone without which there is no rest; for it is upon this stone that the Prophet says—as a true Alchemist—God "set my feet," denoting perpetual rest; for without the <term>cornerstone</term> <note>The "lapis angularis," a frequent alchemical metaphor for Christ as the foundation of the work</note> it happens that all men wander and never find rest. And the Prophet <margin>Psalms 118:22</margin> David recognizes that God is the only rock, whom he also calls the light, the salvation, and the strength of his <margin>Psalms 27:1</margin> life. And elsewhere he calls him his rock, his cliff, and his fortress; <margin>Psalms 71:3</margin> indeed, elsewhere he speaks more clearly of that rock: *The cornerstone which the builders rejected, this is the head of the corner; this is from Jehovah, and it is marvelous in our eyes.* <margin>Psalms 118:22</margin> And Daniel <margin>Daniel 2</margin> calls this stone the one "cut from the mountain without hands," which, after it had struck the statue, was changed into a great mountain filling the whole earth. Similarly, this was that "spiritual rock" which the Apostles embraced so often and with such great devotion, which the Wise Alchemists, filled with divinity, are most practiced in seeking and bringing forth from darkness into light. From this it follows that men of this sort are true practical Theologians, just as those who only teach with the living voice and produce nothing in action are to be called "theoretical" theologians. But the Apostles were engaged in both parts: for they both celebrated the praises of this rock to the world through preaching, and they applied its power in practice, by means of which they showed so many wonders to those of the world, cast out so many demons, raised up so many of the sick, and brought many other stupendous things to a happy end and conclusion. Christ also taught us this "practice"—He who was the true spiritual rock—when he says: *Be doers of the word.* And elsewhere, *work out your salvation,* and elsewhere, *knock, ask, seek.* But Marin will say that the Chemist understands one thing and the Theologian another; to which I respond that this is true, if he means the "adulterous" <note>Fake or fraudulent</note> Chemists, and not the true ones: For indeed true Alche-

->Tractatus<-

The initiates <note>original: *mistae*, referring here to those initiated into the alchemical mysteries</note> have signaled this very thing in explicit words. For just as **Solomon** confessed that he received **Wisdom**, or that **holy Spirit of discipline**, from God and from the holy heavens—and elsewhere acknowledges that it is a gift of God—so too the true Chemical Sages seem to confess the same. They affirm that although the Philosophers found the matter and the operation through their own genius and labor, it must nevertheless be said that they possessed both through God revealing or inspiring them. This is because God, who is the first cause, creator, and governor of all things, through His Wisdom and goodness, bestows various 
<margin>Concerning the Philosopher's Stone</margin>
graces upon different men according to the time and place, as He sees fit for those upon whom He lavishes them. These are the words of *Laurentius Ventura*. And elsewhere: *Upright Philosophers have deservedly received this gift of God, so that they might be self-sufficient and do good to others; wherefore King Khalid says: The secret of the glorious God is the greatest sister of Philosophy; it was inspired by God into His Prophets and certain chosen ones who believe in Him.* And **Hermes** says: *You have the knowledge of this art only from the inspiration of the one God.* And **Morienus the Roman** says: *The entire intention of any man seeking this divine science should be to consider it nothing other than a gift of the most high and great God, who shows it to His servants, whose name be forever blessed.* Likewise, **Geber** says: *Our art is reserved in the power of God, who bestows it on whom He wills and withdraws it.* And **Parmenides** says in the *Assembly of Philosophers* <note>The *Turba Philosophorum*, one of the oldest Latin alchemical texts</note>: *This is specifically that to which God grants power.* And **Balgus** says in the *Assembly*: *Its governance is greater than can be perceived by reason, unless it be given by divine inspiration; for this reason, all Philosophers say that it is a gift of God, because God bestows it upon the one who knows and perfects it and does not withdraw it; but from the one who knows and perfects it but does not receive it [spiritually], God bestows and then withdraws it, because it vanishes from his eyes when he ought to retain it.* From these quotes, it is explained clearly enough that even the Chemical Philosophers of the "Ethnic" <note>meaning "Pagan" or non-Christian</note> faction recognized that the subject of Chemistry is a gift of God and proceeds from divine inspiration. 

But now let us see how these things agree with the Holy Scripture. The Apostle says *that it is not of him who wills or runs, but of God showing 
<margin>Wisdom 9.</margin>
mercy.* And **Solomon** says: *Who shall know the counsel of God, unless God gives Wisdom and sends the Holy Spirit from the highest places?*

But **Marinus** <note>Marin Mersenne (1588–1648), Fludd's intellectual rival</note> will say: "This is the sending of the Spirit of God from on high to whomever He wills; what does this have to do with the chemical work, which is accustomed to treat some earthly thing or some metal?" To him I say: let Marinus first consider this: that this Holy Spirit does not have its seat in a single place in the world—namely, either in the empyrean, stellar, or elementary heaven—but fills every place. Hence the Wise Man says: *The holy Spirit of discipline fills the whole world.* And elsewhere: *Christ fills all things and is all in all*; but **Christ** is the Word, by whom all things were made, and without whom nothing exists, in whom is life, and that life is the light not only of man but of the entire world. Therefore, it must be understood that when he speaks of the sending of the Spirit from the holy heavens, he does not mean specifically the empyrean or stellar heaven, but from those heavens wherever they are turned. For wherever this Holy Spirit is present, there is heaven, since that is His seat. But this Spirit is in the earth, and that most abundantly; therefore, the earth also is most full of heaven, and thus we have heaven in the earth, and also the earth in the heavens. For how absurd it would be to say that the spirit of man, or the internal man, is the temple of the Holy Spirit if there were no heaven in man? Or could anyone be so insane as to think that **St. Paul** was snatched up into that worldly empyrean heaven either bodily or spiritually (for he himself confessed he did not know), or rather that he had a vision of the "third heaven" enclosed within the earth itself? Does not the Prophet also say: *Let the earth be opened and bring forth a Savior?* But he certainly does not say this is to be understood of common earth, but of "fleshly" earth. Yet I will demonstrate that just as <term>Cephas</term> <note>Aramaic for "Rock" or "Stone," the name given to St. Peter</note> or the "human stone" is the subtle human earth, which is called the <term>animal stone</term> by the Philosophers—which they extol far above the two other kinds of stones, namely the vegetable and the mineral—so indeed <term>Aben</term> <note>Hebrew for "Stone"</note> is the foundation of the earth, from which those three stones and all other things have their being and existence, as **Jehovah** clearly teaches us...
