# Fludd’s Response,

floods, and so on, have raged throughout nearly all of Europe for many years now, and even today they spread most cruelly; yet the peak of this evil has not yet been reached. Rather, greater and worse things are to be expected. Therefore, since no one can truly be called happy before his final day <note>original: "nemo ante vltimum diem suum beatus reuera dici possit"—a reference to the Greek sage Solon’s warning that fortune can change until the very end of life</note>, let the boastful Gassendi himself beware, lest that same prognosis, which he so greatly mocks and ridicules, should touch and distress him as well. For it is not within his power to resist the decree of the Most High, or to turn it aside at his whim. Thus, since matters are not yet ripe, let no fruit be gathered before its maturity. Nor can the arrival of the **Brothers of the Rose Cross** <note>The Rosicrucians, a mysterious secret society of sages Fludd famously defended</note> provide any restoration of these things; only God dwelling in the heavens can do so, who works all these things and has given signs of them both in the heavens and on the earth. Only the Wise, indeed, are able to observe and distinguish them. The **Brothers of the Rose Cross**, I say (formerly so called, whom we today call the "Wise," having dropped that former name as if it were a hateful veil of ignorance to wretched mortals, and now almost buried in human oblivion), can certainly bring about no such changes in Europe themselves. However, they are able to openly announce to Europeans that such evils will shortly be brought upon them by God, because they foresee these decrees of God from afar through "new stars" <note>likely a reference to the supernovae of 1572 and 1604</note> and other miraculous observations in nature—no differently than those three Magi, through the appearance of a new star, foresaw that the Spiritual King of the Jews had been born, and that wonderful deeds had to be performed by him in future ages and brought to a happy conclusion.

<margin>Daniel 2</margin>
And now the end of that final Monarchy <note>Refers to the "Four Monarchies" theory of history common in the 17th century</note> seems to be close at hand, so that, according to that royal dream in the Prophet Daniel, *that stone cut from the mountain without hands might strike the feet of clay mixed with iron of that great statue made of gold, silver, bronze, and iron, and crush them all together, so that they might be carried away by a whirlwind and never be found again; while that stone itself might finally turn into a huge mountain and fill the whole earth.* For that mixture of iron and clay cannot stand together for long. Therefore, this age seems to be the one in which, according to the Prophet’s interpretation, that Spiritual King—holding the scale of justice in his hand and examining all things with equity—will shatter, scatter, and consume all kingdoms (the golden, silver, bronze, and iron), and will establish and confirm his own kingdom which shall last forever. And I do not speak these things myself; it is the Prophet, led by the divine Spirit, who says them. From the aforesaid, therefore, I see that it was not my intention to indicate that the "new constellation" portends the appearance of the Brothers of the Rose Cross, but rather that modern wise men, just like those three Magi of old, are able to recognize the future truth from the stars and preach it to the world. Nor did I myself predict anything in that celestial chart of mine that has not partly come to pass in the world. Wherefore I would wish that Gassendi, before he makes further judgment on my conjecture, would look back at the outcome of that conjunction. 

For, according to my assertion, there have been: cruel wars; unheard-of slaughters; horrendous thunders; unusual conjunctions of the heavenly lights; the struggles of one religion or sect against another—Lutherans against Calvinists, Papists against both; and the new rise of the Arminian faction <note>A theological movement within Protestantism that caused significant political friction in the Netherlands and England</note>, which produced great disturbance in various provinces. Then there is the **Brotherhood of the Rose Cross**, which offered wonders to worldly men, but because of their perversity, granted little or nothing except to the worthy—judging it impious to throw the bread of the children of men to profane dogs. Hence they are mocked by the unworthy, blasphemed, and cursed, and are held to be entirely a "non-entity" in the nature of things and clearly nothing at all. I say nothing of the general famine and plague, the floods, etc. Just as these and other changes have been verified according to my prediction, so many other things can still happen before the end of the predicted conjunction. We must therefore wait for the end. For the end either utterly casts down, or raises up and "crowns the work."

Since I have now dealt—though under compulsion—with my two charts (one of which Gassendi, in his playful and witty manner, called into question) by proving their truth and utility from their effects, now the logic of order seems to demand that, just as Gassendi was a diligent "Inquisitor" into my affairs, I also should strictly investigate Gassendi’s own celestial observations and see what substance is hidden in them, or what wonderful utility can be drawn from them. But, as has already been said, it is not my intention now to pursue them all; I will only touch upon one or two in passing. In the first place, he presents an image of the last glowing appearance, which represented the form of a star with six rays; and there he simultaneously explains the name of the wind blowing at that time, etc. Another observation was composed of three bare rods, etc. Then he sets down observations of past eclipses of the Moon and Sun: the transit of the Moon near the "Spica" of the Virgin <note>Spica is the brightest star in the constellation Virgo</note>; the contact of the Moon and Venus; and other such things commonly happening in the sky. I confess that these observations are full of curiosity and even delightful to some, but to what end (I ask) are they useful? Or in what way do they contribute to the benefit of mortals? Should the more useful labors of others in celestial observation be mocked because of these? As if no one but Gassendi should be respected, and only his speculations should be accepted? But I restrain myself from saying more, nor will I say anything harsher against Gassendi because of his modesty in the preceding sections. It is this very modesty that stayed my pen—not any admirable depth in his philosophy, nor any unheard-of celestial observation, nor any stunning formula for refuting Aristotle, nor any tremendous strength in his exercises against the Fluddean philosophy. For modesty, even in adversaries, always holds command over me.

## Preface.

I would have you know (Benevolent Reader, elevated on the wings of knowledge) that just as three adversaries rise up against me in this single business, so each of them takes it upon himself to claim a particular duty or office in attacking my opinions. And among these, Gassendi, that giant antagonist of mine, seems to take upon himself the place and power of a sort of "Royal Prosecutor." For he himself, on behalf of the mass of accusations...

### To the Impieties, Member IV. Port. I. Part I. 31

In constructing this mass <note>Referring to the "structure of impieties" being built against him</note>, he delights in collecting from my works the pebbles or stones which he thinks most suitable, and lists them and lays them down before you, the Judge. His own words indicate this clearly enough:

<margin>Gassendi, page 272.</margin>
> I did not collect so many things as I touched upon a few, since my only aim was that, by revealing the mind of the adversary, I might level the path for you, by which you might march against him. Therefore, this remains your work: to fight most strenuously for Religion and for Nature.

->And on page 271:<-

> I only add, if anything from that conjecture should perhaps please you, it is my wish that you use it skillfully against Fludd.

Then La Noue <note>Franciscus Lanouius</note> occupies the Judge’s Tribunal. For he is most ready to judge rashly and to deliver an unjust sentence. This is expressly confirmed by that splendid title prefixed to his own Letter:

->To the Reverend Father Marin Mersenne (he says), the Judgment of François de La Noue concerning Robert Fludd.<-

The same is also very clearly evident from Mersenne’s Letter, where he says:

> I would say here what all the Doctors think of Fludd himself, but in the name of everyone it will suffice to subjoin, a little later, the judgment of the most learned La Noue.

Finally, Marin Mersenne, although he stands as the source and origin of this entire evil and contention, nevertheless usurps the place of nothing but some stupid Herald, content only to publish these things to the world and to trumpet them abroad under the form of "Six Impieties," which are proposed to the rash Judge La Noue by Gassendi, acting as a royal Prosecutor. And that bold and unjust Judge finally uses a hard enough mouth <note>original: "ore satis duro"—meaning he is brazen or shameless</note>; surely,

->Woe to that Judgment, in which someone is made the Judge and the pronouncer of the sentence in his own cause!<-

What, truly, is the reason why this structure of Impieties is fashioned by him into a hexagonal figure <note>A structure of six parts</note>? It is because he himself, near the end of my Treatise entitled *The Battle of Wisdom with Folly* <note>original: "Sophiæ cum Moria certamen," published in 1629</note>, was so convicted by me of those **Six things abominable before God**, and the seventh which His soul detests, that he cannot redeem himself forever. And mindful of this thing, he now attempts to return like for like. But he does so most maliciously. For it will soon appear that I can very easily extricate my reputation from those things with which he attempts to entangle it, and wash away most cleanly that stain which he strives to spatter upon my conscience. But he—how will he purge his own crimes, of which I demonstrated him to be guilty before your very eyes in that struggle? Indeed, I think it worth the effort to write those same words here again, just as they lie there:

<margin>Concerning *The Battle of Wisdom with Folly*. fol. 118. Proverbs 16 <note>The text cites Proverbs 16, but Fludd is actually quoting the famous "seven things God hates" from Proverbs 6:16-19.</note></margin>
I ask you (O learned Judges of this world) to take serious notice of those words brought forth by Solomon; and I entreat you to compare them, bit by bit, with the individual actions and conditions of Marin Mersenne, as enumerated in his volume along with Folly: so that from there, you may afterwards be able to render a just Censure of him in your contest. These are the words of the Wise Man:
> These six things Jehovah hates, and the seventh his soul detests: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood, a heart devising wicked imaginations, feet swift to run to evil, a false witness breathing out lies, and finally, one who sows contention among brothers.

<margin>Pride.</margin>
If, therefore, you bring Marin Mersenne to this touchstone <note>original: "Lapidem istum Lydium"—a Lydian stone used to test the purity of gold</note>, you will find him without a doubt depicted in his true living colors. For he, led by Pride and Self-love <note>original: "Philautia"</note>, thinks himself to be preferred above all in science and learning; so much so that he delights to call into question, examine, judge, and refute, and in his glorious manner condemn not only the most famous Philosophers, Mathematicians, those most skilled and famous in Astrology and other sciences, Physicians most expert in their art, Cabbalists and Rabbis most profound in hidden mysteries and raised far above his grasp, but even Kings themselves and Monarchs anointed by God. Whether, therefore, in this condition of his, he is abominable to God or not, I leave to you; it is not for me to judge a brother, but I pray from my heart to God, the Best and Greatest, that He may convert him for the better.

<margin>Deceitful Tongue.</margin>
Would that his tongue were also not deceitful, not to say lying, since it falsely imposes fictions and falsehoods not only upon me—calling me sometimes an Atheist, and sometimes a Heretic-Magician and a Heretic—but also various crimes and offenses upon others. Whence he has spoken unjustly of good men, according to the wicked will of his Master.

<margin>Bloodthirsty Nature.</margin>
> That his hands are also prone to shedding innocent blood is proven by that passage concerning me. "Whether," he says, "Fludd be a Magician or not, he should nevertheless be afflicted with no less a punishment than a Magician, as an example to others."

These are his words; let God judge him, and not I, who am indeed unworthy of the place of a Judge. Furthermore, concerning true Alchemists he says: "Woe to those scoundrels <note>original: "nebulonibus"</note>, would that a millstone were hung about their neck, and they were drowned in the depth of the Ocean." From which things his bloodthirsty disposition clearly reveals itself. Finally, he calls almost all most skilled men "insane," and this most severe Judge decides that they must be damned to flames, waves, wheels <note>The breaking wheel, a form of execution</note>, and unheard-of punishments.

<margin>Wicked Imaginations.</margin>
<margin>False witness.</margin>
<margin>Lies and concocted Contention among brothers. Col. 1151.</margin>
<margin>Contention among brothers.</margin>
Therefore, behold the man, pointed out as if by the finger of Solomon. His mind fashions wicked thoughts:
> for he not only maliciously inveighs against all learned men, but also has judged them wickedly in many places of his volumes, led by a lying Spirit, by wickedly twisting the meaning they intended. That he is also a false witness is clear from the fact that he has falsely heaped the crime of Atheism and heresy upon very many who are in truth servants of the living God, more sincere and faithful than Mersenne is, or can be, unless he changes his ways. Furthermore, he does not hesitate falsely and injuriously to accuse the Abbot Trithemius, Ficino, Bacon, Agrippa, and myself with many others as evil magicians <note>original: "Cacomagos"</note> in many parts of his work; nay indeed, to proclaim it to the world. And what is greater, he seems to spare neither Thomas Aquinas nor Albertus Magnus. Finally, he sows contentions among brothers, insofar as he attempts with all diligence to render men distinguished for their knowledge—both from the Roman Religion and from other sects of the Christian Religion—abominable to their brothers, as is lucidly explained in the Catalog of Authors prefixed to this Treatise. We ask you (just Readers), upon more mature consideration of these things, to discern whether this man, in his qualities, is lovable or abominable to God. I would not dare to judge; much less do I desire to condemn anyone; but I humbly commend myself together with him, first to our God, and then to your most merciful Censure: praying God that He may preserve you safe and unharmed from the worst lips of the malevolent and from viperous tongues.

Since, therefore, at the end of that Treatise of mine, I demonstrated in Mersenne those six vices which Jehovah hates, and the seventh which His soul detests, he has for that reason [invented] certain Impieties, six in number, in the very...

# Fludd's Response,

at the very beginning of his dedicatory Epistle, he busies himself with depicting these [accusations] and falsely attributing them to Fludd, so that they might be rendered more conspicuous to the readers. But the end, finally, will crown the work <note>original: "exitus demum coronabit opus"</note>. For through a strict examination, the truth will at last shine forth.

Now, he has yearned to express those six fabricated and imaginary impieties, which he has devised against Fludd, in this series of words, and to trumpet them forth publicly.

->*From the Letter of Mersenne.*<-

Behold, Fludd is convicted of holding the opinion and teaching, among other things:

*First*, that the whole of Holy Scripture refers to Alchemy, and to Alchemical principles. That the mystical sense of Scripture is none other than that which is explained through Alchemy and the Philosopher's Stone. That it does not matter to what Religion you belong—Roman, Lutheran, or any other. That man alone is "Catholic" <note>Mersenne is punning on "Catholic" meaning "Universal"</note> who believes in the Catholic Stone—that is, the Philosopher's Stone—by whose power men may cast out Demons, speak in new tongues, etc.

*Second*, that since God is a certain Light diffused through the whole world, He nevertheless does not enter into any thing unless He has first put on, as if a garment, a certain Ethereal Spirit, such as is extracted by the works of Alchemy and is called the Fifth Essence <note>The "Quinta essentia" or Quintessence</note>. That God, therefore, creates a composition with this Ethereal Spirit. That He resides with it especially in the sun, from whence it is vibrated for the generation and vivification of all things. That God is, in this way, the "form" of all things, and thus performs all actions, so that secondary causes do nothing by themselves.

*Third*, that the composite made of God and this Ethereal Spirit is the World Soul <note>original: "Anima Mundi"</note>. That the purest part of this Soul is the Angelic nature and the Empyrean heaven, which is understood to be mixed into all things. That Demons are also particles of the same essence, but bound to malignant matter. That this same Soul is the Angel Michael, or Metatron.

*Fourth*, what is more, that this same World Soul is the true Messiah, the Savior, Christ, the Corner Stone, and the Universal Rock upon which the Church and all salvation are founded. Namely, that this is the chief part of the Philosopher's Stone, which, since it turns red when thickened, is thereafter called the blood of Christ, by which we are cleansed and redeemed. For we are not cleansed by the human blood of Christ, but by this divine and mystical blood.

*Fifth*, that a just man is an Alchemist who, having found the Philosopher's Stone, becomes immortal by its use. He is said to die, however, when he casts off his corruptible parts; to Rise again when he becomes incorruptible; and to be glorified when he thereafter attains those same endowments which are attributed to glorified bodies. That the men who have escaped to this state, called the Brothers of the Rosy Cross <note>original: "Fratres Crucis Roseae"</note>, know all things, can do all things, and do not think it a robbery that they are equal to God, since the same mind is in them as was in Christ Jesus.

*Sixth*, that Creation is not the production of a thing from nothing, as we commonly understand "nothing." That Matter (which he very often calls "Darkness") is that which is properly called "nothing"; and therefore, when God is said to create or make something from nothing, it is understood as creating or making from Matter. That Moses, when he described the Creation of the World, was an Alchemist, and likewise David, Solomon, Jacob, Job, and all the others, so much so that even the true Cabbalists are nothing other than Alchemists; as are the Magi, Wise Men, Philosophers, Priests, and others.

These, I say, are those Impieties which this good little friar <note>original: "fraterculus" - a derogatory reference to Mersenne, who was a member of the Minim order</note> has devised and fashioned against me in his usual false and malicious manner. But so that I may more easily demolish and utterly overturn this lying structure of his, I will first cite the heap of stones gathered from my own works, from which Mersenne attempts to build this hexagonal Tower of Babylon; and afterwards, I will scatter it and turn it plainly into nothingness or smoke. Then, I will confute each individual member of every impiety in a few words; and finally, in the last place, I will confess before God and men what my Alchemy is, and of what sort? Truly, it is a true, sincere alchemy, differing and separated as much as possible from that worldly kind; so that at last, that mystical subject of the whole of Holy Scripture may appear.

<margin>
Therefore, this member contains two portions, and of these:
</margin>

> The first has six parts, of which:
>> 1. *The First* will penetrate to the deep marrow of the first deceptive Impiety.
>> 2. *The Second* will investigate the truth or falsehood of the following Impiety.
>> 3. *The Third* will open to the world the mystery of the third Impiety, and will prove it to be an engine not of justice, but of Impiety.
>> 4. *The Fourth* will deal with the fiction of the fourth Impiety.
>> 5. *The Fifth* will examine the laws of the fifth Impiety, and will debate whether they be pious or not.
>> 6. *The Sixth* finally, will pierce the center of the sixth Impiety, and will expose the evil deceit of its builder, as well as his ignorance.
> 
> The second portion explains that divine and mystical Alchemy, as the Author understands it, by which God, by means of His word, works in the { Macrocosm & Microcosm. }

# Regarding the Impieties, Member IV, Portion I, Part I.

This impiety is, according to that saying of the Poet: *bees of various colors* <note>original: "variisq; coloribus apes"</note>, a certain extravagant thing, and poorly consistent with itself (just like its inventor); that is, it is fashioned from parts that cohere badly and are heterogeneous by nature. For what business do we have with a single impiety made of so many monstrous members? Certainly, it is a formless monster, and therefore a monstrous and prodigious form suits it. Otherwise, in its very center, it would not treat the universality of Religion when it intends only to discuss the *Philosopher’s Stone* <term>Lapis Philosophorum: the legendary alchemical substance capable of turning base metals into gold or achieving physical and spiritual perfection</term>.

Therefore, this must be divided into two parts: in the first, the question will be handled whether Fludd correctly refers the whole of Scripture to *Alchemy* and *Alchemical* principles—since his [Gassendi’s] opinion is that Fludd’s mystical sense of Scripture is nothing other than that which is explained through *Alchemy and the Philosopher’s Stone*. In the second part, the question will be treated whether it matters to Fludd what Religion you belong to, whether *Roman, Lutheran*, or any other. Concerning these, God willing, I shall dispute in order.

## PART I, CHAPTER I.

->*Here, to discuss the first question, a mass of "Stones" <note>original: "Calculorum." Fludd is playing on the word "calculus," which means both a pebble used for counting and a logical argument</note> collected by Gassendi from Fludd’s works is described, from which Mersenne constructed the chief portion of that impious and Babylonian tower.*<-

IN the preceding pages, I compared *Pierre Gassendi* to a subtle royal prosecutor, who collected a heap of accusations, like stones, from my works and laid them out, opened them, and published them before that unjust and audacious judge, *François de La Noue*. *Mersenne*, however, that faint-hearted herald of ours, then proclaimed them as impiety. I wish, therefore, to bind all those stones of that deceptive mass into a single bundle, so that I may better survey each of them with the examination of truth, and at last, with God's help, be able to reduce them—as vain things and empty fictions—into smoke and plainly into nothing by the *Alchemy* of my own wit. In order, therefore, I will recite the "stones" or objections of this nature, and then afterwards I will respond to each of them effectively and (as I hope) with perfect precision.

->*Stone 1. Gassendi page 12.*<-

>Furthermore, since the principles of *Fluddean Philosophy* are merely *Alchemical*, etc.

->*Fludd.*<-

I responded to this above, in *Member 3, Part 2, and Text 7*, where I dissolved the rebellious and robust hardness of that "stone" with the sharpest vinegar of truth and turned it into nothing. But more will be said in what follows.

->*Stone 2. Gassendi page 14.*<-

>He [Fludd] replies to *Kepler* in this way: In the wheat itself, or its matter, I observed five elements, distinct in nature, substance, and quality; I extracted each one alternately, separated them from one another, purified them, and saw one have dominion over another in place and dignity, etc.

Upon this, *Gassendi* says:

>Which things I do not only commemorate, but I also desire to be noted diligently: for from this, as I believe, hangs the whole mystery of the *Fluddean Kabbalah* <term>Cabbalæ: Fludd’s Christianized version of Jewish mysticism, which he used to explain the structure of the universe</term>.

->*Fludd.*<-

Restrain your laughter, friendly Reader, while you see here the blind led so elegantly—indeed, so extravagantly—by the blind. Do you believe the key to *Fluddean Philosophy and Kabbalah* is so fragile, and that it hangs from a matter of such small importance, as *Gassendi* reports? Do you think the spirit of *Fludd* is so sterile and half-baked that he would think a *Universal* key <note>original: "clauem Catholicam"</note> springs from a specific thing? Certainly, by symbolic custom and method, we can indeed demonstrate universals through special and visible things; but to think that all things are from any one thing, or that the whole depends on some part, is most foolish. Therefore, the symbolic demonstration of the *Universal* <note>original: "Catholici"</note> through particulars is common, as much among *Philosophers* as chemists and *Kabbalists*; but that the universal depends on the particular, no one of sound mind will admit. Here, therefore, lies prostrate the entire strength of that sharp *Gassendian* investigation. For he has no other matter of greater importance or efficacy to detect and refute my principles than this conjecture: and even how erroneous this is, I believe no one fails to see. For did he truly open the mind of *Fludd* by nakedly asserting that the principles of his *Philosophy* are merely *Alchemical*, and that the whole mystery of his *Kabbalah* consists in a vulgar anatomization <term>anatomisatione: here meaning the chemical breakdown or analysis</term> of wheat or wine, or an examination by chemistry and fire? But more on these things below.

->*Stone 3. Gassendi pages 19 and 20.*<-

>In a second way, he usurps the name of "Creation" for an *Alchemical* operation, in the progress of which, from the thickest coverings—if he does not reveal the light entirely—at least he comes very close to it, namely to its genuine cloak and vehicle, etc.

->*Fludd.*<-

God gave me a better intellect than to impose the name of true creation itself upon some operation of vulgar chemistry, such as that fiery dissection of wheat. And in truth, he refutes himself with his own pen. For he writes:

>To him, all things are *Symbols*. And again: see how he accommodates the mystery of creation to this, etc.

And yet, a symbol of a thing is not the thing itself, nor is "accommodation" the "usurpation" of the thing itself; for just as the "similar" is not the "same," so symbols or images are not the same as the thing signified. For example: we can describe the form of a sword by its scabbard, and the glory of God is expressed through His creatures; but no prudent person will think that the scabbard itself is the sword, or the creature is God Himself. So Christ Himself was depicted parabolically through the exterior things of the Old Law, etc. Who, then, does not see that all of *Gassendi’s* words are mere smoke, and of their own accord vanish with the smoke into nothing?

->*Stone 4. Gassendi pages 95, 96, and 97.*<-

>It does not seem to me that those act consistently or religiously enough who, if they dream of anything in *Physics*, immediately seek patronage in the Scripture. As if the *Holy Spirit*, in dictating the *Sacred Books*, did not labor solely so that men might maintain innocence of character joined to divine worship, and might be made participants of both grace and glory, which are gifts above nature? As the elegant weaving of words [continues]...

# Fludd’s Response

...such sublime learning of natural things is neglected in Scripture: because since the salvation of all men is at stake, it ought to have been contained in both words and matters that would least exceed the grasp of even the most unrefined people. See how Christ the Lord always uses the most familiar parables—of the vineyard, the field, and the like? Concerning that *first matter* <term>materia prima: the formless primordial substance from which all things were created</term>, or the *fifth essence* <term>quinta essentia: "quintessence," the purest or most refined substance, often associated with the celestial bodies</term>, he is altogether silent. See how Moses the Lawgiver, etc.? The intention of Scripture is not to teach us exquisite physics. Its mind is that we should be taught whatever pertains to salvation, and once we have perceived that, it cares little whether all things agree perfectly with the standard of the Physicists. But to what end, you will ask, is all this? Surely, only to hint that I do not approve of Fludd when he boasts so greatly of his Physics being founded on the text of Scripture. And I do not deny, indeed, that Moses could have instructed us even in Physical matters; yet, that he actually willed to do this, no one will easily persuade me. He [Fludd] wants all things to be accommodated to chemical operations, but if such imagining were permitted, there would be no craftsman at all who could not, with equal right, derive his entire art from Genesis, etc.

<margin>Gassendi</margin>
<margin>Fludd</margin>
**Text.** They do not (he says) seem to me to act consistently enough, or religiously, who, if they dream up something in Physics, immediately seek patronage for it in Scripture.

If there is any truth in Philosophy, as there certainly is (otherwise the "love of wisdom" <note>original: "sapientiæ amor," the literal translation of the Greek "philosophia"</note> would be falsely named); and if all truth lies hidden in the sacred Scriptures, as is indeed the case, why, I ask, do they act irreligiously who, by examining a branch of truth, look back toward its trunk, and even to the root itself? For, since truth is unique and simple, and is chiefly contained in sacred things, what, I pray, stands in the way of even Physical truth being tested against this *Lydian stone* <term>Lapis Lydius: a touchstone used to test the purity of gold; here used metaphorically for the Bible as the ultimate standard of truth</term>, and proven by a sacred examination, so that it may appear whether it is truly truth or not? Most poorly, therefore, in my judgment—or at least quite ill-advisedly—do those act who place faith in a matter that is discordant with the Scriptures. Much more, indeed, are those to be disapproved (of whom Gassendi is one) who, while they themselves turn away from such an examination, also strive with all their might to discourage and lead others away. Thus, that "they do not seem" of Gassendi is dissolved by my "they do seem." For why should my "do" not have as much force as his "not"?

<margin>Gassendi</margin>
**Text.** As if the Holy Spirit, in dictating the sacred Books, did not focus solely on this: that men should maintain innocence of character joined to divine worship, and at the same time become partakers of grace and glory, which are gifts above nature? Thus, while the texture of the words is indeed elegant, sublime learning of natural things is neglected in Scripture.

<margin>Fludd</margin>
**I respond:** This assertion of Gassendi’s is most false. For the Holy Spirit, besides handing down those things which look toward morality alone—so that men might indeed maintain innocence of character joined to divine worship—also teaches the mysteries of God and His wonderful operations in His creatures, so that every rational creature may be able, through the speculation of natural things, to be raised to the contemplation of his supernatural Creator, and to know Him from His marvelous works. For how could one compose the character and the reasons of one's life according to the precepts of God his Creator? Or how would he worship Him, unless he first knew Him? The greater portion of the sacred Scriptures, therefore, is occupied with this object. For example:

<margin>Psalm 103</margin>
<margin>Job 28</margin>
> *The works of God are wonderful and vast, which He made in wisdom.* <note>Psalm 104:24 in modern numbering</note>
> *God in His wisdom assigns a weight to the air, and weighs the waters by measure; He makes statutes for the rain, and a path for the lightning of the thunder.*

<margin>Job 37</margin>
> *Hearken with your ears, stand still, and consider the wonders of the strong God. Do you know when God disposes them, when the light of His cloud shines? Do you know the balancings of the thick cloud, the wonders of God, perfect in knowledge? etc.*

<margin>Psalm 77</margin>
> *The waters saw thee, O God, and they were afraid: the clouds poured out waters, the upper clouds gave a sound, even your pebbles [hailstones] passed through: as your thunder sounded in that world, lightnings illuminated the habitable earth, and the comet, and the earth trembled, etc.*

<margin>Psalm 78</margin>
<margin>Job 28</margin>
> *He commanded the clouds above from on high, and opened the doors of heaven, raining down manna to eat.*
> *Who fashioned the sapphire clouds in wisdom? Who can tilt the jars of heaven?*

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 43:17</margin>
> *The treasuries were opened, and the clouds and mists flew out like birds.*

<margin>Psalm 104</margin>
<margin>Job 28</margin>
> *God covers the heavens with thick clouds, who prepares grass for the earth.*
> *Thick clouds are His pavilion, who walks upon the wings of the wind.*
> *Do you know where the way is by which the vapor is divided, by which He scatters the wind upon the earth?*

<margin>Psalm 135:7</margin>
> *He brings forth the wind out of His treasuries.*

<margin>Psalm 147</margin>
> *God gives snow like wool, and scatters the frost like ashes; He casts down ice like morsels; who can stand before His cold? He sends out His word and melts them; as soon as He blows His wind, they flow.*

<margin>Job 38:21</margin>
<margin>Job 37</margin>
> *Have you entered into the treasuries of the snow, or have you had a look at the treasuries of the hail?*
> *The strong God brings forth ice by His breath; by the blowing of God, the frost is thickened.*

Do you see, then, what a great cloud of sacred sayings is here, which speak of nothing but physics? Indeed, I could derive infinite other testimonies from the sacred fountain here—namely from Moses, Job, David, and the other Prophets; indeed, even from Christ himself, or his Evangelists and Apostles; but the preceding things more than enough reveal and confirm the absurdity of the Gassendian opinion. To what end, then, more? I pass over also those things which conclude that God is the internal actor and mover in natural things, and I add only this: if you except that immediate revelation which occurred for the Apostles and a few other holy men of God, it is impossible to reach a perfect and complete knowledge of God if the work of nature is ignored. It is, therefore, an argument of extreme ignorance and folly among mortals to affirm that the Holy Spirit, in His writings, did not intend to lead men, as if by the hand, to nature and physical things, and through the knowledge of these to the Creator Himself: since almost every demonstration of divinity, after the fall of Adam, is made among mortals *a posteriori* <term>a posteriori: reasoning from effects back to their causes (e.g., observing the creation to understand the Creator)</term>, that is, through the creatures; not indeed *a priori* <term>a priori: reasoning from cause to effect; in this context, direct knowledge of God's essence without needing to look at the physical world</term>, that is, immediately from the divine essence, which, as was said before, can today be rightly known and discerned in no ordinary way except in the creatures. All of which that wisest of mortals [Solomon] confirms with this style of words:

<margin>Wisdom 13</margin>
<margin>Romans 1</margin>
> *Vain are all men by nature, in whom there is ignorance of God, and who, from those good things which are seen, could not understand Him who is; nor by considering the works did they acknowledge the craftsman. For that which can be known of God is manifest in them. For God has made it manifest to them. For His invisible things, while they are understood from things that were made, are clearly seen from the creation of the world as eternal, namely His power as well as His divinity, so that men might be without excuse.*

By which sayings of the wise man and the Apostle, it is clearly indicated that the invisible things of God are revealed to us through the steps of knowledge of natural things and visible creatures, without the knowledge of which, an entrance to the absolute knowledge of God is impossi-

<meta>This page continues Robert Fludd’s vigorous defense of "Mosaic Philosophy"—the idea that the Bible contains a complete system of natural science—against the criticisms of the French priest and philosopher Pierre Gassendi. # Against the Impieties, Member IV, Portion I, Part I.

...we have said it is so, unless some immediate divine revelation intervened. Hence it was that Moses saw only the "back parts" of God; but his face, or his front parts, he was denied to see. <note>A reference to Exodus 33:23, where God allows Moses to see His back but not His face; Fludd uses this to illustrate the limits of human perception of the divine essence.</note> But why should such a great Philosopher and Theologian contradict these things just to blind the ignorant of the world? Does he not think that all that history of the weather and of animals, expressed everywhere in the Scriptures, is of no importance or use? As if the Holy Spirit, through the holy men of God, had dictated something to us in vain and fruitlessly? For if the whole purpose of the Holy Spirit (as he asserts) is directed only toward our mortality and the piety of life, how (I ask) will those discourses in the sacred Text concerning the weather lead to that intention? But truly, if he understands the scriptures to be opposed to common Philosophy—inasmuch as it derives its origin from the pagans—in that, because it is most true, I agree with him. <note>original: "vulgari Philosophiæ, vtpote q̄ ab ethnicis suam originē ducit." Fludd rejects Aristotelian physics because it is "pagan" or "ethnic," preferring a "Christian" physics derived from the Bible.</note> But are not Christian men therefore insane, especially those who exceed the common order and excel in the mysteries of Philosophical wisdom, if they prefer to be directed and governed by the fallacious rudiments of a vain Philosophy propagated by the pagan world, rather than by the doctrine of that true and holy one which is from Christ, in whom, according to the mind of St. Paul, all the fullness of the divinity dwells bodily? For so he says:

<margin>Colossians 2:8–9</margin>
> See that no one deceives you through Philosophy and empty fallacy, according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ: because in him dwells all the fullness of the divinity bodily, and you are filled in him, who is the head of all principality and power, etc.

Where the Apostle expressly inveighs against that pagan philosophy, invented and handed down by men, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ, who is the very truth itself, and in whom dwells all the fullness of the divinity. Nor is it a wonder. For since true Philosophy, whose essential subject is wisdom, is the "love of wisdom"; and wisdom itself, which is the fullness of divinity, is the Holy Spirit of discipline, whose job it is to teach all things (as Scripture testifies), why (I pray) should we not be taught both natural and moral philosophy by him rather than by another? Indeed, it cannot be denied that, as that Holy Spirit of discipline most absolutely delivers one part of philosophy which Gassendi intends—namely, that leading to mortality and civility, which is to say, toward divine worship and respect for one's neighbor—so it also includes the other, namely natural philosophy; and even indeed that <term>Magic: in Fludd's context, this is 'Natural Magic' or the study of God's hidden laws in nature, not sorcery.</term>, and mystic and divine Physics. Does it not teach the mysteries of the heavens, the stars, fire, air, water, earth, and the creatures produced from and in them? Let Gassendi therefore read, and read less drowsily, and re-read the sacred Books of the Holy Spirit, and he will see how advisedly and how considerately he denies that Physics is proposed therein. And specifically, let him look at the words of Solomon, solidly refuting his assertion, where he says:

<margin>Book of Wisdom 7</margin>
> The Holy Spirit of discipline gave me true knowledge of those things that are, that I may know the disposition of the world, and the virtues of the elements, the beginning and the end, and the middle of times, the changes of vicissitudes, the permutations and completions of times, the changes of manners, and the divisions of seasons, the courses of the year, and the dispositions of the stars, the natures of animals, and the rages of beasts, the force of winds and the thoughts of men, the differences of shrubs, and the virtues of roots, and whatever things are hidden and unforeseen I have learned, for wisdom, the artisan of all things, taught me.

From these things, therefore, it is evident how vain and false is that doctrine of Gassendi: that the Holy Spirit neglects the doctrine of natural things, and teaches only innocence of manners joined with divine worship. And it is truly a wonder that a learned man, and especially a professed Theologian, would wish to write such things and affirm that the Holy Spirit does not teach a chosen man of God Physics, Astronomy, Medicine, and all things, against those express words of Solomon: *for wisdom, the artisan of all things, taught me.* I conclude therefore against Gassendi, that it is impossible but that the Bible, the book of all books, contains the sublime learning of all erudition, even though in his "sublime" eyes the style of the Bible is humble and the matter contained therein is base.

<margin>Gassendi</margin>
**Text.** Since the salvation of all men is their concern, it [the Bible] ought to be contained in such words and matters as would not exceed the grasp of even the most unrefined, etc.

<margin>Fludd</margin>
Is not this "excellent" doctrine of that man, Philosopher and Theologian, entirely contrary to the intention of Christ and Solomon? For it was not because the salvation of all men is their concern that all things had to be brought together indiscriminately in the sacred writings in such words as to be understood by anyone, even the most unrefined; but it was enough that only those few things, on which the hinge of human salvation turns, were described precisely in the said manner. And this has been done most clearly and brilliantly in the Scriptures. But the rest, since they are of higher speculation and pertain to more solid erudition and instruction, are therefore treated more obscurely. Hence Solomon spoke to the common people in riddles and parables where he makes mention of the secrets of hidden Wisdom. Whence elsewhere it is "the part of the wise man to conceal a matter." And Christ ordered his disciples to speak to the common people in parables, lest they "throw pearls before swine," or "the bread of the children of men to the dogs." And elsewhere: <margin>Matthew 13</margin> *The mystery of the kingdom of heaven is given to you disciples: but to them it is not given.* And the Apostle says: <margin>Romans 16, 2 Corinthians 2</margin> *The mystery of Christ shall be silent for eternal times.* Finally, St. Paul: *We speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, which is hidden, which God predestined before the ages, for the glory of the elect and the Apostles;* he does not say "of the common people." I conclude therefore, against that assertion of Gassendi, that a wise man should not always nor everywhere use such words as do not exceed the grasp of even the most unrefined: considering that Esdras, from those books which he had written as the Holy Spirit dictated, reserved seventy (by the command of the Lord himself) for only the wise of his people, so that they alone might read them and understand those things which it was a sin to publish to the profane commoners. <note>Fludd is referencing 2 Esdras (or 4 Ezra) 14:45–46, a common text used by esotericists to argue for a hidden, oral, or secret tradition alongside the public Bible.</note> Moreover, if Gassendi's proposition is true, why does the Apostle Paul say he was caught up even to the third heaven and saw things not to be revealed to mortals? Why also does he say elsewhere, "we speak wisdom to the wise," etc.? Why say more? I wonder that Gassendi, although he is a professed Theologian of the Roman Church, did not hesitate to apostatize from his own Theology, just to oppose me. For all Roman Theologians teach that Holy Scripture is obscure and impossible to understand without an interpreter: and therefore they completely forbid the reading of the Scriptures to the "Laity" (as they call them), nor is anyone among them allowed to read the Bible unless he has received the "sacred thrice" (as it is said to them); <note>A jab at Catholic restrictions on lay Bible reading during the Counter-Reformation period.</note> yet Gassendi determines the opposite: that scripture is very easy to understand, so that it can be understood by anyone, even the most unrefined. Who, then, does not see his notable error on both sides? But to the rest.

<margin>Gassendi</margin>
**Text.** See how Christ the Lord always uses the most familiar parables—of the vineyard, the field, and the like? But concerning that <term>materia prima: the formless primordial substance from which all things were created</term>, or <term>quinta essentia: "quintessence," the purest or most refined substance, often associated with the celestial bodies</term>, he is altogether silent.

<margin>Fludd</margin>
And yet his parables are so familiar to men that I believe Gassendi can scarcely—hardly at all—unravel their mystic sense, even though he is esteemed as a great Theologian among some Christians. For not all that glitters is gold. As for that *first matter*, does he not everywhere make notable and excellent mention of the *water*, which is the principle of things? Does he not mention the *darkness* which is the privation of light? Does he not likewise mention the *luminous Word* which was the actor of all things? Did not Christ also comprehend and understand that *quintessential force* under these words: <margin>John 6</margin> *I am the living bread which came down from heaven:* and again: *the true bread is he who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.* Does he not speak of the same thing elsewhere under another form? *You have an unction from the Holy One and you know all things.* And elsewhere: *His unction teaches you about all things.* And elsewhere: *The unction which you have received from him, let it remain in you.*

<meta>This page continues Robert Fludd’s vigorous defense of "Mosaic Philosophy"—the idea that the Bible contains a complete system of natural science—against the criticisms of the French priest and philosopher Pierre Gassendi. Fludd is arguing that the "waters" mentioned in Genesis are not just physical water, but a mystical, divine substance from which all things were made.</meta>

# Fludd’s Response

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 15:3</margin>
<margin>4 Esdras 14:39</margin>
Also concerning the mystical water, where the sacred text speaks—namely, of the living water, the true water of baptism. I do not say that the **fifth essence** <note>The "quintessence," or the purest, highest element in medieval and Renaissance alchemy/physics.</note> is the divinity itself, but rather that it is full of divinity. For this reason, the son of Sirach says of such water: *the water of saving wisdom shall give him to drink.* <note>original: "aqua sapientiæ salutaris potabit illum."</note> Ezra also understood this when he said: *Behold, a full cup was reached to me.* This was full, like water; but its color was like fire. And I took it and drank; and when I had drunk of it, my heart overflowed with understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, and so forth. But Gassendi will say, along with Lanovius, <note>François de La Noue, another critic of Fludd.</note> that I interpret these scriptures partly impiously and partly foolishly to establish my dogmas; I would like them to prove how my interpretation deviates from the truth. For the bread of life descended from heaven; that sacred ointment with which the Prophets were anointed came from on high; and Ezra received the cup from heaven, or from the divine hand. By these things, it is verified that it was of the more excellent marrow of heaven, full of the divine spirit, which true Alchemists call the **fifth essence**. Finally, the sacred page testifies that both Solomon and the Apostles mentioned that first matter from which the heaven, the earth, and all things in them were created: *Thy almighty hand made the world out of formless matter,* <note>original: "Manus omnipotens tuum mundum ex informi materia effecit."</note> according to the interpretation of Tremellius, or as Saint Jerome has it, *from invisible matter.* But if it was from formless matter, then it was from **prime matter** <note>The fundamental, undifferentiated substance from which the universe was created in Aristotelian and Neoplatonic thought.</note> or pre-existing matter, which was in potentiality toward action and form, and not yet actuated or shaped.

<margin>Wisdom 11:18</margin>
<margin>Job 12:22</margin>
<margin>Job 26:7</margin>
<margin>Hebrews 11:3</margin>
<margin>1 Corinthians 1:28</margin>
<margin>2 Peter 3:5</margin>
Hence Job also says: *He reveals foundations from darkness and brings the deadly shadow into light.* And elsewhere: *He stretches the north over the empty place and hangs the earth upon nothing.* And according to the aforementioned sense of Saint Jerome, the Apostle says: *Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were made from things which are invisible.* And elsewhere: *God chose the things that are not, to destroy the things that are.* Moreover, Saint Peter testifies that this formless and invisible matter was water, which is truly the first matter of all things: *The heavens,* he says, *were of old, and the earth, consisting of water and through water, by the word of God.* But the world consists of heaven and earth; therefore, that invisible or formless matter noted by Solomon, from which the world was made, was water. From these things, therefore, it is clear that this doctrine of Gassendi is also erroneous, since the Sacred Text mentions prime matter and that fifth essence, albeit under different names. But I shall proceed to the following parts of his text.

### Gassendi

**Text.** The intention of Scripture is not to teach us exquisite Physics. Its mind is that we should be taught, in whatever way, those things which pertain to salvation; and provided we have perceived that, it matters little if everything does not align perfectly with the rules of the Physicists.

### Fludd

Bah, how foolishly this is said! But, although these matters have already been dealt with quite clearly in the preceding pages, I think, we shall nevertheless examine this double clause of his text. The first is as follows:

### Gassendi

**Text.** The intention of Scripture is not to teach us exquisite Physics, etc.

<margin>Psalm 104:2</margin>
<margin>Psalm 135</margin>
<margin>Psalm 144</margin>
<margin>Job 9</margin>
<margin>Job 28</margin>
<margin>Psalm 147</margin>
<margin>Psalm 148</margin>
<margin>Job 5</margin>
<margin>Job 12</margin>
Alas, how false and far from the truth this is! For it is impossible to understand God Himself, or to grasp Him with sense or mind, except through His creatures configured in a Physical way. Are not all things empty and void without the presence of the divine mind or wisdom, whose role is to fill all things, to give form to all natural things—since it is **Nature Naturing** <note>original: "natura naturans"—a philosophical term for God or the creative power of the universe as an active force, rather than the created world (natura naturata).</note>—and to bring them into physical action? Does not the Apostle say that this eternal wisdom gives life to all things? And giving life is the more formal part of physics. If, therefore, the intention of the scriptures is not to teach exquisite physics, but only that we should acquire innocence of character and salvation: why do they say: *God is clothed with light as with a garment, stretching out the heaven like a skin; he makes the clouds his chariot, who walks upon the wings of the wind, who makes the winds his angels, and his ministers a flaming fire? Causing vapors to ascend from the end of the earth, he makes lightnings with rain, and brings the wind out of his treasures? He bows the heavens, descends and touches the mountains so that they smoke. He sends forth lightnings, removes mountains, shifts the earth, forbids the sun to rise, seals up the stars, stretches out the heaven, walks upon the sea, makes Arcturus, Orion, and the Pleiades? He puts his hand upon the flinty rock and overturns mountains by the roots; he ordained fire, hail, snow, stormy wind, frost, hoarfrost, cold, wind, springs, and rain to perform his word? If he holds back the waters, all things will dry up; if he sends them forth, they overturn the earth? He reveals foundations out of darkness and brings the deadly shadow into light?* Finally, the sacred writings everywhere describe the wonderful works of God in nature and through nature, but especially the Psalms, and Job chapters 9, 12, 26, etc., and the Books of Moses. Concerning which the royal Psalmist says: *Let one generation praise the works of God to another.*

<margin>Wisdom 19</margin>
<margin>Psalm 19:1</margin>
<margin>Psalm 104</margin>
<margin>Job 28</margin>
We conclude, therefore, that God perfected all natural things by His wisdom: from which also descends the harmony of the elements, about which the Wise Man says: *The elements were changed among themselves, just as the notes in a Psaltery change the name of the rhythm,* even though the sounds remain the same everywhere: which can indeed be conjectured from an accurate observation of the things that have been made. Does not also the Prophet say in his hymn: *The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands.* And again: *How magnificent are your works, O Lord, you have made all things in wisdom! By which he gives weight to the air, and weighs the waters by measure, makes a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunders.* Truly, the greater part of the scriptures describes only the wonderful operations of God in nature. Nor can we in any better way know God Himself, or apprehend Him in thought, without His attributes engaged in the nature of things; because through His glory emanating from the creatures, we understand not only His **existence** <note>original: "τὸ ὄν"—Greek for "the being" or "that which is."</note>—namely, *that* He is—but also in many things the **reason why** <note>original: "τὸ διότι"—Greek for "the because" or "the cause."</note>—namely, *why* He is and acts in His creatures. For example: we know Him to be light, love, union, eternity, etc. Hence the son of Sirach says: *The sun that gives light looks upon all things, and all his work is full of the glory of the Lord, etc.* When these things are well weighed, who but one lacking in mind would affirm that the intention of the scriptures is not to teach us exquisite physics? Where (I ask) shall we find a physics truer, holier, or more exact than in this sacred fountain, in which we are taught that God (whose role is to work all in all) is the effecter of natural things through His eternal wisdom? What? Is it in that false and spurious physics of your pagan Aristotle, springing from worldly wisdom and human invention? Truly, if Gassendi says the scriptures do not teach *that* physics, I will easily believe him; but I boldly and constantly affirm that the scripture itself is full of **Sacred Philosophy**. Since this is so, what or in what way (I ask) does that physical doctrine expressed there contribute to obtaining salvation through innocence of character? Therefore, I would have Gassendi understand that the whole power of the scriptures does not tend toward holiness of character alone, but equally looks toward the mysteries of God in nature: so that by that two-fold response of the Mosaic Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>, divided into two by our Savior, we may understand that man is bound by the law not only to the love of his neighbor, but also to know God in His creatures, and having known Him, to fear, revere, and worship Him. For we notice that the work of human genius is not entirely occupied in ethics alone, but principally in physics. For unless we see the divinity, or rather the divine glory...
<margin>Ecclesiasticus 42:16</margin>

<meta>The text cuts off mid-sentence at the catchword "ri" (likely "gloria"). Fludd is concluding that studying nature (physics) is a religious duty just as important as studying morality (ethics).</meta>

# Concerning Impieties. Member IV. Portion I. Part I.

...we may know and draw forth through the observation of physical creatures; it is not possible that we should reach any of His attributes. But to the latter clause.

->Gassendi<-

Text: And once we have perceived this, he cares little whether all things agree exactly to the rule of the Physicists, etc.

->Fludd<-

He speaks rightly, if it were possible to know or recognize God without visible creatures. But the Scriptures, as has been shown in the preceding sections, teach us that God the Creator is revealed through creatures and in creatures. For the wondrous works of God in nature explain His immense power in creation, generation, and preservation. Therefore, it is impossible for us to ascend to the supernatural life unless it be done through natural means. For Jacob’s Ladder <note>A biblical reference (Genesis 28) to a ladder reaching from earth to heaven, often used by Fludd to represent the hierarchy of being.</note> is composed of the steps of nature, and the Chain of Jupiter <note>original: "catena Iovis." A classical metaphor for the interconnectedness of all things from the divine down to the material.</note> bound to the Throne begins from the earth. It is clear from these things, therefore, that Fludd must prove to any wise man, contrary to Gassendi’s opinion, that he has extracted the root of his Physics from the text of Holy Scripture—namely, from the living fountain of true and sacred Philosophy. Consequently, it is Gassendi himself who deserves to be rejected by all, as he unjustly tries to uproot and tear out the root of true Philosophy from the only soil of truth. Do you see here (judicious Reader) how far this doctrine of Gassendi wanders from the straight path of truth; and how thoughtlessly he has attempted to divide and disconnect exquisite Physics from that unique fountain of true Physics?

### Calculation 5. Gassendi page 264.

Therefore, we do not so much disapprove of that first member regarding the various senses of scripture as to deny that a mystical sense lies hidden beneath the historical: certainly, this variety of senses was taken by Fludd from our Theology. What we cannot bear is that the mystical sense is translated into a single Alchemy: that whatever is said of Christ and His precious blood is made to look toward a single Ethereal spirit and the philosopher’s stone; and that whatever is preached concerning the resurrection and the happiness which the blessed shall enjoy in the heavens, all of it must be understood as referring to the Brothers of the Rosy Cross. <note>original: "R.C.F." referring to the Rosicrucians.</note> For what else is this but to hold the profession of Christianity in wicked mockery?

->Fludd<-

See the response to this calculation in Member 3, Part 2, and Text 60. For there, I moved him from his place, and having shattered and pulverized him, I threw him to the wind.

### Calculation 6. Gassendi page 55.

How greatly, by the immortal God, the common crowd in the Schools of the Philosophers is blinded, while the causes of these things are sought without knowledge of chemistry!

->Fludd<-

The causes and origins of meteors <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and lightning.</note> can be expressed and demonstrated in various ways, namely Mathematically, Physically, and Chemically; but the chemical demonstration is the most certain of all, since the method of their production is effected by natural chemistry. For example: Aristotle (who is the Master of this age) says a cloud is made from vapor extracted from water and earth by the attractive power of the heat of the sun and stars, etc. Here you see that the subject from which the subtle part is extracted is water or earth; the vessel is the region of the air, whose bottom is in the earth (the place of natural dregs, as it were); the head of the alembic, <note>An alchemical still used for distillation. Fludd is comparing the layers of the atmosphere to the parts of a laboratory still.</note> in which vapors are resolved into clouds and drops by the force of cold, is the middle region of the air; the Fire or agent is the heat of the sun and the other stars. And so it is with the rest. But more on these things below, when we come to the question.

### Calculation 7. Gassendi page 86.

I do not hesitate in explaining what he means by his Wisdom [Sophia] and what he means by your Folly [Moria]. Namely, it is now clear that only those are wise to Fludd who apply themselves to Alchemy, who seek the Philosopher’s Stone, who affect to become Brothers of the Rosy Cross; <note>original: "F.C.R." (Fratres Crucis Roseae).</note> who, in a word, have as their only goal and in their prayers that eternal wisdom which, incarnate, is called Christ, and applied, is called the Savior, etc., in the sense explained above. Conversely, he despises all those, and you [Mersenne] <note>Marin Mersenne, the French polymath and Gassendi's correspondent, to whom Fludd is also responding.</note> especially, who seek another truth, who are detained by other studies, who do not receive this doctrine, and who—to embrace everything in a few words—are not Alchemists at all, etc.

->Fludd<-

I would wish him first to understand my Alchemy, and afterwards, if he can, let him condemn it. For if he perceived it well, he would by no means hold it for Folly; rather, he would think those people are foolish and raving from a sickness of the mind who would reject it, and consequently reject the cornerstone. <note>original: "lapidem angularem." A play on the "Philosopher's Stone" and Christ as the "Cornerstone."</note> As for the investigation of "another truth," I know this is a poorly chosen phrase, because there is no other truth besides this beloved one which we seek: regarding which, more below. Therefore, since the contents of this text do not touch my Alchemy or my meaning, they collapse of their own accord.

### Calculation 8. Gassendi pages 86 & 87.

It would seem more a matter of grief if you were wise in the Fluddian sense; if, to prove the truth, you did not choose another cornerstone than this Alchemical one—using that ancient touchstone <note>original: "lapide Lydio." A stone used to test the purity of gold.</note> which he argues was rejected by you as a false builder—having cast away that true one through whom we are saved and liberated: the true Christ, true God, and true man.

->Fludd<-

Certainly, if Gassendi and Mersenne worship another stone than that true cornerstone which is the object of the true Chemists, I boldly affirm that they are infidels and reprobates. For there is only one such stone to which divine worship is due. I would wish them to learn to understand Fludd, therefore, before you go about provoking him with false taunts.

### Calculation 9. Gassendi page 89.

Having therefore lowered his speech to the everlasting wisdom, or the soul of the world (what kind he makes it, so that he wants it as his God; in what sense he prays is now sufficiently understood), likewise to that preface to the "sons of doctrine," or Alchemical brothers, etc.

->Fludd<-

Doubtless he thinks here, following that diligent investigation of his into my works, that I hold the "balm of bread" <note>An alchemical preparation Fludd derived from wheat, which he viewed as containing a high concentration of divine light.</note> extracted chemically to be my God, or the eternal wisdom. For he affirmed before that this was the key to my principles. But he errs by the whole width of heaven; and therefore he achieves nothing. But let it be: even if I were so thoughtless as to worship this creature instead of the Creator Himself; yet from error and sin (so to speak...

### C O N C L U S I O N .

From these things, therefore, you see that all these calculations <note>Fludd refers to Gassendi’s numbered arguments as "calculi," the Latin word for small stones or pebbles used in counting.</note> are reduced to smoke by the mere sight of the truth. For it is clear from Fludd’s response that the entire aim of divine Alchemy revolves around that true and unique Cornerstone <note>original: "Lapis Angularis"</note>, so often sung of and celebrated by the Patriarchs, Prophets, and Apostles in the Holy Scriptures. Consequently, it is impossible for the whole of Scripture not to be rightly referred to by Fludd in his Alchemy. For upon this stone, as an immortal and eternal base, all things are primordially founded; since by it (as the Evangelist says) all things were made, and without it nothing was made. Whence, if that Cornerstone were taken away, all things would collapse and be reduced to nothingness and the void; as will be said more clearly in the second part of this section. Therefore, it is evident that Gassendi, together with his disciples (namely, Lanovio <note>Jean de Launoy (1603–1678), a French philosopher and theologian.</note> and Mersenne <note>Marin Mersenne (1588–1648), a famous French polymath and correspondent of Descartes.</note>, who accepted his words as if they were divine oracles), is entirely deceived when he thinks that Fludd’s "Stone" is that of the vain alchemists, who so greedily desire worldly gold and silver, rather than that of God, which is to be bought from Christ. In vain, then, does he proclaim so triumphantly before the world—and especially before the judge and herald of those reckless men—that the "key" to Fludd’s Alchemy has been discovered by him, and that it is the "Balsam of Wheat" <note>original: "Balsamum Tritici"</note>, and the "Quintessence of Bread," and I know not what other fictional imaginings, which are as far as possible from the mark of truth, as will be shown more extensively below. But now I hasten to the discussion of the second question regarding this "Impiety."

## C H A P T E R  II .

->In which the second doubt is resolved; namely, does it not matter to Fludd what religion you belong to, whether Roman, Lutheran, or another? I shall therefore proceed to the examination of the second part of this corner in that Babylonian tower; and I shall break the calculation of both Gassendi and Lanovio, and reduce it to nothing.<-

->Gassendi’s Calculation 2, page 266.<-

*Fludd desires that an Alchemist can exist within any Nation or Religion, by whom the Ethereal Spirit, or that mystical Christ, can be rightly recognized.*

**Fludd.**
This text shows how erroneously, sophistically, and falsely Gassendi deals with us, and how unmindful he is of himself and of the truth. For although on page 39 he admitted that I said the "World Soul" <note>original: "mundi animam"</note> is the purest spirit of universal nature, formed and quickened by the rays of divine light emanating immediately from the eternal Monad—that is, animated by the eternal wisdom, or the Word and Christ—yet in this place he again falsely says that I have taken the "Ethereal Spirit" to be the "mystical Christ." I confess indeed, being instructed by Holy Scripture,

<margin>Ephesians 4.</margin>
that God is in the heavens, and the mystical Christ fills all things; according to that word of the Apostle: *Christ descended, and it is he who ascended above all the heavens, that he might fill all things;* but nevertheless, I do not conclude that the Ethereal Spirit *is* the mystical Christ.

Now, as for the first portion of the text: I say boldly that since there is only one truth, there ought not to be in essence more than one Church and one Religion, which existed from the origin of the world (or that first *Fiat* <note>The divine command "Let there be" from Genesis.</note>) and will endure until the world finally perishes. But as Adam slipped and fell from his prior state, the number "two"—the number of confusion—entered into the world. Thus, the knowledge of good and evil, and the root of righteousness and iniquity, were opened to mortals. From this arose the Mosaic Law to suppress vices, while that primordial law remained untouched, which was originally inscribed on the tablets and temples of the flesh; just as the Mosaic and external Law was inscribed on tablets and temples of stone. Hence, two Churches are numbered by Scripture among men in this world: the Internal, which is true and Archetypal, pertaining to the Law of Christ; and the External, which is typical and Mosaic, upon which so many Religions in the world are founded. These include the Jewish and Muhammadan religions, and so many sects among Christians, such as the Arian, Brownist, Anabaptist, Papist, Lutheran, Calvinist, and so on. For all these names differ only in their ceremonial form, or in various positions differing from truth or reality, and in the variety of their interpretation of the scriptures. Yet it is beyond all doubt or controversy that there is but one truth, at which all these religious sects so zealously aim. There is, therefore, either worldly/human wisdom (according to Scripture) or divine wisdom. The rites of the Worldly Church are founded chiefly upon the bases of the Mosaic law; such a Church is called "political" and, as it were, "typical." It is concerned chiefly with morality and the instruction that ought to be practiced among men for divine worship, and it pertains to that portion of the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments.</note> which Christ summarized as "love of neighbor." But indeed, that Internal Church, which refers to the mystery of God—that is, to the profound contemplation of the Divine Identity—is called "mystical." It is unique insofar as it is occupied with truth alone, leaving behind contentions, variations, and worldly ceremonies. Regarding these two laws in the world, the Evangelist says this: *The Law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ, etc.*

<margin>John 1:17.</margin>
Arguing from this, the Mosaic Law is not the truth itself, but a type <note>In theology, a "type" is a symbol or foreshadowing of a greater reality (the "antitype").</note> of the truth, while truth alone was made through Jesus Christ. Furthermore, the Apostle says this of the mystical Church: *You are built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, with Jesus Christ himself as the chief cornerstone, in whom the whole structure, joined together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord; in whom you also are built together into a dwelling place of God in the Holy Spirit.*

<margin>Ephesians 2:20.</margin>
What the Political and external (or worldly) Church was and is, the Scripture explains everywhere. Similarly, it mentions an external temple made by hands, and an internal one, which it establishes to be the human body. Finally, the Apostle teaches what the mystical wisdom of God is, and what that human and worldly wisdom is.

# To the Impieties. Member IV. Portion I. Part I.

->Calculation 2. From the Letter of Lanovius.<-

In the works of the Brothers of the Rose Cross <note>original: "Fratribus Roseæ Crucis"; the Rosicrucians, a mysterious secret society of the era that Fludd famously defended.</note>, he resorts to a mystical interpretation, by which he undoubtedly describes the "Libertines" <note>In the 17th century, "Libertine" often referred to religious skeptics or those who believed the soul was part of God and thus above moral law.</note>, of whom there is such an ample harvest in this century. He himself is worthy of a beating from Calvin <note>John Calvin, the Protestant Reformer. Fludd is using biting irony here.</note>, so that "man may be a wolf to man" <note>original: "homo homini lupus"; a proverb suggesting humans are naturally predatory toward one another.</note> and the Libertines may fight among themselves—provided that Fludd is not even more irreligious in this regard than Calvin, for by approving of all sects, he signifies that he has none left for himself.

I have responded clearly enough to this text elsewhere. Look, therefore, at Text 19, Member 2, Part 2. For there you will find that this calculation has been turned into smoke and plainly into nothing. Thus, when these things are rightly weighed, it will appear whether it matters to Fludd what religion you belong to, or not.
