### Fludd.

Indeed, I can twist all these things to the contrary and throw them back at Gassendi. And to accomplish this more effectively and present it more clearly to the reader, I will attack each small part of that text separately.

### Gassendi.

**Text.** For thus there will be no creature that is not some little God—namely, one composed of God, etc.

### Fludd.

<margin>composed, etc.</margin>
On the contrary, it is rather thus: there is no creature that does not acknowledge the benevolence and grace of its one and only Creator, who gave it life. Therefore, worship and veneration are owed to Him alone, since He is not only the giver of its life, but also its guardian and preserver, and He reigns everywhere—that is, both within the creature and outside of it.

### Gassendi.

**Text.** Thus it will not be necessary at all to worship any other nature than our own divine nature; for even if certain other greater Gods existed, they would not be more "God" than we are, etc.

### Fludd.

Quite the opposite: if we worship the one and infinite God within us and outside us, He is in truth the only and unique God of Himself. For we shall consider within ourselves that divine honor, worship, and glory are properly owed not to those equal to us, nor to those superior to us, but to that Highest of all, from whom all these others come.

### Gassendi.

**Text.** Thus there will be no reason why idolatry should be forbidden to men, since the essential form of both Wood and Stone is God.

### Fludd.

Indeed, in this way we shall avoid all idolatry. For by considering that there is nothing but the one God and Creator of all things in all things and outside all things, we shall not worship anyone besides that one God, according to that commandment of the Decalogue: *You shall have no other God before me.* <note>The Decalogue refers to the Ten Commandments.</note> Consequently, we shall neither worship nor invoke Gassendi’s "saints." <note>Fludd, an English Hermeticist, often clashed with the orthodox Catholic views of his French contemporary, Gassendi.</note>

### Gassendi.

**Text.** Thus the demons themselves will also be Gods and to be venerated with equal right.

### Fludd.

<margin>1 Corinthians 8</margin>
Rather, driven by these spurs of truth, we shall abstain from the worship of Angels and demons. For we shall recognize that they are nothing but "made gods," or creatures such as we are, animated and brought to life only by the kindness of the Creator. Wherefore, in this respect, we say with the Apostle: *There are those who are called gods in heaven and on earth; yet for us there is one God the Father, from whom are all things, and we in him, and one son of his, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through him.*

### Gassendi.

**Text.** Thus no soul will be more mortal or immortal than another; nor will the soul of a beast be said to perish more than the soul of a man, etc.

### Fludd.

<margin>Job 34:14–15</margin>
On the contrary, led by a secure faith, we shall recognize that every good of the creature, after death or the dissolution of the composite thing, is carried back to its principle from which it was taken. For "good" is not divided from the source of goodness. And in this sense, that sentiment of Job is to be approved: *If God should set his heart upon man, if he should gather to himself his spirit and his breath, all flesh would perish together.* <note>original: "Deus apponit homini animam suam..." Fludd quotes a version of Job 34 emphasizing God's total control over the breath of life.</note> Likewise that of the Psalmist: *When God gives to the creatures, they receive life; when He takes away His spirit, they expire.* God therefore gives life to every creature, and takes it away again.

### Gassendi.

**Text.** Thus there will be no action of the creature, but only of God, whether mediated or immediate, etc.

### Fludd.

In this way we shall acknowledge with the Apostle that God works all things in everyone, and the act or power of working shall be attributed to Him alone, and not to any of the other gods.

### Gassendi.

**Text.** Thus every action, whether of virtue or of vice, will belong not to man but to God alone; and therefore God alone, at least in some part of Himself, will be affected by either reward or punishment—here unhappy, there blessed; here a fool, there a wise man, etc.

### Fludd.

<margin>Job 12</margin>
Finally, in this way we shall recognize that, according to the teaching of Christ, He must be ardently prayed to: *And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.* Since the kingdom and the power belong to Him alone, we shall confess with Job: *The one who errs and the one who leads into error are His.* <note>original: "Ipsius esse errantem, & in errorem inducentem," quoting Job 12:16.</note> For it is He who makes counselors walk stripped and makes judges fools; who removes the heart of the leaders of the earth and makes them wander in a pathless waste where there is no light. Indeed, in this way we shall perceive that God can neither be compensated by any reward—since He Himself gave and gives all that they have to the creatures—nor can He be affected by punishment, since He is the highest of all and the sole actor. Therefore, He can neither be conquered nor suffer.
<margin>Daniel 4</margin>
Furthermore, I wish Gassendi would turn his mind to the words of the Prophet: *Who is there to ask Him, "Why have you done this?"* <note>Referring to Daniel 4:35.</note> Nor do I advise him to hold those words of Job in low esteem: *Far be impiousness from God, and iniquity from the Almighty.*
<margin>Ecclesiasticus 11</margin>
Likewise those words of the Wise Man: *Good and evil, life and death are from God.* Finally, how can unhappiness touch Him who is entirely blessed—nay, who is Blessedness itself, elevated above all things? To Him, therefore, who gives life to all things and works all things in all, be praise, honor, and glory, through the Word, Amen!

Why say more? On these matters, see abundantly above at Text 10, Member 2, Part 2. On the nature of Angels, see Text 41, Member 3, Part 2. Moreover, that absurd "composition" of creatures out of God, which Gassendi falsely assumes and from which he tries to infer I know not how many absurdities, has been refuted everywhere above. We therefore refer the benevolent reader there.

<meta>This page continues Robert Fludd’s defense against the accusations of heresy and "impiety" leveled against him by the French scholars Marin Mersenne and Pierre Gassendi. Fludd is systematically addressing specific "particles" or points of accusation, using a mix of biblical citations and references to Church Fathers like Augustine to justify his Hermetic philosophy.</meta>

# Fludd’s Response, CHAPTER II.

In which each individual part of this "Impiety," as proposed by Mersenne, is cleared away. For once the aforementioned calculations of Gassendi have been reduced to nothing, it is very easy to turn every limb of Mersenne’s "Impiety" into smoke. We therefore approach his argument limb by limb in the following manner.

### Point 1. Mersenne.

->*Fludd believes and teaches that the soul of the world is a composite made of God and that ethereal Spirit.*<-

### Fludd.

<margin>page 37.</margin>
Ha, ha, he! How ridiculous this is, and how it contradicts the confession of his own teacher, Gassendi. For Gassendi himself says that Fludd defines the <term>Soul of the World (Anima Mundi)<note>The concept that the entire universe is a living being animated by a divine spirit.</note></term> as the union of the immortal Light—emitted from the ray of eternity—with the most subtle and worthy portion of the "moist nature," or the waters leaping forth from the womb of dark Chaos. And again, he says that I defined the mind of the world as the purer spirit of Universal Nature, formed and quickened by the rays of divine light emanating immediately from the eternal Monad, and reduced by the union of holy love into a certain living and spiritual nature. 

And yet, this "good man" of ours—an ignoramus—says that I teach the world’s soul is composed of the *Ethereal spirit*. See, I ask you (Good Reader), how do these things fit together? As if the soul of the world was not created before the production of the firmament or the ethereal spirit! Surely it was created when Light was produced by the Creator on the first day of creation. 

Hence Augustine said: "If no scripture is found that contradicts it, it seems it must be said that the soul of Adam was created in the beginning with the Angels, and afterwards came to the body voluntarily to administer to it." These are his words. Therefore, if the soul of Adam is believed to have been created on the first day, much more so the soul of the world. 

But we prove from many places that the life of the world consists of subtle water as the "passive spirit," and the uncreated spirit as the "living and most essential agent." Through this union, the entire mass of waters is distinguished into internal and external, divided, and exists eternally. The internal and central actor for the life and existence of the world is the eternal Word itself, which alone moves in the world, drives all things by its act, and imbues all things with life. 

<margin>2 Peter 3.</margin>
*Saint Peter says: The heavens existed long ago, and the earth was formed out of water and through water by the word of God.* <note>original: "Cæli erant prius de aqua & per aquam conſiſtens verbo Dei."</note> 

From these things it is clear that both the life or spirit of the world (namely, heaven) and the body (namely, its earth) are moved, animated, quickened, and consist in their being and act by means of the Word. Consequently, heaven—which is the spirit or subtle moist nature, or the more subtle portion of water—is quickened, moved, and animated by the Word or the Spirit of Wisdom, whose fountain is the Word. 

Hence the Apostle appropriately says: <margin>Titus 1:6, John 1, Judith 16, Ephesians 5, Wisdom 12.</margin> *God gives life to all things.* If He gives life to all, then He gives life to the spirit of the world as well. And the Evangelist: *In the Word was life: all things were made by Him, and without Him was nothing made. He was in the world, and the world was made by Him, and the world did not know Him, etc.* 

Was not the Spirit of the Lord carried over the waters, imparting a fiery power to them, as Augustine says in his commentary on Genesis? *You sent forth your spirit* (says Judith) *and all things were created.* *God is the Father of all* (says Paul) *who is over all, and through all, and in all.* *Thus an incorruptible spirit is in every thing, etc.* 

What, therefore, can be inappropriate in my assertion when I affirm that God quickens and animates heaven, and moves it by His life-giving act according to His will? Is there any "Impiety" to be found in this statement of mine? But God is the Word, and Life, and is everywhere; if therefore God is everywhere, why should I not say with the Apostle that God gives life to all things? And since His chief seat is heaven, it follows that heaven itself is fuller of His glory and life than the earth, even though the earth is also called His footstool. Do not all philosophers by unanimous consent confess that heaven acts upon lower things just as the soul acts upon the body? Why then should we Christians not say that God acts upon the spirit of the heavens <margin>1 Corinthians 12.</margin> just as the divine mind acts upon the human spirit, since, as the Apostle testifies, *God works all things in everyone*? You see (Readers) how empty these things are which Mersenne has brought forth, being ignorant of sacred matters and mysteries. But let us proceed.

### Point 2. Mersenne.

->*The purest part of this soul is the Angelic nature and the Empyrean heaven, which is understood to be mixed with all things.*<-

### Fludd.

How poorly our Mersenne agrees with himself in this point. For before, he affirmed that I said the soul of the world was composed of *Ethereal spirit*; but here he says the purer part of the world's soul is the Angelic nature and the <term>Empyrean heaven<note>The highest part of the heavens, associated with pure fire and light.</note></term>. As if I were so absurd as to believe or teach that the Empyrean heaven and the Angelic nature, which were the works of the *first* day, were composed of a portion of the work of the *second* day! 

For the Empyrean spirit—the vehicle of the light created in the beginning—was produced first. The Ethereal spirit, or the firmament, was produced on the second day by the <term>spagyric<note>A term from alchemy, referring to the separation and recombination of elements; Fludd views God’s creation of the world as a divine alchemical process.</note></term> power of the divine Word. Who, I ask, is so lacking in mind as to think the principle proceeds from that which is derived, rather than the derived proceeding from the principle? 

It is necessary, <margin>Psalm 68.</margin> certainly, that a liar have a good memory. Finally, if God fills all things, and if God's seat is the heaven of heavens, as the Psalmist says, who would doubt that heaven is as much in the earth as it is in the sky? But I know well enough that these things are hidden from Mersenne.

### Point 3. Mersenne.

->*Demons are also particles of the same essence, but tied to malignant matter.*<-

### Fludd.

<margin>On Genesis.</margin>
Does not Saint Augustine support this assertion of mine most excellently where he asserted that demons are aerial and fiery animals? And elsewhere he says they had aerial bodies in their creation, formed from the purer part of the upper air, so that they might be more fit for acting than for suffering. But by reason of their fall, he says, the bodies or external forms of the evil demons were reduced back into the nature of grosser air, so that they might feel the torments of fire more keenly. 

And Peter Lombard says that the Angels take the bodies in which they appear to men from the highest air, and put on a solid appearance from the celestial element. And Basil says: that Angels are *thin, aerial, and pure spirits.* And Artephius, in his *Key of Greater Wisdom*, says that the external part of the devil is air, while the internal part is fire. 

But what need is there for more words, when reason itself suggests the matter is so? For if the Angelic nature were excluded from the nature of the heavens, then it would either be nothing, or God Himself; but since it is fashioned from light or fire and a watery spirit, it is called a "creature" and "alterity," just as God is called "identity."

He distinguishes between the different days of creation to correct Mersenne’s chronological errors regarding the Empyrean and Ethereal spirits.</summary>

# To the Impieties of Part IV, Portion I, Part III.

Finally, if an Angel were not composed of a twofold nature, it would be impossible for it to suffer; yet I believe it escapes no one's notice that Angels are subject to passions <note>Fludd is arguing that since Angels can experience "passions" or suffering—like the fallen angels—they must have a composite nature rather than being purely simple, divine essence.</note>. It follows, therefore, that this particular piece of his "Impiety" falls apart on its own.

### Point 4. Mersenne.

> All souls, both of humans and of beasts, are nothing other than particles of the same soul.

->Fludd.<-

If the Spirit of God, which gives life to all things, is one and indivisible; if one and the same breath animates all things—indeed, the entire spirit of the world and consequently all things composed from it—then it must be said, and not without justice, that all souls gush forth from the same fountain and derive their origin there. For the Scriptures say: <margin>*Isaiah 42*</margin> *God, creating the heavens and establishing the earth and the things that sprout from it, giving breath to the people who are upon it, and spirit to those walking upon it.* And elsewhere: <margin>*Judith 16*</margin> *And creatures were made; you sent your spirit and they were created anew.* And elsewhere: <margin>*Acts 17*</margin> *God, needing nothing, gives life and inspiration and all things to all. So also in the same place: In God we live, move, and have our being.* And again: <margin>*2 Corinthians 5*</margin> *All things are from God.* Moreover, God is one. God is the Father of all, who is over all, and through all, and in all: and by consequence, he gives life to all things, because in the Word is life. <margin>*Romans 11*</margin> And Job: <margin>*Job 34*</margin> *God established man upon the earth, applying His own soul to him; if He were to take back His spirit or breath to Himself, all flesh would fail and expire, and man would return at once to his ashes.* And David: <margin>*Psalm 104*</margin> *When God gives to the creatures, they gather; when He hides His face, they are troubled; when He takes back their spirit, they expire; when He sends forth His spirit, they are created anew.* Finally, from Him, through Him, and in Him are all things. <margin>*Psalm 33*</margin> We conclude, therefore, with the Psalmist, that *by the word of the Lord the heavens were made, and all their power by the spirit from his mouth:* and consequently, all the lives of creatures, both spiritual and corporal, exist, live, and operate in that same spirit, and are animated by that same spirit: <margin>*1 Corinthians 8*</margin> namely, the Word, in which is universal life. And hence the Apostle says: *There is one God the Father from whom are all things, and one Lord Jesus Christ through whom are all things:* and by consequence, also all quickening and animation, etc.

### Point 5. Mersenne.

> The same soul is the Angel Michael or Metatron.

->Fludd.<-

The wiser <term>Cabalists<note>Followers of Jewish mysticism, which Fludd integrated into his Christian philosophy.</note></term> testify that this great Angel Michael is the one who is the presiding officer and prefect of the sun. What this Angel actually denotes is proven by the interpretation of his name. For *Michael* is as if one were to say: "Who is like God," or the divine power. He is thought by the more skilled to be that Great Angel whose face was splendid like the Sun, and whose right hand held seven stars, denoting that all celestial stars receive their light and glory from the universal virtue of this Angel—who is called in the beginning of that chapter the Alpha and the Omega. This was also he who overcame the ancient Dragon, and who has dominion over every principality, power, and domination. Is it not believed by interpreters that this is that Angel of whom Jacob spoke in his blessing: <margin>*Genesis 48*</margin> *May that Angel who rescues me from all evil bless these boys?* Is not the person of that Angel whom God sent before Moses and the Israelites to keep them in the way through the desert, in whom was His name, ascribed to him? Certainly, almost all interpreters agree on this.

As for the name <term>Metatron<note>original: "Mitattron"; a high-ranking angel in Jewish mystical texts, often viewed as the celestial scribe or a mediator.</note></term>, if you interpret it, it signifies "the gift of God." For, since "Angel" indicates a messenger, an emission, and an emanation from the Father as if from the fountain of divinity, what else, I ask, was the Eternal Wisdom? As is said by the Syrian, Wisdom *was created before all things*, and was with Jehovah (as Solomon says) arranging all things in creation and quickening, and consequently sent forth in the manner of an Angel, like a gift to future creatures, so that He might create all things. Wherefore it is said by Solomon elsewhere: <margin>*Proverbs 8*</margin> <margin>*Wisdom 7*</margin> <margin>*In Art. Cab. Book 3*</margin> *A vapor of the power of God, and a certain emanation, or a flow of the clarity of Almighty God, and the brightness or splendor of eternal light, and a mirror of the Majesty of God without spot*, by means of which all things were made, quickened, and animated, and without it, nothing. Hence the Cabalists (as you will find in Reuchlin <note>Johann Reuchlin, a famous Renaissance scholar of Hebrew and Cabala.</note>) call this Angel the <term>Agent Intellect<note>The "Intellectus Agens," a philosophical concept of a mind that makes human understanding possible by illuminating ideas.</note></term>, from whom all forms flow. And according to the opinion of Rabbi Moses <note>Maimonides.</note> and Rabbi Bereshith, this Prefect of the universe, by whom all individual virtues are governed, is called Metatron. And these opinions of the Cabalists agree exactly with the words of David: "By the Word of the Lord," he says, "the heavens were established, and all their virtues by the spirit from his mouth."

From what has been said, therefore, it is clear how fragile is the basis of this "impiety," and how weak and insufficient—not to say ignorant of these matters—the Author himself is. I shall proceed, therefore, to the fourth Impiety.

***

## PART IV OF PORTION I, MEMBER IV.

### In which the fiction and insufficiency of the fourth Impiety is treated. The fabricated Impiety itself is this:

->Mersenne in his Letter.<-

**Fourthly**, Fludd feels and teaches that the same soul of the world is the true Messiah, the Savior, Christ, the Cornerstone, and the universal Rock upon which the Church and all salvation is founded. Namely, that this is the chief part of the <term>Philosopher’s Stone<note>A legendary alchemical substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting eternal life; here used metaphorically for Christ.</note></term>, which when condensed grows red, and from then on is called the blood of Christ, by which we are cleansed and redeemed. For we are not cleansed by the human blood of Christ, but by this divine and mystical blood.

->Fludd.<-

Here this herald [Mersenne] fabricates in a wonderful way; transcending by far the limits of my meaning, he yearns to poorly mix the ideas of Joachim Frizius <note>A pseudonym likely used by Fludd himself or an associate in earlier Rosicrucian writings.</note> with mine. But because Joachim Frizius expressed those things which he wrote in an enigmatic way through symbols, I will voluntarily undertake to openly defend his cause against these adversaries, and I shall begin with that chief calculation which Gassendi put forward, and upon which this "Impiety" most heavily relies.

# Fludd’s Response,

## CHAPTER I.
### In which the principal reckoning of this Impiety is set forth.

->Reckoning 1. Gassendi, page 265.<-

I observe only what he has in this book concerning that passage from Saint John, *The blood of Jesus Christ the son of God cleanses us from all sin* <note>original: "Sanguis Iesu Christi filii Dei emundat nos ab omni peccato"</note>; he holds in these words that this speech does not intend—supply "Saint John" here—human blood, but that which is divine and mystical. Whence he speaks of the blood of Jesus Christ, the God-born, and not human blood. But I ask you, was not Christ the Savior a true man just as he was the Son of God? Did he have or pour out blood on the altar of the cross as God, and not as man? Was this blood not truly human, even if, through that ineffable union, it excelled all other blood? Could any other blood have the power to cleanse us from all sin? Who then is this other "gore," not human but mystical, which according to Fludd’s mind could perform this?

->Fludd.<-

This reckoning I have thoroughly uprooted elsewhere; namely in *Text 10, member 2, part 1, and text 62, member 3, part 2,* where I responded to every objection therein. Therefore, lest I do what has already been done, I refer you (benevolent Readers) to those places, and I hasten to refute the individual members of this "Impiety."

### In which every small part of this Impiety is reduced to nothing in a few words, and converted from Impiety into Piety.

Fourthly, Fludd feels and teaches that the same soul of the world <note>The *Anima Mundi*, a concept suggesting the universe itself is a living being animated by a divine spirit.</note> is the Messiah, the Savior, Christ, the Corner Stone, the Universal Rock, etc.

<margin>

But Fludd did not say that the soul of the world *is* the Messiah, etc. Truly, if he shall have proved that the animator of the soul of the world—namely its center and driving force—is the eternal wisdom and the Word of God: will it then be so great a crime in Fludd to assert accordingly that the internal act and life of the worldly soul is the Messiah, the Savior, Christ, the Corner Stone, the Universal Rock, etc? For is not Christ the Messiah, the Savior, and the Corner Stone one and the same with the Word and the eternal wisdom of God? God (says the Apostle) gives life to all things. The Word (says Saint John) is the life of the world, for in the Word was life. Christ (says Saint Paul) carries all things by the word of his power; and he in the beginning founded the earth, and the heavens are the work of his hands. The true bread is he who descends from heaven and gives life to the world. But Christ and the Word is that bread descending from heaven, as he himself witnesses elsewhere. It follows, therefore, since all things draw their life from the universal life of that Catholic <note>Here meaning "universal."</note> soul, that the root and fountain of life is the Word, Christ, the Messiah, the eternal wisdom, and the corner stone. Concerning which the Apostle also says: *All ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the Rock was Christ,* etc. Behold, Mersenne, here you have the life of the world, the spiritual food, and the nourisher described, and at the same time proved to be the Messiah, Christ, the Word, the Corner Stone, and the Universal Rock. I say "Universal" because he fills all things. *He who descended is the same who ascended, that he might fill all things,* says the Apostle.

I conclude, therefore, that the eternal power of the soul of the world is the Messiah, the Savior Christ, the bread descending from heaven, the Word, the eternal wisdom, the corner stone, the universal rock, the life and sustenance of mortals, and finally Jesus Christ himself, who is all in all.

->Part 2. Mersenne.<-

->Upon which universal rock the Church and all salvation is founded.<-

->Fludd.<-

Isaiah 28.

Indeed, I certainly acknowledge that the Church and the entire salvation of the world are situated upon that Rock. *A stone* (says the Prophet in the person of God) *I will place in the foundations of Zion, a tested stone, a corner stone, precious, set in a founded foundation.* This stone is Christ, who was rejected by you builders, but who has become the head of the corner. Upon this highest stone, as upon a foundation, the faithful are built up. Concerning which, and the hidden and secret structure of the mystical Church, Saint Paul says: *You are no longer strangers and foreigners, but you are citizens with the Saints and members of the household of God, built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, with the chief cornerstone being Jesus Christ, in whom the whole building, being joined together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord, in whom you also are built together into a dwelling place of God in the Holy Spirit,* etc. Saint Peter says: *Upon that stone, Christ himself, you are built up as living stones, a spiritual house, a holy priesthood,* etc.

From these things I would now like Mersenne to understand: what is that true Theo-Philosophical stone <note>Fludd’s term for a spiritualized version of the Philosopher’s Stone.</note>, and what is that mystical temple? But if he does not understand, or scorns to notice, let the shameful brand of ignorance be upon him, and not upon me. Regarding the essential foundation of the Church, both its external and internal aspects, see after text 50, member 3, part 2, in the sections concerning the Highest Good.

->Part 3. Mersenne.<-

->That this rock is the principal part of the Philosopher’s Stone; which, when thickened, grows red, and from that is said to be the blood of Christ, by which we are cleansed and redeemed.<-

->Fludd.<-

If there is any "more-than-perfection" in the common Philosopher’s Stone (as one must believe if a single grain is to convert a great mass or quantity of leprous metal—say, lead or iron—into true gold, for nothing natural exceeds the degree of its own perfection), it follows surely that a spark of that divine stone is present in that stone. For truly, nothing is "more-than-perfect" that is not full of divinity. We say without hesitation that the mystical spiritual stone of the Theo-Philosophers, and the true rock of the Patriarchs, Prophets, and Apostles, is most full of divinity.

But in that place where Fries <note>Likely referring to a source or colleague of Mersenne.</note> says that this rock, when thickened, grows red, and is thereafter called the blood of Christ by which we are cleansed; I would have the Reader know that he speaks parabolically or metaphorically, expressing the powers and multiplication of spiritual and invisible things through the visible symbols of common Alchemists. For just as they gape at a visible stone or powder, which grows together from a flowing and volatile substance into a

<meta>This page continues Robert Fludd’s vigorous defense against the accusations of Marin Mersenne. Here, Fludd elaborates on his "spiritual alchemy," explaining how alchemical stages like the 'Red Lion' are metaphors for the soul's purification through Christ. He transitions from discussing the mystical blood of Christ to refuting the 'Fifth Impiety' regarding the nature of a just man and the Brothers of the Rose Cross.</meta>

# To the Impieties, of Member IV, Portion I, Part IV.

The **fixed rock**, which they <note>Referring to the alchemists</note> believe first matures in **whiteness** <note>original: "albedine"; the stage of purification in alchemy</note>, and is afterwards increased in fiery power, passing from whiteness into **yellowness**, and from yellowness into **blood-redness**, and then they call it in their fashion the **Red Lion** <note>original: "Leonem rubrum"; a term for the final, potent stage of the alchemical stone</note> and by many other names: so too does Frizius <note>Likely Joachim Frizius, a name Fludd used as a pseudonym</note> compare the increase of grace multiplied within a human being to the compression of a solid thing. For every thing that is expanded in all directions, if it be thickened, is constricted into a narrower place. Therefore, that **Light of grace** contracted within a person becomes visible, and is accustomed to appear in him through its effects in no other way than the invisible air itself is contracted into a visible cloud. And this gift of the divine word, flowed from above into the heart and blood, and inhabiting the spiritual blood, can not undeservedly be called the **blood of Christ**, as if it were the vehicle of Christ's power in us. For that Light is, as the Apostle witnesses, <margin>Romans 10:</margin> *In our mouth and in our heart* <note>original: "In ore & corde nostro"</note>, and we are his members. Does not Saint John also say this? *Christ,* he says, *is in his Father,* <margin>John 14.</margin> *and you in him, and he in you.* <note>original: "Christus, ait, est in Patre suo, & vos in eo, & ipse in vobis"</note> Frizius points to this mystical, quantitative multiplication as that "thickened rock," and I too have made mention of it where it is said that the *kingdom of God grows from a grain into a mountain*; and through its "reddening," he argues for the fullness of the divine, calling it the **blood of Christ**, in exactly the same way as common Alchemists signify their stone by the **blood of the Red Lion**. 

Therefore, Frizius compared Christ's blood parabolically to a visible thing when it reigns effectively in someone. Thus in the scriptures, he is symbolically called the **Lion of the Tribe of Judah**. Thus wisdom is compared to a carbuncle, a Topaz, and the purest **Tincture** <note>A substance in alchemy capable of transforming other metals or healing the body</note>. Moreover, Christ seems to have sought this dominion of divine power from the Father, saying: <margin>John 17.</margin> *Glorify your son, as you have given me power over all flesh, so that all which you have given me, he may give to them eternal life.* <note>original: "Clarifica filium tuum... det eis vitam æternam"</note> Furthermore, that a bodily appearance of wisdom could also occur was right to gather from these things. *In Christ dwells all the fullness of the godhead bodily.* <note>original: "In Christo habitat omnis diuinitatis plenitudo corporaliter"</note> He does not say "in the body of Christ," but "in Christ," the fullness of the godhead dwells bodily. For the growth of the **cornerstone** is openly indicated through the word "fullness." Finally, concerning this multiplication, the Apostle says thus: <margin>1 Corinthians 3.</margin> *Paul plants, Apollo waters, but God gives the increase.* <note>original: "Paulus plantat, Apollo rigat, sed Deus dat incrementum"</note> It is necessary, therefore, for Mersenne to know that Frizius, in that entire thread of his discourse concerning the cornerstone, the rock, and Christ, is speaking of spiritual and intellectual things. He did not understand them as bodily, or elemental, or sensible in the common way, but as spiritual and intellectual. But concerning these things, more will be said more broadly below.

### Small Part 4. Mersenne.

> For we are not cleansed by the human blood of Christ, but by this divine and mystical blood.

->*Fludd.*<-

See the response to this small part in Text 62, Member 3, Part 2, and there you will find this "Impiety" turned into piety. I descend, therefore, to the fifth Impiety.

# MEMBER IV. PORTION I. PART V.

## Here the fifth Impiety is treated: and it is as follows.

### Mersenne in his Letter.

Fifthly, Fludd teaches that a **just Man is an Alchemist**, who, having found the **Philosophical Stone**, becomes immortal through its use. Yet he is said to "die" when he casts off his corruptible parts; to "Rise again" when he is incorruptible; and to be "glorified" when he consequently attains those same gifts which are attributed to glorified bodies. Men who have escaped to this state, called **Brothers of the Rose Cross**, know all things, can do all things, and do not think it robbery that they are equal to God, since the same mind is in them which was in Christ Jesus.

# CHAPTER I.

### In which (omitting those calculations upon which Gassendi relies, since they are reviewed in the aforementioned places) all the members of this Impiety are briefly removed and reduced to smoke.

### Small Part 1. Mersenne.

Fludd feels and teaches that a just man is an Alchemist, etc.

->*Fludd.*<-

Fludd does not deny that a pious and just man is a **spiritual Alchemist**. But does Mersenne know, or does he recognize a true Alchemist? Indeed, it is he who can distinguish truth from falsehood, virtue from vice, darkness from light, and the impure stain of sin from the purity of the God-formed soul, and separate them by the fire of divine genius. For by this and no other way is **leperous lead** turned into **gold**: namely, by the required washing and cleansing. Thus by tears, and penance, and abstinence, sin is separated from that super-celestial spark of life—from the true gold (I say) and from the world's Christ. Thus a son of darkness, by his own industry and by the divine act of the Word operating and assisting, rises up and is exalted into a **son of God and of light**. Thus an impious and unjust man, through the clarifying of that spiritual Alchemy, is sublimated out of darkness into the shining sphere of piety and justice. And the sacred Scripture is concerned with this kind of divine Alchemical business. For example:

<margin>John 3.</margin>
> He who does the truth comes to the light, so that his works may be made manifest, because they are done in God.

<margin>John 12:</margin>
> The light is still a little while among you. Walk while you have the light, lest the darkness overtake you; he who walks in darkness does not know where he goes. Therefore, it is the work of the **Christian Chemist** to separate the darkness from his soul, multiplying his light, walking in the light and not in the darkness. Whence Christ says:

<margin>John 17.</margin>
> Glorify your son, that your son may glorify you; I have glorified you on earth, I have finished the work you gave me to do; now, Father, glorify me with yourself with the glory I had with you before the world was made.

From which it is clear that clarification and purification from darkness through Jesus Christ is quite necessary before anyone can truly be called just.

<margin>Matthew 5.</margin>
> Let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your father. That is, put away and separate the darkness from your hearts, so that the light which is in you may shine forth, and so that from sons of the world you may become sons of God.

<margin>Matthew 6:</margin>
<margin>Matthew 13.</margin>
> If the light that is in you is darkness, how great will that darkness be, etc.

> The just shall shine like the Sun in the kingdom of their Father.

# Fludd’s Response

<margin>
Matthew 13.
Romans 13.
John 7.
John 1.
Psalm 75.
</margin>
Christ was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the Sun, etc. 
Let us cast off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light. 
A just man is accustomed to attribute the glory of his virtue to God. 
The Lamb of God takes away the sins of the world. 
The just shall drink from the purity of the cup of Jehovah and shall be exalted, but the wicked shall be weighed down by its dregs.

<margin>
Job 1.
Job 22.
</margin>
Regarding the manner of the separation of darkness from light in a just man, Job says: *A man who is whole, upright, and fearing God, retreating from evil.* <note>original: "Vir integer, rectus, timensque Deum, recedens à malo."</note> This is the process of separating the darkness and the filth of ignorance from the living gold of one's own life. Hence, concerning the effect of this kind of **Alchemy**, it says elsewhere: *The just man returning to God shall abound in gold; for the Almighty shall be his choice gold and silver, and his strength.* Or thus: *If you return to the Almighty, you shall be built up, and you shall put iniquity far from your tabernacle. He shall give flint for earth, and for flint, torrents of gold, and he shall heap up silver for you. Then you shall abound in delights, and you shall lift up your face to God; you shall ask him and he will hear you, and you shall pay your vows. You shall decree a thing and it shall come to you, and light shall shine in your ways, etc. For he who has been humbled shall be in glory. That is, he shall be exalted, etc.*

Here, therefore, let Mersenne <note>Marin Mersenne (1588–1648), a French mathematician and priest who was a fierce critic of Fludd’s mystical philosophy.</note> see, if it please him, what kind of Alchemist a just man is. I do not mean a false alchemist, but a **mystical and true** one. Let him also see how, by the effect of this kind of alchemy—or the true **Theo-philosophical stone**—one might reach the peak of immortality. Christ says: *I am the bread descending from heaven; he who eats this shall live forever.* But concerning this species of true Alchemy, I shall speak more abundantly below.

->**Point 2. Mersenne.**<-
> Yet they are said to "die" when they cast off their corruptible parts; and to "rise again" when they become incorruptible.

->**Fludd.**<-
And why not? Since "death," as it is commonly spoken of, is the separation of the corruptible body from the incorruptible spirit. In truth, I know of no other death. Moreover, that the **resurrection** is the reviving of a dead thing through the incorruptible Spirit of God, Saint Paul teaches us.

->**Point 3. Mersenne.**<-
> They are said to be "glorified" when they consequently achieve the same gifts which are attributed to glorified bodies.

->**Fludd.**<-
And why not likewise? Truly, this is defining the same thing by itself.

->**Point 4. Mersenne.**<-
> Men who have escaped to this state, called the **Brothers of the Rose Cross**, are said to know all things, to be able to do all things, and do not think it robbery to be equal to God, since they affirm the same things are in them which were in Christ Jesus.

->**Fludd.**<-
I would wish that Mersenne would not proceed to lie with such rashness. For neither I, nor Frizius <note>Joachim Frizius, a pseudonym or close associate through whom Fludd often published.</note>, said that the **Brothers of the Rose Cross** are equal to God. They themselves say in their Letter, and do not blush to assert, that the Spirit of God—or the Divine Mind which is in them—is God, and that this is no "robbery" to God <note>A reference to Philippians 2:6; Fludd argues that because God dwells in them, they possess God's spirit, not that their human nature is God.</note>. For Sacred Scripture testifies that Jesus inhabits our lowly bodies, and that we are members of Christ, and the temple of the Holy Spirit, whose role it is to teach all things: and by whose kindness and power Solomon knew even the very thoughts of men. Therefore, the **Brothers of the Rose Cross** conclude that he who is united to Christ becomes one spirit with him; and consequently, he can understand all secrets in Christ and through Christ. But if I had said it thus, would I disagree with the words of the Sacred Text, which are as follows?

<margin>Philippians 2.</margin>
*Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God, etc.* I would like Mersenne to examine those words: I shall say no more. Finally, what the subject of the Alchemy of the true Brothers of the Rose Cross is, and what its power and action are, and what the stages in its operation are, may be drawn from those things which Frizius explained in their Letter. As for what pertains to me, many things are attributed to me by Mersenne and Gassendi <note>Pierre Gassendi, another prominent philosopher and contemporary critic of Fludd.</note> which are not mine. Yet, because even those things which belong to my friend Frizius rest upon their own reasons—which are not at all discordant with the truth if inspected a little more diligently—then those very things (as it seems to me) are very easy and light to support. I proceed therefore to the final Impiety, which is of the same grain as the rest: and therefore, once the former ones are resolved, this one must necessarily collapse of its own accord.

# MEMBER IV. PORTION I. PART VI.
->In which the sixth Impiety is examined, which is this:<-

->**Mersenne in his Letter.**<-
Sixth, Fludd teaches that **Creation** is not the production of a thing from nothing, as we commonly understand "nothing." He teaches that **Matter** (which he very often calls **Darkness**) is that which is properly called "nothing," and therefore when God is said to create or make something from nothing, it is understood as creating or making from Matter. He claims that Moses, when he described the Creation of the World, was an **Alchemist**, as were David, Solomon, Jacob, Job, and all the others, so much so that even the true **Kabbalists** are nothing other than Alchemists; as are the Magi, the Sages, the Philosophers, the Priests, and others.

## CHAPTER I.
->In which the sixth corner of that Babylonian tower built by Mersenne is destroyed.<-

->**Point 1. Mersenne.**<-
**F**ludd teaches that creation is not the production of a thing from nothing, as we commonly understand "nothing"; that Matter, etc.

->**Fludd.**<-
The Sacred Text says: *The hand of the Almighty created the world out of unformed matter;* <note>original: "materia informi"</note> as it is held in the interpretation of Tremellius: or as Jerome says, *from invisible matter.* Therefore, it was from pre-existing matter.

But because I have fully responded to that objection above in the third question, Text 10, Member 2, Part 2 of this Treatise; I therefore refer my benevolent readers to that place. For there, I have utterly uprooted this point.

<meta>This page continues Robert Fludd’s vigorous defense against the French scholar Marin Mersenne. # To the Impieties, Member IV. Portion I. Part VI.

### Point 2. Mersenne.

Mersenne claims that Moses, when he described the creation of the World, was an Alchemist; likewise David, Solomon, Jacob, Job, and all others; so much so that even the true Kabbalists <note>original: "Cabbalistæ"</note> are nothing other than Alchemists, as are the Magi, Sages, Philosophers, Priests, and others.

->Fludd.<-

We boldly say that Moses, in the book of Creation or *Genesis* <note>original: "Berischith"</note>, spoke exact words concerning divine Alchemy, or the effect and work of mystical Alchemy. In this Alchemy, the fiery operator of the divine Alchemist was the Word <note>The *Logos* or Christ</note>: the first matter or chaos, around which he worked, was the darkness: the material subject extracted from the darkness, or the "second matter," from which all things—namely heaven and earth—were extracted by the working Word, was water. And these waters the same Word, the Spirit of God <note>original: "Ruach Elohim"</note>, divided by his <term>spagyric</term> <note>Spagyric refers to the alchemical process of separating parts and recombining them into a purer form</note> power; namely, he separated the thin waters from the thick ones by means of the intermediate waters. By this kind of description, I say, Moses demonstrated himself to be an excellent Alchemist. I do not say a spurious and adulterated one, but a divine and God-taught <note>original: "Theodidactum"</note> one.

<margin>Psalm 118.</margin>
David also spoke many words concerning the Cornerstone: *The Stone which the builders rejected (he says) has become my salvation; this has become the head of the corner. This was done by the Lord, and it is a miracle in our eyes,* etc. The Apostles also treated this wondrous Stone in *Matthew 21, Luke 20, Acts 4, Romans 9, and 1 Peter 2.*

<margin>Isaiah 28.</margin>
The Prophet Isaiah described its origin and seat thus: *I place a Stone in the foundations of Zion, a tried Stone, a precious cornerstone, founded in the foundation.*

Jacob mentioned this spiritual Stone typologically when he asserted that the Stone, which he set up as a monument and upon which he poured oil, was the House of God and a place in which he was wonderful: which for this reason he called *Bethel* <note>Hebrew for "House of God"</note>.

<margin>Prov. 3. Wisdom 7. Prov. 8.</margin>
Solomon describes the wondrous powers and acts of eternal wisdom, saying that it works wonders in the world, and is a thing so precious that it excels gold, precious stones, and choice silver.

Job also speaks abundantly to the understanding about this subject and its mystical apparatus, from *chapter 28 to the end of the Book.* And regarding this matter, read my response to *text 20, Member 2, Part 2. See also Portion 2 of this Member 4, Part 1, chapter 3 in its entirety.*

Finally, that the true Kabbalists and true Alchemists are concerned with one and the same thing—likewise the Magi, Sages, and Philosophers—can be hidden from no one of sound mind: since there is only one Supreme Good and one true Stone, at whose goal all true sages aim with the most vigilant eyes: some of whom are occupied with the Kabbala, others with Alchemy, others with Theo-philosophy, and others with natural Magic.

Here then you see (Readers who hold the scales of justice) how fragile, sterile, and collapsing by themselves are those dregs of impieties, or rather the fragments of Mersenne, if they are considered with mature judgment and right reason: except that he stains them with a fouler appearance, overflowing with lie upon lie. For this malevolent brother of ours adds many things of his own so that those things which are good in and of themselves might seem evil to the world at first glance. And thus he longs to sprinkle and defile the truth with falsehood.

Now indeed I will hasten to reveal the key to my Alchemy in some way, so that the world may be able to discern in the light of truth that my aim and intention are not as impious as Mersenne makes them out to be.

## Member IV. Portion II. Part I.

#### In which it is proved that God himself, through his Word, or Wisdom, or the Cornerstone, and Christ, by divine and wondrous Alchemy, established the world or macrocosm, and all things in the world, and also formed them in diverse ways.

## PART I. CHAPTER I.

->Here, what Alchemy truly is is explained in few words.<-

<margin>On the Chemical Art. Dorn. Augustine. Pantheus. Voarchadumia. Albertus Magnus. Arnold of Villanova.</margin>
Some define Alchemy as nothing other than the purification of nature, asserting that the thick matter itself cannot be cleansed and purged of its filth unless it receives water into itself as a medium. Others want Chemical Philosophy to teach how to investigate the latent forms—according to the truth of the thing and not appearance—and to separate them from the fecal and dark subject. Others say that the Alchemical profession is that which teaches the method of transmuting things; and it is not to be hoped for [by human skill], but rather to be attained by divine grace. Others say that this transmutatory art is called Alchemy from the Hebrew word *Alchemo* <note>A speculative etymology used in the Renaissance</note>, which signifies: "the leaven of vain counsel is interposed." That is, when the matter has no true existence of gold and silver, but a completely empty and false appearance, it is rightly to be condemned and utterly removed. It is as if he had said: Alchemy is the division of the pure and true from the impure and false; of light and clarity from darkness and gloom; of sin and vice from goodness and Virtue—just like true gold and silver are separated from false worldly filth. Others think that through Alchemy the metals which are corrupted and imperfect in the mines are reduced to perfection: that is, the substantial and healthy are distinguished and freed from the corrupted and fecal. Others likewise conclude that Alchemy is one hidden part of natural Philosophy, and necessary above other parts, from which a single art is constituted, to which there is no equal. For by it imperfect precious stones are perfected, and the sick human body is restored to health.

From these definitions it is evident that the effect of this Art is to distinguish and segregate the vile and fecal (or filth) from the precious; the thick from the subtle; the impure from the pure; the false and merely apparent from the true and essential—and that by number, weight, and measure. And truly, as every Art is the "Ape" or imitator of nature, so indeed nature is the Image of the Divine Word itself; since nature acts, lives, and moves in the Word or divine Spirit, or eternal wisdom, as much in purification and refinement as in condensation and thickening. Created nature <note>original: "natura naturata"</note>, therefore, received the laws of its Alchemy from uncreated nature <note>original: "natura naturante," referring to God as the creative source</note>. For just as Nature is taught and moved by eternal wisdom, so indeed and not otherwise does she operate in her chemical workshop,

# Fludd’s Response

...and artificial alchemy itself imitates nature in every matter, and is seen to be governed by nature's mediating Agent. When these things are rightly considered, it is evident that there is an **archetypal alchemy** <note>The "archetype" refers to the divine blueprint or original form in God's mind</note>, which is that radical process through which the divine Spirit acts in both the greater world <note>the macrocosm or universe</note> and the lesser world <note>the microcosm or human being</note>. There is also a **natural typical alchemy**, which does all things in imitation of that archetypal one, though not without the <term>spagyric</term> <note>the art of separating and recombining elements to purify them</note> virtue of the archetypal Actor. For in this way, the celestial Sun works upon the worldly Spirit through subtilization, and the winds and stars work through both thickening and purification; yet they do not do this by themselves, but by the action of Him who placed His tabernacle in the Sun. Finally, there is **artificial typical alchemy**, in which God works through nature in both worlds.

From what has been said, it is clear that the term "Alchemy," in respect to the subject it treats, can refer to the actions of the supernatural, the natural, and the artificial alike. But it is as impossible for natural chemistry to perform more without divine action than it is for artificial chemistry to work without the help and assistance of nature.

Now, I shall briefly explain who the actors are in archetypal or radical alchemy, and I will show in short that, although they are distinguished by many names in the sacred text, in essence they are but a single actor and operator.

# CHAPTER III.

### Here it is shown that the entire fabric of the Macrocosm is completed by the Spagyric virtue of the Word (or the Spirit of Wisdom, or the spiritual Christ), dividing the pure from the impure into regions and spheres.

Since the entire perfection of Alchemy turns upon the division of the pure from the impure, the darkness from the light, and the subtle from the gross; let us see, I pray, who is the actor and operator in the true and Highest Alchemy? And what kind of **Cornerstone** is it that He hides in the composition and reveals again in its resolution? Now, since the end is named by the beginning—that is, the end reveals the beginning through resolution, by reducing it back into its first matter—and since whatever makes something a certain way is itself even more that way; it must be believed that this Spiritual Stone, which is revealed through the power of the Word, was that very angular foundation upon which all things in the world (and consequently the world itself) were constructed. For when the word **"Let it be"** <note>original: "Fiat"</note> was brought forth according to the will of the Speaker, the creature was made; it was founded upon the spiritual Cornerstone of that Word; and in it, the creature exists and persists, since He is the one who sustains all things, according to the Apostle: *Christ carries all things by the word of his power.*

<margin>The words of Psalm 12. <note>original: "Verba Psal. 12"</note></margin>
<margin>Hebrews 1.</margin>
That nothing is purer or more subtle than the Word and the truth is testified by the Royal Psalmist: *The words of Jehovah are pure, like silver refined in an earthen furnace, purified seven times.* And Solomon says of it under the title of Wisdom: it is a *subtle spirit, mobile, sharp, possessing all power, more mobile than all mobile things,* <margin>Proverbs 8.</margin> *reaching everywhere because of its purity, able to do all things; for it is the vapor of the power of God, and the brightness of eternal light,* and finally, by its activity, it composes all things and, in turn, resolves composed things back into their principles. Therefore, that Spirit is the highest agent in divine and supernatural Alchemy. For Wisdom herself, or the Word "**Let it be**," has within itself the Spagyric Virtue of both composing and separating each and every thing from the dark matter—as if from Nothing into Being, from darkness into light, from night into day, and from confused waters into liquid substances that are separated and recognizable. Thus all things came from the hidden into the manifest through <margin>Hebrews 4.</margin> the Word of God, which is living and sharper than a two-edged sword (as the Apostle says), reaching even to the division of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow. It is no wonder, then, if Moses said that light was produced from darkness—that is, extracted and separated by the power of the Word "**Let it be**." Hence also Job says: <margin>Job 12.</margin> He reveals the foundations out of darkness and brings the shadow of death into the light. He stretches out the North over the empty and void, <margin>Job 26.</margin> and hangs the earth upon nothing. Has it not also been said that the Almighty created the world from unformed or invisible matter by His Word, as if by His hand? But let us proceed to the stages of extractions or divisions which God ordained by the Spagyric power of His word in the making of the world.

In passing (Kind Reader), I would not want it to seem harsh to you that I said "by the Spagyric power of the Word": because this word *Spagyrist* or *Spagyric*, so often used by the Chemists, signifies and intends one who discerns the true from the false, the good from the evil, and the impure from the pure—that is, one who casts away the "two" while preserved the "one." In this way, the power of the Word, sharper than any trial, separates Light (or truth) from darkness (or fiction); day from night; and morning from evening. Then, it separates the subtle, bright, and holy waters of the higher heaven from the thick and dark waters of the lower or elementary heaven. And then finally, by the force and activity of a similar wisdom, by dividing the mass of dark waters into the flimsy and the thick, He made the dry land (or Earth) appear in their midst as if it were the dregs of all the waters. In this way, you see that Saint Peter's axiom is true: <margin>2 Peter 3.</margin> namely, that the heavens existed before, and the earth was standing out of the water and through the water by the word of God. That is, by means of the divine Spirit or the Spagyric power of the Word, He converted the subtle part of the waters into a spiritual nature or heaven, and their thickness into the substance of the earth. In this manner, from the mass of waters, by this divine Alchemy, the world was forged into heaven (which is its subtle part) and earth (which is its gross part). And so, from the creation until this day, the heavens and the earth and all their host consist by the act and power of that word—no differently than a palace erected upon its cornerstone, by that stone (which is of the structure...

Furthermore, this divine Spirit acts through <term>natural Chemistry</term> <note>Fludd views the movements of nature as a series of chemical reactions directed by God.</note>, placing his tabernacle in the Sun. Thus, by his <term>Spagyric</term> <note>The "Spagyric" art refers to the alchemical process of separating and recombining elements to achieve purity.</note> action, weather phenomena are daily procreated in the airy heavens. He sometimes places his fiery workshop in the air to dissolve and liquefy, and at other times uses a cooling vessel to coagulate and condense things that were thin and subtle, changing and transmuting that heaven into earth—namely, changing air and waters into snow, hail, frost, and ice. Hence David says: *With his word running most swiftly, and his speech sent forth upon the earth, God gave snow like wool, and scattered frost like ashes; he casts down his ice like morsels; who can stand before his cold? He sends forth his Word and melts them; as soon as he breathes his wind, the waters flow.* By these things it is evident that the act of divine Chemistry consists of congelation by cooling and liquefaction by heating, through the power of the Word. Truly, this same Spagyric office is also assigned to him under the title of Wisdom. For the patient man <note>Referring to Job.</note> says: *God by his Wisdom fits the weight to the air, and weighs the waters in a measure; he makes statutes for the rain, and a path for the lightning of the thunders.* At his presence the earth was moved, the waters shall be afraid, the clouds poured out waters, the upper clouds gave forth a sound, even his stones passed through, and as the thunder sounded, lightnings illuminated the habitable earth in that orb; the earth was moved and trembled. His way is through the sea, and his path through the ample waters. At his presence the mountains melt like wax; he makes the clouds his vehicle or chariot, and walks upon the wings of the wind; he makes his Angels winds, and his ministers a flaming fire. Finally, by the either dilating or contracting power of his Word, God does whatever he wills in the heavens and on the earth, through the seas and all the abysses, making vapors ascend from the ends of the earth; he makes lightnings with the rain, and brings forth the wind from his treasures. From these things it is evident that nothing in the whole world is perfected by nature that the Word of God does not work through Chemical or Spagyric operation. Thus he also sends down uniform influences, and emits by his Word winds that both rarefy the Spirit of the world and condense it. Briefly, he works all in all in the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "Macrocosm" refers to the great world or the entire universe.</note> by way of Alchemy: that is, by purifying nature and separating the gross from the subtle, and consequently by Spagyric virtue and faculty: that is, by separating the impure from the pure, the true from the false, unity within the binary number or multitude, and the subtle within the gross, by way of composition and constriction, from the subtle parts of the Macrocosm combined with the gross.

Now, I shall show in a few words what sort of thing this divine Alchemy is in the nature of the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "Microcosm" refers to the "little world," or the human being, viewed as a reflection of the universe.</note>; and what that <term>Cornerstone</term> is—the truly God-philosophical Stone—which all Wise Men have sought with such great desire and craved with the appetite of Tantalus:

# CHAPTER IV.

->Here it is declared that, according to all true Alchemists, this is the gift of God, which they establish as the foundation of their Art; and then, what that Gift is, is shown in a few words.<-

<margin>Job 10.</margin>
The Word works no differently in the Microcosm—namely, in its composition from the seed, as if from an imperfect mixture extracted from all the father’s members, whether earthly or heavenly, like the subtle from the gross, to multiply its species infinitely; no differently, I say, than in other compounds imbued with a soul. Hence the patient man says: *Have you not poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese? You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and woven me together with bones and sinews; you have exercised kindness toward me with life, and your visitation has preserved my Spirit.* Here, therefore, one may see how, by the wonderful separation, solution, and coagulation of the Alchemical art, he produced the Microcosm—namely, man—in his own image; for he divided him into heaven and earth: and then afterwards preserved him, by working wonderfully within him through his Spirit or Spagyric art and natural chemistry. For he prepares the bread descending from heaven in the left chamber of the heart, and preserves that which is prepared in the Aorta for the quickening of the whole, and for sustaining the Spirits of life; by secreting the more subtle parts of it from the grosser, he adapts them like the "upper waters" to perfect the animal and rational functions; the middle parts, however, like the "waters of the firmament," he destines for performing the actions of life: and finally, he drives the lower spiritual parts of that world to the life of the lower bodily waters, and to perform the life-giving natural virtues. Furthermore, to preserve the clay house of this Microcosmic heaven, he grinds and prepares food in the mouth as if in a mill; he draws that which is prepared into the Stomach-pot for cooking, and there digests it as if in a <term>Bain-marie</term> <note>original: "Balneo Mariae," a water bath used for gentle heating in alchemy.</note>; then he separates the gross from the subtle, the bad from the good, the superfluous from the useful, and that which is gross and dreg-like he thrusts downward and casts out; that which is good and chyle-like he raises through filters—namely, the mesenteric veins—and distills it into the Vessel of the Liver. There he cleanses the whitening chyle, like lead that is still "leprous" <note>In alchemy, "leprous" metals are base or impure metals awaiting purification into gold.</note>; and the superfluous Melancholy <note>One of the four humors, associated with the element of earth and the spleen.</note> he sends out by distillation to the side, namely through the splenic branch, into the spongy capsule or storehouse of the Spleen; that which is bilious he drips down into the gallbladder; the watery and serous substance he pours out into the bladder, by the marvelous craftsmanship of natural Alchemy; and finally, that which is extracted from the truth of the matter, he transmutes into ruddy blood, like "animal gold." But he proceeds even further by purifying, and sublimates the blood prepared in the Liver up to the heart, and in the right ventricle of the heart, he again reduces it into a more pure substance, so that it may contribute to the preservation and nutrition of the light lungs. Finally, from this species of Alchemy he proceeds to the coagulation of liquid—namely, of blood into flesh, and fleshy juice into nerves, cartilages, and bones. He does all this himself through his Word, whose role alone it is to work all things in all by himself.

That this Word, or divine wisdom, or Light of men, is the goal of the wisest true Alchemists, at which they aim, may be gathered from their own words. King Calid says: *The secret of the glorious God is the greatest sister of Philosophy; it was inspired by God into his Prophets and certain elect believers in him.* Hermes says: *I have the knowledge of this art only from the inspiration of the one God.* Morienus the Roman says: *The subject of this work ought not to be thought of as anything but the gift of God Most High and Great, who shows it to his servants; may his name be forever blessed.*

# To the Impieties, Member IV, Portion II, Part I.

And elsewhere: This mastery is nothing else than the mystery and **Secret of Secrets** of the Most High God; He himself entrusted this secret to the prophets. **Geber** <note>Geber, or Jabir ibn Hayyan, was a legendary 8th-century polymath often considered the father of chemistry; Fludd cites him to lend ancient authority to his spiritual chemistry.</note> says: *Our Art is reserved in the power of God, who grants it to whom He wills and withdraws it.*

**Parmenides** says this: *But this is specifically that which He granted God to be able to do.*
**Bulgus** in the *Assembly of Philosophers* <note>original: "Turba [Philosophorum]" — one of the oldest Latin alchemical texts, written as a transcript of a meeting of ancient philosophers.</note> says: *It is given by divine inspiration: for which reason all Philosophers say that it is a gift of God, because God grants it to the one who knows and perfects it, and does not withdraw it. But to the one who knows and perfects but does not receive it, God does not grant it, but withdraws it, because that which he ought then to retain vanishes from his eyes.*

Certainly I could bring forward infinite other testimonies; but it would be too long to recite them in this place. But does not that saying of the Apostle also perfectly agree with these: *it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth (he says), but of God that showeth mercy.* <margin>Wisdom 9.</margin> And **Solomon**: *Who shall know the counsel of God, unless God gives wisdom, and sends the Holy Spirit from the highest places?* <margin>Wisdom 7.</margin> Is it not said that wisdom is a vapor of the Power of God, and an emanation of the brightness of the Almighty, and the whiteness or splendor of the Eternal Light, renewing all things, powerful in all things, and yet remaining in itself, transferring itself into holy souls, and establishing the friends of God or prophets. Indeed, the wise man concludes; that God loves no one, except him who dwells with wisdom. By these words we see how the Sacred Text concurs with the opinion of **King Calid** <note>A reference to Khalid ibn Yazid, an Umayyad prince associated with early alchemy.</note> and of other wise Chemists, whose **Alchemy** is far different from that which is only sought after by common people. And no wonder. For worldly men gape after worldly things. But all those deeply versed in **Theosophy** <note>Fludd uses "Theosophy" to mean "divine wisdom" or the study of God through nature and scripture.</note> have judged the greatest work to be within man; and that of the greatest labors of Hercules, to know oneself rightly is not the least. Therefore, wise man, <note>original: "Γνώθι σεαυτὸν" / "Gnothi seauton"</note> **Know thyself**. Nor can a Prudent man acquire anything greater or more excellent than a sound Mind in a sound body. But if anyone should say that the Word, or Christ, or the Holy Spirit of wisdom, is in the Microcosmic heaven; he would be held as impious and abominable by the blind worldlings; although the sacred text says in open words: that the life of man is the breath of God; that life is in the Word, and that life is the light of men. And the Apostle says: *Say not in your heart, who shall ascend into heaven, that is, to bring Christ down, or who shall descend into the abyss, that is* <margin>Genesis 1.</margin> *to recall Christ from the dead?* But what does the scripture say? *The Word is near, in your mouth and in your heart.* <margin>John 1.</margin> And elsewhere: *Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ?* <margin>Romans 10.</margin> Again: *Do you not know that your members are the temple of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have from God: Glorify and carry God in your body.* <margin>1 Corinthians 6.</margin> Furthermore, the Apostle addressing the Heathens, and those who followed unknown Gods: *God is not far from each* <margin>Acts 17.</margin> *of us: for in Him we live, move, and have our being, for we are also his offspring.* <margin>Isaiah.</margin> Whence also the Prophet says: *look back to the Rock from which you were hewn.* But the Rock was Christ. <margin>Ephesians 2.</margin> Hence the Apostle: *Be built up as living Stones upon the stone Christ himself.* <margin>1 Corinthians 10.</margin> It is also proved thus: Christ is the spiritual Rock, according to Paul, and <margin>1 Corinthians 10.</margin> the highest Corner Stone: But Christ is in us, and the Spirit of God dwells in us: for that Spirit <margin>Ephesians 2.</margin> which raised Jesus from the dead dwells in us, according to the same Apostle: Therefore Christ, that highest <margin>Romans 8.</margin> cornerstone, is in us, upon whose bases we are built up. Wherefore we are not incongruously called members of Christ by the same man. <margin>1 Corinthians 6.</margin>

Just as Christ is the most worthy of all spirits, so he is exalted according to his dignity, and has his seat in the most worthy heaven of the Microcosm <note>The "Microcosm" is the human being, viewed as a miniature map of the entire universe.</note>, namely the **Soul**. Whence also elsewhere Christ is not unjustly called the head of every man. For He alone is Truth in the Microcosmic heaven, without which the Spirit of the Microcosm would be empty, which is the vehicle of the divine spark: which spark, fixed and permanent, is that pure gold to be bought from Christ; the Word (I say) *Fiat* <note>The "Let there be" of creation.</note>; by the power of which Adam was made into a living Soul, as the Text says. But the Truth of the **Alchemist**, according to the doctrine of Christ or the incarnate Word, they seek and knock for, so that they may arrive at the knowledge of that life of fire and the bread descending from heaven, and may know how to multiply that grain of life in a fivefold or tenfold proportion, and finally, having thus multiplied those talents committed to them as faithful servants, they may emerge from the darkness, in which there is weeping and gnashing of teeth, and receive their reward in the kingdom of heaven: This is the true species of **Alchemy**, to exalt the Light overwhelmed by gloom out of the darkness. The fire of this Alchemy is that of the divine genius excited by the Word, drawing out spiritual tears of repentance to purge away the leprosy of sin, and to pour out the sighs of the praying soul to God, who, having heard the prayer, sends forth the Spirit, clarifies Christ surrounded by darkness and as if crucified, and puts to flight the volatile [spirits] of that golden spirit, and makes it one with his living gold, and thus the rational creature becomes one Spirit with Christ. <margin>John 17.</margin> Hence Christ said: *Father, glorify me with yourself, with the clarity which I had with you before the world was made. Father, those whom you have given me, I will that where I am, they also may be with me, that they may see my clarity, which you have given me,* etc.

Finally, concerning this kind of chemical method of purging, the Apostle says most excellently: *but even until this day, when Moses is read, the veil is placed over their heart; but when they shall have turned to the Lord,* <margin>2 Corinthians 3.</margin> *the veil shall be taken away.*

*Now the Lord is the Spirit: but where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty; but we all with unveiled face (that is, with the darkness laid aside) beholding the glory of the Lord, are transformed into the same image, from clarity to clarity, as by the Spirit of the Lord,* etc. By which he seems to intimate, that the operator and multiplier in this Alchemy is the Spirit of the Lord; but the subject is the human, who, immersed in the darkness of ignorance, cannot lay aside the veil of the Mosaic Scripture: that is; he cannot separate the literal or external, impure, and dark, from the Spirit or internal luminous [part]; or, men cannot understand Spiritual things, and behold the glory of the Lord with the face of Scripture revealed, unless they turn themselves and adapt themselves to the Lord, so that they may be so clarified by His Spirit or Word, that they may be transformed into the same image with Christ, namely from clarity to clarity, through multiplication.

Similarly he says these things elsewhere: *He himself said that light shines out of darkness, He himself has shone in our hearts, for the illumination of the knowledge of the clarity of God in the face of Jesus Christ.*
> *We have this treasure in earthen vessels: Although our man who is without is corrupted, yet* <margin>2 Corinthians 4.</margin> *he who is within is renewed from day to day.*

Since this is so, I do not see the reason why the names of **Alchemists** may not meritly be ascribed to those very people who give their labor, by means of the divine spirit, to separate spiritual darkness from spiritual light, the spiritual and invisible impure from such a pure thing, sin and injustice from justice, Vice from Virtue, ignorance from knowledge, fiction from truth, and to clarify a thing that is opaque and covered with internal gloom, and to render it limpid and transparent, and finally to exalt what is base and depressed and to raise it to a worthier state.
