# Fludd’s Response

Indeed, the artistry of this Alchemy can be as aptly attributed, metaphorically speaking, to Christ himself and his Apostles as it is to the arts of Agriculture or Gardening. 
<margin>John 15.</margin>
Did not Christ himself say, *I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman: every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away: and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit?* <note>original: "purgabit" — in an alchemical context, this suggests purification or refining.</note>
<margin>Ibid. 4.</margin>
Furthermore, he speaks there of the structure built upon the Cornerstone <term>Cornerstone (Lapis angularis)<gloss>In alchemy, Christ is often identified with the "Philosopher's Stone" that serves as the foundation of spiritual transformation.</gloss></term> metaphorically in these words: *As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me. I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.*
<margin>Ibid. 8.</margin>
*Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit.* Here, therefore, you see the method of multiplying and clarifying <note>original: "clarificandi" — refers to the alchemical process of making a substance transparent or pure, here applied to spiritual "glory."</note> applied to Agriculture.
<margin>1 Cor. 3.</margin>
By a similar reasoning, the Apostles express their work of multiplication through the mystery of Gardeners: *I (says Paul) have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase. So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase. Now he that planteth and he that watereth are one: and every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labour. For we are God's fellow-workers: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building.* Again, the Apostle applies this spiritual work to Architecture. *According to the grace of God which is given unto me (he says), as a wise master-builder <note>original: "Architectus"</note>, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.* This agrees with the preceding text from John: *I am the vine, ye are the branches; without me ye can do nothing.* Then he proceeds in the manner of the Chemists to his examination in this way: *If any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day of the Lord shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved. Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you? If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are, etc.* Here, therefore, you have it expressly explained that the mystical work of the New Testament—and its stages toward perfection, multiplication, and examination—is expressed by the Sacred text in ways that are Agricultural and Gardening-related, as well as Architectural and Alchemical. Not otherwise have the wise Philosophers sometimes expressed their own Chemical art through the craft of the Farmer and the Gardener, in their own parabolic or metaphorical way. For example: **Jodocus Greverus** <note>A 16th-century priest and alchemist known for his work "Secretum nobilissimum," which describes alchemy through the metaphor of farming.</note>, a Priest, wrote one chapter on the sowing of seeds into the earth; another on the harrowing of the sown field; a third on the budding of the sprout; a fourth on the growth of the sprout; a fifth on the emergence of flowers and the formation of seeds; a sixth on the ripening of the seed; a seventh on the harvest, and so on. We say, therefore, that the nature of Alchemy agrees perfectly with the above-mentioned words of St. Paul. For, as Paul says, *I planted, and Apollos watered, but God gave the increase;* and Christ says, *I am the vine, you are the branches; he who remains in me brings forth much fruit, because without me you can do nothing;* so indeed in Chemical Philosophy—which teaches one to investigate hidden forms according to the truth of the thing and not its appearance, by the division of the pure from the impure—the artist can do nothing unless he disposes the matter, waters it, and makes it fit to receive the celestial influxes which God pours in. *The Holy Spirit (says the Scripture) will not enter an unclean thing, nor will God give wisdom from on high to an impure heart.* From these things it can be seen that this Alchemy is that perfect and most true Alchemy, or Divine Philosophy depicted through Alchemy, which even the wiser Chemists seem to acknowledge in these words: 

**Basilius Valentinus** <note>A legendary alchemical figure, likely a pseudonym for several authors, credited with popularizing the concept of the three principles: Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury.</note> says: *Although the animals of the earth are composed of flesh and blood, just like man, and have a life-giving spirit and breath instilled in them, yet they are destitute of a rational soul, with which man is endowed above all other animals. Therefore, when the Brutes exchange life for death, it is utterly over for them. But man, if he offers his life to his Creator through temporal death, his soul shall live on; and when he has been clarified <note>or "glorified"</note>, his soul, returning into a clarified body, shall dwell there, so that the body, soul, and spirit may be gathered together and show forth their celestial brightness, which can never be separated for all eternity. Wherefore man, by reason of his soul, is acknowledged as a fixed creature; for (though he may seem to die outwardly) he is to live forever. For death is the clarification of man. However, a spirit can dwell in a certain body, but it does not follow from this that it will be fixed; although the body and spirit may agree, yet both lack that strong bond which binds and confirms the body and spirit together, and protects and defends them against all dangers: namely, the most precious, noble, and fixed soul. And this is one of the greatest secrets that it befits the wise man and the diligent seeker to know. Yet my conscience did not allow me to pass this over in silence, but to reveal it to those who love the foundation of all wisdom, etc.*

It should be noted in passing that of the three species of the Stone <note>Alchemists often divided the "Stone" into Mineral, Vegetable, and Animal types.</note>, the **Animal Stone** is most praised by the wise (as it is found in the *Rosary of the Philosophers*), which they have asserted to be that **Cornerstone** which the truly wise and knowing love, but the foolish and stupid hold in derision; according to that aforementioned saying of the Apostle: *rejected and repudiated by the ignorant; but esteemed by the elect as divine power and the Gift of God, and desired by the truly knowledgeable in every age, and sought after with the appetite of Tantalus.*

But back to the matter. **Artephius** <note>A famous medieval alchemical author, often claimed to have lived for a thousand years by means of the Elixir.</note>, a very wise man, seems not to disagree with the aforementioned words of Valentinus when he says: *God is bound to His creatures through His word, and separated from them insofar as He transcends them. For He created nothing equal to Himself; but of His great benefits, this is the greatest: that He has bound our body with the most subtle of all elements, namely the soul, which sees hidden things clearly, provided that the power of the body does not dominate it. For as much as the powers of the body are strengthened, so much must the virtues of the soul be weakened.* Hence says the Master **Belenius** <note>Often identified with Apollonius of Tyana in alchemical literature.</note>: *Place your light in a clear glass vessel, and note that all the wisdom of this world revolves around these three: namely, the binding of a corporeal soul with a corporeal soul, a spiritual soul with a corporeal one, and a spiritual one with a spiritual one. But the bond of a corporeal soul with a corporeal one is closer and easier than that of a spiritual one with a spiritual one.* These are his words.

The prudent man **Belenius** also says: *Do you seek your light, which is your soul? Seek it in a small glass vessel; that is, in a body not too fattened: for thus can the intellect know and comprehend the secrets and wonders of God.*

**Morienes the Roman** <note>A legendary hermit-alchemist said to have taught the secrets of the art to the Umayyad prince Khalid ibn Yazid.</note> says this: *God placed man among the elements themselves as a greater ornament. Why should I relate more? For this thing is extracted from you, for you are its mine; for they find it within you, and to confess the truth, they receive it from you; and when you have proven this, your love and affection for it will increase within you.*

# Regarding the Impieties, Member IV, Portion II, Part I.

This mastery <note>original: "magisterium" — in alchemy, this refers to the successful completion of the Great Work or the process of transmutation.</note> is nothing other than the secret and mystery of secrets of the Most High God. For He himself entrusted this secret to His prophets, whose souls He has placed in His paradise.

**George Ripley** <note>An influential 15th-century English alchemist and cleric.</note> says: *Remember that man is the noblest creature in the earthly composition, which God never [otherwise] created, in whom there are four elements proportioned by nature; a neutral mercuriality, which consists of nothing at all, is produced by art from its mineral.*

**Geber** <note>Referring to the legendary 8th-century figure often called the "Father of Chemistry," whose Latinized works were foundational to European alchemy.</note> teaches that one cannot reach the perfection of true Chemistry unless they recognize its principles within themselves.

Finally, to come to the Alchemy of the **Brothers of the Rose Cross** <note>The Rosicrucians, a mysterious spiritual and scientific movement that Fludd defended against charges of heresy.</note>, since I perceive the vehemence expressed everywhere in the writings of **Gassendi**, **Mersenne**, and **Lanovius** <note>Prominent 17th-century scholars and critics of Fludd, particularly the priest and mathematician Marin Mersenne.</note> against the aforementioned Brothers—while they hold those men and their doctrine, and especially their Alchemy, in ridicule and contempt—we say that the subject of their Chemistry, their Stone, and their governance during the production of that **Cornerstone**, does not differ from that of the holy men and truly wise who have labored in this business throughout every age. To demonstrate this more clearly, we will examine the words of their Epistle published by Joachim Frizius at the end of his treatise *On the Highest Good*.

Regarding the entire subject of true Alchemy within us, they say:

> We read in John that God is the highest Light, and we walk in the Light, because we show the Light (though in a closed lantern) to the world. But you, worldly man who denies this, you are ignorant, or you do not see; you ought to know that Jesus inhabits your lowly body.

<margin>Colossians 2.</margin>
<margin>John 1.</margin>
<margin>Colossians 3.</margin>
Here, therefore, according to the aforementioned doctrine of both the most profound Alchemists and the Apostles and Prophets, you see that the operator of all wonders is within us: precious Jesus, I say, inhabits our houses of clay. For, as Scripture testifies, *in Jesus Christ dwells all the fullness of the Divinity bodily:* so indeed, by the same testimony, *of his fullness have we all received.* It does not hinder anyone to assert that this discourse is understood of the Apostles alone, and not of all men indiscriminately. For he says elsewhere, *Christ is all in all.* But I proceed.

That the subject or effect of their Alchemy is that **Cornerstone** <term>Cornerstone (Lapis angularis)<gloss>Fludd argues the alchemical "Stone" is a spiritual reality: Christ himself, the foundation of the human soul.</gloss></term>, which the Patriarchs, Prophets, and Apostles thirsted for with such fervor, is explained in these words:

> Do you proudly wish to rise above the circles of heaven? Do you ambitiously wish to rule over this earth and your dark body in heaven? Or do you, unworthy ones, wish to do all wonders gracefully? Therefore, recognize the rejected Stone, what it is, before it is sought.

<margin>Genesis 28.</margin>
Here he describes the goal and boundary of divine Alchemy, at which all lovers of Christ are accustomed to aim: namely the Cornerstone, or the rock which is Christ, as the Apostle testifies. For the Stone which the Patriarch Jacob erected and anointed with oil, calling it the house of God, typologically designated that spiritual one.

<margin>1 Corinthians 10.</margin>
By that hard rock from which Moses drew water, this spiritual and cornerstone was typologically prefigured. For the Apostle, speaking of it, said: *And that Rock was Christ.*

<margin>Psalm 118.</margin>
This is the Stone that the Psalmist intends in these words: *The Stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.*

<margin>Isaiah 8.</margin>
<margin>Isaiah 28.</margin>
<margin>Isaiah 51.</margin>
<margin>Daniel 2.</margin>
<margin>Zechariah 3.</margin>
This is the Stone of which the Prophet Isaiah says: *A stone of stumbling, and a rock of offense, it shall be for a snare to both houses of Israel, etc. I will lay in the foundations of Zion a Stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation.* And elsewhere: *Look to the Rock from which you were hewn.* And it is that of which the Prophet Daniel spoke: *A stone cut without hands from the mountain, crushing the clay, iron, bronze, silver, and gold; the King is Christ the Lord, reigning forever.* And again: *The stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.* And the Stone of which the Prophet Zechariah spoke, *which I have set before Joshua; upon one stone are seven eyes, behold I will engrave its inscription.* Finally, it is the Stone of which

<margin>Acts 4.</margin>
<margin>1 Peter 2.</margin>
<margin>Ibid.</margin>
<margin>Ephesians 2.</margin>
<margin>Romans 9.</margin>
<margin>1 Corinthians 10.</margin>
the Apostle Peter spoke: *Christ is the Stone, which was rejected by you builders, which has become the head of the corner, and there is salvation in no other. Upon this stone, Christ, be you built up as living stones, a spiritual house, a holy priesthood.* And again: *I lay in Zion a Stone, a chief cornerstone, tried, elect, precious, and he who believes in him shall not be confounded.* And Paul: *Upon the chief cornerstone, in the foundation, the faithful are built up.* And again: *I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, etc.* And elsewhere: *A spiritual Rock followed the Fathers, and that Rock was Christ.*

From these things, therefore, it is clearer than light that this spiritual Rock is that which not only the Brothers of the Rose Cross, but also the men chosen by God—namely the Patriarchs, Prophets, and Apostles, whom they imitate in this spiritual Alchemy—looked upon. Consequently, an exact response is given here to the final point of **Mersenne’s Impiety**, which is this: *Fludd teaches that Moses, when he described the creation of the world, was an Alchemist; likewise David, Solomon, Jacob, Job, and all others, etc.*

<margin>Wisdom 7.</margin>
<margin>Ibid.</margin>
<margin>Ibid. 8.</margin>
For it is clear from the Holy Bible that all these men sought the possession of this spiritual Stone. And Solomon gives the reason: *Because (he says) wisdom gave me true knowledge of these things which are, so that I might know the disposition of the world, the virtues of the elements, the beginning, the end, and the middle of times; the changes of the solstices and the successions of seasons, the circuits of years and the positions of stars, the natures of animals and the tempers of wild beasts, the force of winds and the thoughts of men, the differences of plants and the virtues of roots; and all such things as are secret or manifest, I learned. For Wisdom, the worker of all things, taught me. She makes friends of God and Prophets, and loves only those who dwell with wisdom. For I preferred her before kingdoms and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison to her, nor did I compare to her any precious stone, because all gold in comparison to her is a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her. I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for her light is unquenchable. All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches through her hands; and I rejoiced in them all, because this wisdom went before me, and I knew not that she was the mother of them all. She is an infinite treasure to men, which they that use become partakers of the friendship of God.*

<margin>Proverbs 3.</margin>
<margin>Proverbs 8.</margin>
<margin>Ecclesiasticus 6.</margin>
<margin>Ecclesiasticus 24.</margin>
Finally, *she is more precious than all works, and all things that can be desired are not to be compared to her, for in her right hand is length of days, and in her left hand riches and glory; wherefore her fruit is better than gold and precious stones, and her blossoms than choice silver; since she is life, beauty, and her bonds are a healthful binding. Yea, indeed, she is the book of life, the testament of the Most High, and the knowledge of truth: established in Zion, and resting in the holy City—*

He concludes by citing Solomon to prove that biblical figures were "alchemists" in the sense that they possessed divine Wisdom and knowledge of the elements.</summary>

# Fludd’s Reply,

<margin>Isaiah 8. Matthew 21. Ecclesiasticus 6. Ecclesiasticus 21.</margin>
This is the stone of which the Prophet says: *I will place a stone in the foundations of Zion, a tested stone, a cornerstone, precious, a sure foundation.* <note>original: "Lapidem ego mittam in fundamentis Sion..." — Fludd is quoting Isaiah 28:16, identifying Christ as the ultimate foundation of his spiritual alchemy.</note> Yet this is the Stone rejected by the foolish and those who build poorly. For the Syriac text says that wisdom is too harsh for unlearned men, and the heartless man will not remain with her: *The power of the Stone shall be a test for the foolish; they will not delay in casting it aside, for she is at all times a scourge to some, but a teaching to others.* <note>Fludd cites the Book of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus), emphasizing that "Wisdom" and the "Philosopher's Stone" are the same divine substance.</note>

Having duly considered these things, we must see whether it is truly impious or impossible (as **Mersenne** <note>Marin Mersenne (1588–1648), a French priest and mathematician who was Fludd's chief intellectual rival.</note> claims in his "Fifth Impiety") that men who enjoy this Wisdom, or this **Cornerstone** <note>Lapis Angularis</note>, can know all things—even the very thoughts of men, as the Prophets and Apostles understood them. We must ask whether, by the power of this Cornerstone, it is a hard thing to say that a person could become immortal, or whether it is "robbery" to claim that the Holy Spirit within a person—as the head of the inner man—is equal to God. For in truth, this Spirit is a holy emanation and the brightness of God's power; indeed, it is God himself, as the Scriptures say.

<margin>1 Corinthians 2. Ecclesiasticus 6.</margin>
Now we come to the "regimen" <note>The set of rules or the governing process used to complete an alchemical work.</note> that must be observed in this kind of **mystical Alchemy** <term>Alchymia mystica: A spiritualized version of alchemy where the "transmutation" happens within the human soul rather than a laboratory flask.</term>. I call this alchemy "mystical" and not "common" because it reveals to the elect that mystical wisdom of God, of which the Apostle says: *We speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, which has been hidden, which God ordained before the ages for our glory.* And elsewhere: *God predestined hidden wisdom before the ages for the glory of the elect and the Apostles.* The wise man also says: *Come to Wisdom like one who plows and sows, and wait for her good fruits. For in her work you shall labor but a little, and soon you shall eat of her generations.*

The **Brothers of the Rose Cross** <note>The Rosicrucians.</note> therefore understand Alchemy and the "Great Work" far differently than **Gassendi**, **Mersenne**, and **Lanovius** understand it. To the Brothers, the methods of common chemists are nothing but a shadow and a puzzling symbol of the true chemistry. In their Chemical Art, they possess neither the gold of the common people, nor silver, nor common fire, nor artificial furnaces; for all such things are either dead or, at the very least, merely superficial compared to the true materials. Therefore, they say this:

> Among the most approved authors, you shall receive the truth under the shadow of the law (for the wise man reads one thing but understands another): Are you imperfect? Pant after your due perfection. Are you foul and unclean? Purify yourself with tears; <term>sublime</term> <note>In chemistry, to turn a solid to vapor; here, to elevate one's character.</note> yourself through morals and virtues. Adorn and color yourself with sacramental graces. Make your soul <term>subtle</term> <note>Refined and pure, capable of perceiving divine truths.</note> and ready for the contemplation of heavenly things, conforming it to the Angelic spirits, so that you may <term>vivify</term> <note>To bring to life.</note> and whiten your decaying body and vile ash, making it entirely incorruptible and beyond suffering through the resurrection of Jesus Christ our Lord.

For this reason, they say elsewhere: "Be ye transmuted, be ye transmuted, from dead stones into living Philosophical Stones."

The Apostle seems to support them in this matter with these words: *Through Christ we both have access in one Spirit to the Father. Therefore you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the Saints and members of God's household, built upon the foundation of the Prophets and Apostles, with Jesus Christ himself as the chief Cornerstone. In him the whole building, joined together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord, in whom you also are being built into a dwelling place for God in the Holy Spirit.*

Here one may see the nature of this spiritual transmutation and, consequently, the nature of that divine Alchemy of the Brothers of the Rose Cross—which is so greatly despised and mocked by the perverse and the ignorant. One can see the nature of that true Cornerstone, rejected and disapproved with such impiety by "false builders," for it is utterly unknown to those of this world. Regarding this worldly absurdity and ingratitude, St. John says: *He came into the world, and the world was made through Him, and the world knew Him not. He came unto His own, and His own received Him not; but as many as received Him, to them He gave the power to become the sons of God.*

This is that divine transmutation or secret Alchemy, for its Stone is Secret, and hidden most deeply from the senses of mortals. This, I say, is not common, illegitimate, or false Alchemy; it is true and secret. This is why that Fraternity, in its *Confession* <note>The *Confessio Fraternitatis* (1615), one of the founding manifestos of the Rosicrucians.</note>, candidly published these things to the world:

> In conclusion (they say), we earnestly warn you regarding our confession that you remove from yourselves the greater part (if not all) of those books composed by false and illegitimate Alchemists. For we consider it a joke and an impiety when they wrongly apply the Holy Trinity to vain and empty things through such delusions, strange figures, and obscure sentences, intended to deceive the simple commoners of their money. There are a great number of such books published in this age by the instinct and agitation of the enemy of the human race, so that the worst things are mixed with the good (making it harder for worldly people to find goodness) and believed by incredulous mortals. Therefore, we warn you who are wise: avoid such books. We persuade you instead to choose the Holy Bible; let it be the rule of your life and the goal of all your studies, etc. (Thus they say in their confession.)

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 6. Ecclesiasticus 22.</margin>
Why then, I ask, does the world pursue the name of the Brothers of the Rose Cross and their mystical subject with such hatred? Truly for no other reason than that cited from the Sacred Text: *namely, because wisdom is so harsh to unlearned men, and the heartless man will not remain in her; she is at all times as much a scourge to the foolish as she is a doctrine to the prudent.* I call her a "scourge" to the children of this world—that is, the enemies of the Cornerstone—but to the others, she is the teaching of God. The Apostle makes it abundantly clear to us in Romans chapter 9 how much the children of God differ from the children of the world.

Thus, the Brothers of the Rose Cross say of the children of the world, not without cause:
*He who increases knowledge, increases sorrow, because in much knowledge there is much indignation!* We speak from experience. All the worldly ones—boastful braggarts <note>original: "Thrasones" — a reference to Thraso, the "braggart soldier" stock character from Roman comedy.</note>, vainglorious, pompous, talkative, and empty—meritlessly blaspheme and curse us, even regarding things they do not know. But we do not wonder that the ungrateful world has persecuted the professors of the true arts along with Truth itself. Thus they speak of such worldly people as Mersenne and his ilk, and not without merit.

I therefore advise Mersenne to choose more strong and capable athletes or champions for himself to better defend his reputation. For these men are far too weak and powerless

# Towards the Impieties. Member IV. Portion II. Part I.

...to subvert the foundations of Fludd’s Philosophy. They clearly lack the key by which the secrets of Fludd’s Philosophy might be opened; since it is built upon fabulous foundations, it must necessarily collapse on its own. On the contrary, those six stains of sin, which God holds in greatest hatred, and the seventh which his soul detests, cling so firmly to **Marin Mersenne** <note>original: "Marino Merſenno" — Fludd is referencing Proverbs 6:16-19, which lists things God hates, accusing his critic of these moral failings.</note> that they cannot be washed away by any art. Indeed, it is impossible even for his friends **Gassendi** and **Lanovius** <note>Pierre Gassendi (1592–1655) and François de La Noue, contemporaries and friends of Mersenne who were also critical of Fludd's mystical approach.</note> to extricate him from them, or to cover them with some deceitful dye and hide them from the sight of Europeans. I shall therefore conclude this Apologetic Treatise of mine by responding to that last text of Mersenne’s, with which he seems to confirm those six "Impieties" of his own imagining as if with a seal. I will divide it into two parts.

## Mersenne’s Text, from his Letter, part 1.

> I ask you, if these things are not impious, what can be impious?

## Fludd.

I ask you, are these things impious: namely, to assert:

**First**, that the whole of Sacred Scripture refers to that <term>mystic Alchemy</term> <note>Fludd uses "Alchemy" here to mean the spiritual process of refining the soul, rather than the chemical production of gold.</note>, or that holy craft of separating the pure from the impure, light from darkness, and virtue from vice, whose basis is that true spiritual cornerstone, the spirit of wisdom, the eternal Word, and the holy emanation: and that one must believe in this **Theo-Philosophical Stone**, by whose help men cast out demons—namely, in Jesus Christ.

**Second**, that this Word, in which (according to Saint John) is life, or the holy spirit of discipline, fills all things, and consequently animates the heavens and all things; and therefore is present in the composition of matter, especially since the Word was made flesh, and the incorruptible spirit is said to be in every thing.

**Third**, that the <term>World Soul</term> <note>original: "Animam mundi" — The concept that the universe itself is a living being with a rational soul, a core tenet of Fludd's Neoplatonism.</note> is forged and exists from the presence of divine light with the ethereal spirit, as is the Angelic nature; and also that the souls of Creatures are forged from the purest spirit and divine light, without any division of the divine essence into parts.

**Fourth**, that Christ or Wisdom (which is the vapor of the power of God, and the brightness of divine light—that is, the cornerstone and Universal Rock) animates the world-spirit, and that the Catholic Church is radically founded upon this spiritual Rock: and that the spirit of this stone can be typically compared to an intense redness or a multiplied <term>tincture</term> <note>In alchemy, a tincture is a substance that can transform or "color" other matter; here, Fludd uses it to describe the purifying power of Christ's blood.</note> when it is multiplied in a human being and increased by divine influx; and that salvation and redemption are to be expected only through this kind of spiritual and mystic blood.

**Fifth**, that the just man is a mystic Alchemist of this nature, or a disposer of impure matter, so that he may separate the pure Word from it: and that he becomes immortal by the use of this **Theo-philosophical stone**, and rises from bodily death and is glorified: that the **Brothers of the Rosy Cross** <note>original: "Fr. C. Ro." — Fratres Crucis Roseae, the legendary secret society of which Fludd was the primary English defender.</note>, after the discovery of this divine stone and the multiplication of divine grace within themselves, know all things, can do all things, and do not consider it "robbery" to believe that this divine stone, or the holy spirit of discipline within them, is from God, and consequently equal to God, since it is of the divine nature.

**Sixth**, that the World was created by the hand of the Almighty from <term>unformed or invisible matter</term> <note>original: "materia informi ſeu inuiſa" — Fludd argues for creation out of a pre-existing "prime matter" or chaos, rather than absolute "nothingness" (ex nihilo), a point of great theological contention.</note>, and not from absolute nothingness. And that Moses himself was practiced in divine chemistry: which appears in the account of the separation of light from darkness, of the subtle waters from the thick, of the water from the dry land, etc. Similarly, that Jacob, Job, Solomon, Isaiah, and even David himself, were Alchemists of this nature: for they treated significantly of the nature, origin, dignity, and power of the **Theo-Philosophical cornerstone**; and they were, to the best of their ability, "doers of the word," recognizing that God loved no one, nor took anyone into friendship, except those with whom Wisdom stayed or dwelt: for it is only through the Son that we have access to the Father, according to the witness of the spiritual Christ himself, or the Word of God, which spoke through the man Christ and in Christ.

Surely, if these things are not pious, what can be pious, according to the meaning of the scriptures?

This is truly that mystic Alchemy which I embrace, and in which I strive to multiply every Christian good and to ripen it with the mental flame of divine genius, God willing—by opening the seeds of my heart to the divine influx or the spiritual sun (to whom alone it belongs to give grace and glory, as the royal Psalmist testifies), and by cleansing the dark stains of sins with the tears of repentance or the faithful sighs of the heart. For it is not enough that Paul plants, or Apollos waters, unless God grants the gift of growth.

Even if Mersenne and his faction still do not understand the laws of my spiritual Alchemy, which operate in the <term>Microcosmic heaven</term> <note>The "inner world" or heaven within the human soul.</note>; let the shame of this be not mine, but theirs, who think my Alchemy is that vulgar sort concerned with bread and wheat: or that my Messiah, Christ, and Savior is that "Balsam of wheat" which I call the <term>quintessence</term> metaphorically and by comparison; which I extracted from wheat and bread through vulgar chemistry. For in truth I acknowledge that I have the seeds of eternal life in my heart; and my gold is living gold, the gold of God, gold bought from Christ. <margin>Psalm 12:</margin> *The Word, I say, of Jehovah, in which is life, which is as pure* (as David testifies) *as silver refined and purified seven times in a crucible of earth; and it is so powerful and living in our heaven that it is sharper than any two-edged sword, reaching even to the division of* <margin>Hebrews 4:</margin> *soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intentions of the heart,* as the Apostle testifies. Therefore, true Alchemy is to free and resuscitate Christ, who was crucified in us by the fall of Adam, from the darkness of mortal ignorance; and, once Christ is freed again, to imprison and crucify Barabbas (who signifies "confusion," and whom the Jews freed so that they might imprison and crucify the Truth). Therefore, the true **Brothers of the Rosy Cross** are those who have penetrated with the eyes of understanding to the spiritual center of human blood, and strive to take that which is affixed to it—as if upon a bloody and **Rosy Cross**—down from that cross, and to make it rise and come to life again through faith in their hearts. In this way, he might <margin>Hebrews 1.</margin> (according to the words of the Apostle) bring about the purging of sins; and make the two one, breaking down the middle wall of the fence—namely, the enmities in the flesh—and nullifying the law of commandments in its decrees. And in this way, God has appeased, through the mystic blood of that cross, both those things which are on earth and those which are in the **Microcosmic heaven**. This, indeed, is the task of our Alchemy: to separate evil from good, the impure from the pure, darkness from light, so that that eternal light, hidden under a bushel, might finally shine out from the darkness and give light before men, so that its professors may walk in the light and show their good works to the world, that they may glorify our Father who is in heaven.

## Part 2. Mersenne.

Text. Truly, unless all the Universities—not only those of France, Italy, and Spain, but also of Germany, the Netherlands, and Britain, and even the Oxford physicians who are that doctor's colleagues—utterly condemn such dogmas and devote to the flames so many books filled with Impieties, I freely confess myself unworthy to even open a book.

# Fludd’s Response

->**Fludd.**<-

My tenets, upon which this **False-Builder** <note>original: "Pseudostructor" — Fludd’s derogatory nickname for Mersenne, implying he builds on a faulty foundation.</note> has built his deceptive Impieties, are these:

First, that true **Alchemy** is the secretion or separation of the true from the false or the fabricated, the good from the evil, the pure from the impure, and the light from the darkness. Therefore, through **mystic alchemy** <note>Fludd defines alchemy not as the chemical transformation of lead into gold, but as a spiritual process of moral and intellectual purification.</note>, sin or vice must be separated from virtue, truth from falsehood, and light from darkness, according to the judgment of all the Scriptures.

Second, that the **cornerstone** is the spiritual Christ. For "the spiritual Rock was Christ." Toward the acquisition of this (namely, of **mystic wisdom**), the entire host of Patriarchs and Prophets, as well as the Apostles and all the wiser men in every age, have aimed with burning fervor and zeal. This is the unique subject of true alchemy, toward whose perfection all true alchemists have longed to arrive with a **Tantalean desire** <note>original: "Tantalea desiderarunt" — A reference to Tantalus, who was cursed to hunger and thirst while food and water remained just out of reach; Fludd uses it to describe the intense, unquenchable longing for divine truth.</note>.

<margin>
1 Timothy 6.
Acts 17.
</margin>
Third, that the Spirit of God gives life to all things. For, as the Apostle witnesses, *God gives life to all things through His spirit*; or as he says elsewhere: *He gives life, and breath, and all things.* Consequently, He gives life to the **spirit of the world** through the vapor of His power, or His holy emanation, as Solomon witnesses. He also gives life to the spirit of man—that is, the **microcosmic heaven** <note>The "microcosm" is the human being viewed as a miniature version of the entire universe (the macrocosm).</note>—which is seen to be composed of spirit and soul. Who in their right mind would deny that He is the root of life, He who fundamentally gives life? But life is in the **Word**; and life is truly the soul, and consequently, the soul of the world is in the Word.

<margin>
Wisdom 7.
</margin>
Fourth, that all the Patriarchs, Prophets, and Apostles, by that sweet fire of their divine nature, strove to overturn and cast down that massive weight of ignorance and darkness which, by the **Fall of Adam**, was placed between that bright cornerstone of life and their own understanding. Their goal was to cast off the veil of ignorance and the dregs of sin, to purge the keenness of their minds, and thus, illuminated by that splendor of grace kindled in their hearts, to know all things, both hidden and manifest—just as Solomon frankly confesses this very thing of himself. Consequently, metaphorically speaking, they may be esteemed without injustice as both **alchemists** and **spiritual farmers and architects**.

->It follows, therefore, from what has been granted:<-

That anyone who denies that Christ is the supreme cornerstone—the tested, precious stone, chosen by God and honored—belongs to that class of men, the pseudo-builders or those building illegitimately, to whom this true stone, which God placed in Zion, has become a "stone of stumbling," a "rejected stone," and a "rock of offense." Consequently, since these men are "dead stones" because of their own darkness, it is impossible for them (according to the Apostle’s warning) to be built upon this stone, Christ, as "living stones" into a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, and so on. And such a person Mersenne appears to be, along with his society.

I conclude, therefore, against Mersenne’s view: if any European Academy—whether French, Italian, Spanish, German, Dutch, British, or even **Oxford**—should in any way condemn such tenets, since they are founded upon the true cornerstone, which is Jesus Christ, I will say indeed that they have poorly examined those words of the Apostle and true **divine-philosopher** <note>original: "Theo-philosophi" — a philosopher who seeks wisdom through God.</note>, which can and should lead any Christian, even one educated in pagan philosophy, to the very center and seat of the cornerstone:

<margin>
Colossians 2:8–9.
</margin>
> *As you have received (he says) Jesus Christ our Lord, walk in Him, rooted and built up in Him, and confirmed in the faith, just as you have learned, abounding in Him with thanksgiving. See that no one deceives you through philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ: because in Him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily, and you are filled in Him, who is the head of all principality and power.*

From these words, if rightly considered, one can see that Christ—in whom the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily—by imparting the power of His divinity to the world and to all things in the world, alone gives them life. That is, He grants to the world, and to every thing in it, its life and being. He is that sole truth in creatures upon whose base and foundation, as if upon the supreme cornerstone, they are built, exist, live, and remain in reality such as they appear to be in their species. Without Him, or in His absence, they cannot remain; according to that saying of the Evangelist: *All things were made by Him, and without Him was nothing made. In Him was life, and that life was the light of men.* For from the fullness of the divinity which is in Him bodily, we have all received, as Saint John witnesses, and His incorruptible spirit is in every thing. What more? Since the Apostle teaches with a living word that neither an Angel, nor created nature, nor wind, nor element, nor heat, moisture, cold or dryness, nor a meteor, nor any other composite—be it animal, vegetable, or mineral—is in any way able by itself to animate either the world or any thing in the world, or to do anything in the world. Rather, it belongs to God the Father alone, through His son Jesus Christ, to work all in all in this world from eternity. His words are these:

<margin>
John 1.
Wisdom 12.
1 Cor. 12.
</margin>
<margin>
1 Cor. 8.
</margin>
> *Indeed there are those called gods in heaven and on earth; yet for us there is one God the Father, from whom are all things, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through Him.*

It is as if he had said: although those of the world, instructed by pagan tradition, say there are "Gods"—that is, agents acting by themselves, whether angelic, or demonic, or some created nature like the stars, winds, meteors, men, or other similar creatures which they want to work by themselves in this world—nevertheless, for us true Christians, there is only one God the Father, from whom all acts immediately come, and one Lord Jesus Christ through whom (or by whose mediation) all effects in the world are produced, and from whom all powers immediately proceed. Consequently, the world and all things in the world are immediately animated by God through **JESUS CHRIST** or the **Word**.

<margin>
1 Tim. 6.
1 Cor. 12.
Ephesians 4.
Jude 1:6.
Acts 17.
Ibid.
Job 34.
</margin>
Now, that which animates is the soul. But in the Word is life; and it can also be said, not incongruously, that the **Word is in the Word**, since there is nothing in God that is not God Himself. Finally, it is certain that the Apostle’s assertion was not in vain when he said that *God has given life to all things; that He works all in all. That He is the Father of all, who is over all, and through all, and in all; that He, by His own Spirit sent out from Himself, created and animated all creatures by Himself, not needing anyone else; that He has given to all life, and breath, and all things, in whom we men also live, move, and have our being.* And according to that passage in Job: *He has set man upon the earth, applying His soul to him.* From which, if He were to take back His spirit or breath to Himself, all flesh would fail and expire, and man would at once return to dust. From these things it is clear that not only man, but every other creature, lives and exists in God; for without the presence of His spirit, all flesh expires. Whence also David: *When you give to them, they gather; when you hide your face...*

# Regarding the Impieties. Section IV, Portion II, Part I.

<margin>Psalm 104. Romans 11.</margin>
...they are troubled when He hides His face; when He takes away their breath, they die; and when He sends forth His spirit, they are renewed, etc. Therefore, if the spirit of God is the internal life and soul of all things, is it such a great impiety to assert that the world is animated and given life by the divine spirit, which God sent forth to perform that duty? For it is said to be the father of all, *from whom, through whom, and in whom all things exist* <note>original: "ex quo, per quem, & in quo sunt omnia" — A reference to Romans 11:36, emphasizing God as the source and sustainer of the universe.</note>?

I would not wish for Lanouius <note>Jean de Launoy (1603–1678), a French theologian and frequent critic of Fludd’s mystical interpretations.</note> to proclaim hereafter that I translate the scriptures—partly foolishly and against their true and proper meaning, and partly impiously—to establish my own ridiculous and erroneous dogmas. The matter is so apparent to the learned of the world, and the passages of scripture so consistent, that they cannot be twisted into another meaning by anyone of sound mind without evident injury to the truth.

Furthermore, one can see that the goal of my writing is not impious, in that everything I have written leads to the honor and glory of the one God and His son, Jesus Christ. By His power, I proclaim to all, for the glory of my Creator, that every creature exists within the **divine act** <note>original: "in Dei actu" — The idea that God is not just a distant creator, but a constant, active presence maintaining existence.</note> and is founded upon the **cornerstone**, and that the creature has nothing of its own or by itself. This stands against the current of the world—specifically those who are followers of pagan philosophy and are intoxicated by its false and deceptive basics. For that philosophy, as St. Paul witnesses, is deceptive and the foundation of **idolatry**. From this has arisen the worship of fictitious gods and a leaning toward vain philosophical fables, which discourage Christians from the true knowledge of the **cornerstone**—the Christ dwelling centrally within every creature. Instead, they attend more to fantastical and superficial accidents <note>In philosophy, "accidents" are non-essential properties (like color or shape) as opposed to the "substance" or true essence of a thing.</note> than to the truth in which they spiritually live, move, and have their being. That is, they should look with one mind toward the living and essential **Rock** from which all things are carved according to truth, and not fiction. For without this, there is nothing.

->*The final part of Mersenne’s text.*<-

Truly (he says), unless they commit these books, so full of impieties, to the flames, I freely confess myself unworthy to even open a book.

->Fludd.<-

Look here, Mersenne! Do you not see how little the learned of Europe are prepared to fulfill your will? You urge things that are contrary to their own consciences, and for this reason, they refuse to indulge your wish in this matter. They do not believe my books are worthy of the flames; rather, they blame the unworthiness of so great a man as yourself, who—blinded by ignorance and having no knowledge of the matter—is yet so ready to judge and condemn. For there are learned men in Europe who can look upon the matter as it truly is, using the deeper eyes of the intellect.

Regarding your reading of books, I certainly notice no dignity or happiness in you, except for mere boasting and **self-love** <note>original: "philautia" — From the Greek word for excessive or conceited self-love.</note>. I confess only this: that like a **beast of burden** <note>original: "onigeri" — Literally a wild ass or donkey; Fludd uses the metaphor to describe someone who carries books but cannot understand their value.</note>, you are able to collect and carry many gems by turning the pages of books, but you are utterly ignorant (as experience shows) of how to judge them rightly, how to reveal the internal meaning of the authors, or how to properly apply them in your own writings.

->Therefore, I am moved toward you neither by hatred nor ill-will, but rather,<-
->driven by brotherly piety, I pray from my heart for a sounder mind<-
->in a sound body for you.<-

->T H E   E N D.<-

<summary>In this concluding passage, Robert Fludd argues that his philosophy of a God-animated world is biblically sound and Christ-centered, contrasting it with the "idolatrous" pagan philosophy of his peers. He ends with a sharp personal attack on his critic, Marin Mersenne, accusing him of intellectual vanity and a superficial understanding of the texts he critiques.</summary>
